docs.title: PowerGenome Documentation
docs.text:
Welcome to the PowerGenome documentation! PowerGenome is a data pipeline tool that generates input files for capacity expansion models, primarily GenX, with optional output for MacroEnergy.jl (see Output Formats).

First time user or setting up a new system?

Use the PowerGenome System Design tool to generate a starting settings folder for your study area. The interactive tool walks you through selecting regions, planning periods, technologies, and policies, then produces a starting settings folder you can download and customise. You must also obtain the data files referenced by those settings. See the System Design tool documentation for a step-by-step walkthrough.

docs.title: What is PowerGenome?
docs.text:
PowerGenome simplifies the process of creating power system model inputs by transforming raw energy system data (from sources like EIA and NREL) into model-ready datasets. Instead of manually assembling data for each region and scenario, you define your requirements in settings files and PowerGenome generates all necessary inputs.

Other geographies

Custom regions and datasets can be used, but some processing conventions reflect US sources such as EIA and NREL ATB. Check the required schemas and technology mappings when adapting a study; changing region labels alone is not enough.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Existing Generator Clustering: Aggregate thousands of power plants into manageable clusters while preserving key characteristics
  • New Build Resources: Integration with NREL Annual Technology Baseline (ATB) for future technology costs
  • Renewable Resource Groups: Pre-clustered wind and solar resources with generation profiles
  • Transmission Constraints: Inter-regional transmission limits and expansion costs
  • Demand Profiles: Hourly load profiles with electrification scenarios
  • Multi-Scenario Management: Run sensitivity analyses across different assumptions
  • Year-Keyed Settings Values: Define parameter values by planning year across all settings sections
  • Flexible Data Sources: DataManager architecture supports CSV, Parquet, and DuckDB

docs.title: Start Here
docs.text:
1. Run a small, complete example: Follow Getting Started to install a published package with uv and run the published Texas example.
  2. Define your own study: Generate a settings folder with the System Design tool, then configure the input tables. Settings alone are not a dataset: the referenced data files must also be available locally.
  3. Check before a full run: Use Validate Settings, then run run_powergenome -sf settings -rf output from your study directory.

PowerGenome prepares model inputs; it does not solve the capacity expansion model. Run GenX or Macro separately after inspecting those inputs.

# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/PowerGenome/PowerGenome.git
cd PowerGenome

uv venv --python 3.12
source .venv/bin/activate  # Windows PowerShell: .venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1

# Install in development mode with dev dependencies
uv pip install -e ".[dev]"

# Install pre-commit hooks
pre-commit install

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text:
PowerGenome is a data pipeline, not a power-system simulator. Settings select and transform source data into inputs for an optimization model such as GenX. The model is run separately.

graph LR
    A[Settings YAML and scenario CSV] --> B[Resolved case settings]
    C[Source tables and resource profiles] --> D[DataManager]
    B --> D
    B --> E[Processing modules]
    D --> E
    E --> F[Model-specific writers]
    F --> G[Input files for GenX or Macro]

docs.title: Core components
docs.text:
Component Responsibility run_powergenome.py CLI entry point; coordinates cases, periods, validation, processing, and writing. settings.py Loads YAML, resolves scenario/year overrides, and provides settings contexts. database.py DataManager: standardized table access over CSV, Parquet, SQLite, and DuckDB sources. generators.py, new_build.py Cluster existing units, construct new-build resources, and calculate resource attributes. resource_clusters.py Select renewable sites and aggregate their capacity, costs, and profiles. load_profiles.py, distributed_gen.py Build demand and distributed-generation contributions. fuels.py, transmission.py Construct fuel-price and inter-regional network inputs. GenX.py Format GenX inputs: resource tags, column naming, and output files.

These responsibilities explain where to investigate a problem; normal studies are configured through YAML rather than by calling these modules directly.

docs.title: Settings and scenario isolation
docs.text:
Settings load into a mutable dictionary-like Settings object. Each case/period gets its own resolved settings, keeping scenario changes separate from the base configuration. A settings context lets decorated functions obtain arguments without every caller passing the entire dictionary.

This convenience does not make arbitrary settings names valid. Parameters still need to match their consuming functions, and source tables need the expected schemas. See Configure Settings for loading rules and Scenario Management for override precedence.

docs.title: Centralized data access
docs.text:
DataManager is a singleton backed by an in-memory DuckDB connection. It maps settings such as generation_table to standard names such as generation. Processing modules request those standard names instead of knowing source filenames.

By default, file-backed sources use lazy views rather than loading all data at initialization. Row filters and optional column projection control the exposed data. Source columns retain their names; the access layer is not a general schema-conversion service.

At case/period boundaries, the pipeline updates table configurations for the resolved settings. Thus one command can use different demand scenarios without rewriting downstream processing. See Data Tables Settings for source lookup and filter semantics.

docs.title: From resources to model-specific files
docs.text:
Existing generators are grouped by region and technology, then clustered using the configured features. New-build resources come from technology cost and performance tables; renewable site data adds supply limits and generation profiles. Demand, fuels, transmission, and policies are built alongside them.

The resulting DataFrames are formatted for the selected model. For default GenX output, resource attributes are split across resource-type files; they are not written as one legacy Generators_data.csv. Optional Macro output uses the same processed data but has its own asset and file conventions. See Output Formats.

docs.title: Scale and fidelity trade-offs
docs.text:
Runtime and memory use grow with renewable site counts, profile length, existing-unit counts, and requested clusters. Filters, renewable cluster caches, and regional aggregation can reduce work, but they can also change the study's representation.

Time-domain reduction reduces downstream optimization size; it is not a reason to choose a universal number of hours. Select and validate spatial, technology, and temporal resolution against the questions your study must answer.

Some conventions reflect US sources such as EIA and NREL ATB. Other geographies can use custom data, but must supply compatible schemas and mappings rather than only changing region labels.

docs.title: Generator Clustering
docs.text: PowerGenome groups real-world power plants into representative clusters to keep capacity expansion models tractable. Rather than modeling each unit individually (which could mean thousands of rows), generators with similar characteristics are merged into a smaller number of clusters per region and technology type.

docs.title: Why clustering is needed
docs.text:
Detailed generator inventories can contain thousands of individual units. Modeling each unit separately can make the optimization problem much larger; clustering trades some unit-level detail for a more compact model.

Clustering reduces these to a manageable number of representative resources while preserving the key features the model needs: capacity, heat rate, cost, and retirement eligibility.

docs.title: Step 1: Filter and group
docs.text: Generators in the model regions (after region aggregation) are grouped by (model region, technology) pairs. Each group is clustered independently. Retirement status determines which units contribute capacity, not cluster membership.

docs.title: Step 2: K-means clustering
docs.text:
Within each region–technology group, k-means clustering partitions units into k clusters where k is set by the technology entry in num_clusters (or alt_num_clusters for per-region overrides).

Clustering features (by default):

  • heat_rate_mmbtu_mwh — thermal efficiency
  • fom_per_mwyr — fixed O&M cost

Features are standardized (mean 0, unit variance) before clustering so that neither dominates the distance metric purely because of scale. Use generator_cluster_columns to choose different features.

If a region–technology group has fewer plants than the requested number of clusters, the number of clusters is automatically reduced to match the number of plants.

docs.title: Step 3: Cluster aggregation
docs.text:
For each cluster, representative values are computed:

Attribute Aggregation method capacity_mw Sum of operating units in cluster heat_rate_mmbtu_mwh Capacity-weighted average fom_per_mwyr Capacity-weighted average vom_per_mwh Capacity-weighted average capacity_mwh Sum of operating units in cluster

docs.title: Step 4: Resource naming
docs.text:
Each cluster is assigned a resource label:

<region>_<technology_snake_case>_<cluster_number>

For example: CA_N_natural_gas_fired_combined_cycle_1

This name is used as the resource identifier throughout the output files.

docs.title: Missing existing-resource availability profiles
docs.text:
Existing hydro, wind, solar, and other profile-backed resources need usable hourly availability data. PowerGenome checks missing resource groups, missing regional metadata, missing sites, and incomplete time series against a combined regional fallback budget before assigning constant 1.0 availability.

PowerGenome permits a small, combined regional fallback fleet: by default, existing_resource_profile_fallback_max_demand_fraction: 0.005 allows affected operating capacity up to 0.5% of mean regional demand before DG subtraction. The denominator includes regional aggregation and supplemental/flexible demand, uses unrounded hourly values for the selected scenario and years, and precedes time reduction. Means across weather years are weighted by modeled hours.

At or below the limit, a warning identifies the affected resources and PowerGenome retains their capacity, tags, and retirement attributes with availability 1.0 in all modeled hours. Above it, an actionable error stops generation of model inputs. Partial profile coverage charges the entire failing existing-generator cluster; resource-group metadata capacity is never used as the affected capacity. All affected technologies and clusters share the allowance in their model region. Valid profiles remain unchanged, and retired/zero-capacity clusters consume no allowance.

For example, SD (p32 + p38) with 1584.86 MW mean demand has a 7.92 MW allowance: 4 MW of missing run-of-river profiles warns and falls back. Modeling p32 alone with 206.28 MW mean demand gives only 1.03 MW, so the same 4 MW errors. If those units retire in 2030, they contribute zero operating capacity at model year 2030, even if the planning period starts in 2026.

Set the fraction to 0 for strict mode; values must be finite numbers in [0, 1], not booleans. Positive-capacity fallback requires valid demand even with --no-load; complete profiles add no demand requirement. Explicitly profile-free resource groups (group.profiles is None, such as thermal/storage groups) remain exempt, as do unsupported dispatchable technologies. New-build behavior is unchanged. Invalid schemas, unreadable files, ambiguous group matches, and invalid weather-year requests remain errors rather than fallback conditions.

This tolerance is a modeling choice, not an industry standard or reliability guarantee. Constant availability can overstate usable generation. Its full-output energy is bounded by the chosen fraction of gross demand over the same hours, but that bound says nothing about hourly reliability or dispatch. Repair metadata/profile coverage before considering a larger tolerance.

docs.title: Default cluster count
docs.text:
num_clusters:
  Natural Gas Fired Combined Cycle: 1
  Conventional Steam Coal: 1

A value of 1 merges all generators of that type in a region into one representative resource. Technologies omitted from this mapping are excluded unless an override includes them.

docs.title: Per-region overrides
docs.text:
Use alt_num_clusters to set different cluster counts for specific combinations:

alt_num_clusters:
  CA_N:
    Natural Gas Fired Combined Cycle: 3   # Three CCGT clusters in CA_N
    Conventional Steam Coal: 1             # All coal in one cluster
  TX:
    Natural Gas Fired Combined Cycle: 5

Setting a technology's count to 0, or omitting it from both the base mapping and the region's override, excludes those generators. Names match the generation table's technology values, or the grouped names after applying tech_groups.

docs.title: Individual units (no clustering)
docs.text:
To preserve every unit of a technology as an individual resource, set its count to null (or use a large number; PowerGenome reduces it to the number of units):

num_clusters:
  Natural Gas Fired Combined Cycle: null

docs.title: Technology grouping
docs.text:
tech_groups merges similar technologies into a single group before clustering, so they share a resource label:

tech_groups:
  Landfill Gas:
    - Landfill Gas
    - Municipal Solid Waste
    - Other Gases

This is useful for small fuel types where separating them would create many tiny resources.

docs.title: Retirement filtering
docs.text:
Set scheduled retirements in the generation table's retirement_year column. A blank value or missing column means no planned retirement.

A unit contributes its full capacity if it is operating at the planning period's end (model_year): operating_year must be on or before that year, and retirement_year must be later or unspecified. Units that come online during a period are included without prorating their capacity.

Myopic multi-period models

Multi-period output is the CLI default, and --multi-period only makes that explicit. Do not pass --no-multi-period, which omits the retirement requirements described here. Use the same generation data across the periods of a case to keep cluster membership consistent. PowerGenome records scheduled retirements in later periods as minimum retirement requirements for each resource (Min_Retired_* columns).

docs.title: Viewing cluster assignments
docs.text: The CLI writes extra_outputs/existing_gen_units.csv inside each period folder, showing which units belong to each cluster. This is useful for debugging unexpected groupings.

docs.title: Distributed Generation
docs.text:
PowerGenome models distributed generation (DG) — primarily rooftop solar — either as behind-the-meter generation that reduces net load or as a generating resource. This page explains the inputs and both treatments.

For reference documentation on the related settings parameters, see Demand and Load Settings.

docs.title: What is distributed generation here?
docs.text:
In PowerGenome, "distributed generation" refers to small-scale generators sited at customer meters, mainly rooftop photovoltaics. These resources:

  • By default, reduce the net electricity demand that grid-scale resources must serve
  • Can instead be included as generating resources using dg_as_resource: true
  • Are modeled via two inputs: how much capacity exists, and what normalized profile it follows

By default, the pipeline subtracts DG generation from hourly gross load before passing demand to GenX. Resource mode leaves gross demand unchanged; the resource's tags determine its treatment in GenX.

docs.title: Data model
docs.text: DG data is stored in two tables that DataManager loads at runtime.

docs.title: Capacity table (distributed_capacity_table)
docs.text:
Rows: one per region per year Required columns:

Column Description region Base region name, or model region name when it is not aggregated capacity_mw Installed DG capacity in MW year Planning year

Optional column: scenario (for multi-scenario files).

If no requested base region has data for the planning year, PowerGenome interpolates each region between available years, using the nearest value outside the range. If some regions have an exact-year value and others do not, the missing regions are not interpolated. Provide complete coverage for each requested year.

docs.title: Profiles table (distributed_profiles_table)
docs.text:
Rows: one per region per hour per weather year Required columns:

Column Description region Base region name, or model region name when it is not aggregated weather_year Year the weather data comes from time_index Hour index within the source profile value Capacity factor (0–1, relative to installed capacity)

Hourly generation in MW is computed as value × capacity_mw; the profile's maximum need not reach 1. Profiles are reordered and indexed from 1. Supply matching hours and weather years for DG and load. For multiple weather years, list them in ascending order: DG profiles are sorted by year, and subtraction is positional.

docs.title: How DG affects load
docs.text:
During load profile construction, PowerGenome:

  1. Loads gross hourly demand from demand_table
  2. Loads DG capacity for the planning year
  3. Loads normalized DG profiles for the appropriate weather_year
  4. Multiplies capacity × profile to get hourly generation
  5. Multiplies generation by 1 + avg_distribution_loss (default 1) and subtracts it from gross demand → net load

Net load is what is written to GenX's demand input (system/Demand_data.csv in the default v6 format; Load_data.csv in the legacy old_genx_format mode).

docs.title: Minimal setup
docs.text:
# Data location
data_location: /path/to/data

# DG tables (files in data_location)
distributed_capacity_table: distributed_capacity.parquet
distributed_profiles_table: distributed_profiles.parquet

# Optional: restrict profiles to a specific weather year
# If omitted, all available weather years in distributed_profiles_table are used
weather_year: 2012

docs.title: Multi-scenario setup
docs.text:
If your data contains a scenario column, filter it per scenario:

distributed_capacity_table:
  table_name: distributed_capacity.parquet
  scenario: high_electrification

distributed_profiles_table:
  table_name: distributed_profiles.parquet
  scenario: high_electrification

Alternatively, keep separate files per scenario and swap them via settings_management across scenarios.

docs.title: Region aggregation
docs.text: If your data uses sub-regional base regions (e.g., IPM regions) while your model combines them into aggregated model regions, PowerGenome automatically aggregates capacity and computes capacity-weighted profiles when region_aggregations is defined. Provide both inputs for the component regions; each component with a profile needs a capacity value.

docs.title: Migrating from the old system
docs.text: Before the DataManager refactor, DG used a single Parquet file with an DISTRIBUTED_GEN_DATA environment variable. The new system replaces this with two tables in data_location. This section explains how to convert.

docs.title: What changed
docs.text: Old system New system distributed_gen_fn distributed_capacity_table + distributed_profiles_table distributed_gen_scenario scenario key in table config DISTRIBUTED_GEN_DATA env var data_location in settings Legacy region mappings Base-region capacity and capacity-weighted profiles

docs.title: Converting your data
docs.text: Prepare separate capacity and profile tables using the columns above. Use installed capacity, not peak hourly generation, as the capacity value; divide generation by installed capacity to derive the capacity-factor profile. Preserve the actual weather year independently of the planning year.

docs.title: Updating settings
docs.text:
Remove old settings:

# Remove these:
distributed_gen_fn: dgen_profiles.parquet
distributed_gen_scenario: reference
# DISTRIBUTED_GEN_DATA env var in .env

Add new settings:

distributed_capacity_table: distributed_capacity.parquet
distributed_profiles_table: distributed_profiles.parquet
weather_year: 2012  # optional

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
No DG subtraction is happening

Confirm both distributed_capacity_table and distributed_profiles_table are set in settings. DataManager will log a warning if either table cannot be loaded.

Wrong year being used for profiles

Explicitly set weather_year in settings to pin the profile year:

weather_year: 2012

If weather_year is omitted, all available DG weather years are loaded. Ensure they align with the selected demand profiles.

Region names don't match

For aggregated model regions, use their component base-region names in both tables. For other regions, use the names in model_regions.

docs.title: Output File Format
docs.text:
PowerGenome writes input files for the GenX capacity expansion model and, optionally, for MacroEnergy.jl (Macro) in its simpleCSVinputs format. This page describes the folder structure, file names, and the key content of each output.

For the full GenX documentation on input file schemas, see the GenX documentation. For Macro, see the MacroEnergy Examples repository.

docs.title: Folder structure
docs.text:
Each (case_id, planning period) pair produces a folder. Files shown below are examples; empty or disabled outputs are omitted.

results/
└── <case_id>/
    └── Inputs/
        └── Inputs_p<N>/           ← one per planning period
            ├── system/
            │   ├── Demand_data.csv
            │   ├── Fuels_data.csv
            │   ├── Generators_variability.csv
            │   └── Network.csv
            ├── resources/          ← one CSV per resource type
            │   ├── Thermal.csv
            │   ├── Vre.csv
            │   ├── Storage.csv
            │   ├── Hydro.csv
            │   ├── ...
            │   └── policy_assignments/
            │       ├── Resource_energy_share_requirement.csv
            │       ├── Resource_capacity_reserve_margin.csv
            │       └── ...
            ├── policies/
            │   ├── Capacity_reserve_margin.csv
            │   ├── CO2_cap.csv
            │   ├── Energy_share_requirement.csv
            │   ├── Maximum_capacity_requirement.csv
            │   └── Minimum_capacity_requirement.csv
            └── powergenome_case_settings.yml

When running without scenario definitions, case_id = Inputs and the folder is simply results/Inputs/Inputs_p1/.

docs.title: Demand_data.csv
docs.text:
Hourly electricity demand for each model zone. One row per hour, with columns:

Column Description Rep_Periods Number of periods in the file Timesteps_per_Rep_Period Hours per period Sub_Weights Hours each period represents Time_Index Sequential hour index Demand_MW_z<N> Load in MW for zone N

All supplied hours are written as one period, so Rep_Periods is 1, Timesteps_per_Rep_Period is the number of hours, and Sub_Weights equals that hour count.

docs.title: Fuels_data.csv
docs.text: One column per fuel plus Time_Index. The row with index 0 contains CO₂ content (tonnes/MMBtu); subsequent rows contain hourly prices ($/MMBtu).

docs.title: Generators_variability.csv
docs.text: Normalized capacity factor (0–1) for each variable renewable resource, by hour. One column per VRE resource, one row per timestep.

docs.title: Network.csv
docs.text:
Transmission network topology. One row per network line (inter-regional connection):

Column Description Network_Lines Line identifier Network_zones Zone label (for example z1); rows also carry line data Start_Zone, End_Zone Numeric zone identifiers at each end of a line Line_Max_Flow_MW Maximum power flow in MW Line_Loss_Percentage Fraction of power lost in transmission Line_Max_Reinforcement_MW Maximum expansion allowed (if tx_expansion_per_period or tx_expansion_mw_per_period is set) Line_Reinforcement_Cost_per_MWyr Annualized cost to expand line by 1 MW

docs.title: Resource files
docs.text:
Resources are split into typed CSVs based on their primary model tag:

File Resources included Thermal.csv THERM > 0 Vre.csv VRE = 1 Storage.csv STOR > 0 Hydro.csv HYDRO = 1 Flex_demand.csv FLEX = 1 Must_run.csv MUST_RUN = 1

Long-duration storage is identified by the LDS column in storage or hydro files, not a separate resource file. The writer does not currently split electrolyzers into a separate file.

All resource files share a common set of columns, with additional columns present depending on the resource type.

docs.title: Key shared columns
docs.text: Column Description Resource Unique resource name Zone Zone number (integer) Existing_Cap_MW Existing capacity operating at the end of the planning period New_Build 1 if the resource is a candidate for new investment Cap_Size Unit size in MW (for integer investment decisions) Inv_Cost_per_MWyr Annualized investment cost ($/MW/yr) Fixed_OM_Cost_per_MWyr Fixed O&M cost ($/MW/yr) Var_OM_Cost_per_MWh Variable O&M cost ($/MWh) Heat_Rate_MMBTU_per_MWh Thermal efficiency (thermal resources only) Fuel Fuel name (must match a column in Fuels_data.csv) Min_Power Minimum stable generation as fraction of capacity

docs.title: Storage columns (additional)
docs.text: Column Description Existing_Cap_MWh Installed energy capacity Inv_Cost_per_MWhyr Investment cost for energy component Eff_Up Charging efficiency Eff_Down Discharging efficiency Max_Duration Maximum hours of storage at rated power Min_Duration Minimum hours

docs.title: Energy_share_requirement.csv
docs.text:
Defines Renewable Portfolio Standard (RPS) or Clean Energy Standard (CES) constraints by zone:

Column Description ESR_<N> Minimum fraction of load that eligible resources must serve

The companion file resources/policy_assignments/Resource_energy_share_requirement.csv indicates which resources are eligible for each constraint (1 = eligible, 0 = not).

docs.title: Capacity_reserve_margin.csv
docs.text:
Required reserve margin by zone and constraint:

Column Description CapRes_<N> Reserve requirement as a fraction of peak demand for each zone

docs.title: CO2_cap.csv
docs.text: Emission cap constraints. Each row is one constraint; columns reference zones.

docs.title: Minimum_capacity_requirement.csv / Maximum_capacity_requirement.csv
docs.text: Technology-specific build floors and ceilings. One row per constraint, matched by resource name patterns.

docs.title: Legacy format (old GenX)
docs.text:
If your GenX version uses the older single-file format (Generators_data.csv, Load_data.csv), set:

old_genx_format: true

PowerGenome then writes Generators_data.csv combining all resource types and Load_data.csv rather than Demand_data.csv. These files are directly in the period folder, not the v6 subfolders.

docs.title: Macro simpleCSVinputs format
docs.text:
When enabled (see Macro Output Settings), PowerGenome additionally writes a Macro case in the simpleCSVinputs format — the same structure used by Macro's multisector_3zone_simpleCSVinputs example. Only the simpleCSV format is produced (not Macro's JSON asset format). The semantic mapping of generators, transmission, demand, fuel supply, and CO2 caps follows the GenX-to-Macro converter (lb/multistage branch for multi-period runs).

With macro_output: true, both formats are written in the same run_powergenome call unless GenX output is disabled. Because all intermediate data processing (storage clustering, market data) is shared, writing GenX and Macro inputs together in one run is faster than running PowerGenome twice (once per model). Use --no-genx / genx_output: false to produce Macro inputs only.

docs.title: Folder structure
docs.text:
The Macro case is written at results/<case_id>/ with scenario definitions, or at results/ without them. It contains one stage per planning period:

<macro case folder>/
├── system_data.json          # Top-level manifest: commodities, locations, settings, assets, time_data, nodes
├── settings/
│   ├── case_settings.json    # PeriodLengths, DiscountRate, SolutionAlgorithm, ...
│   └── macro_settings.json   # ConstraintScaling, WriteSubcommodities, AutoCreateNodes, ...
├── system/
│   ├── commodities.json      # Electricity, NaturalGas, CO2, Uranium, Coal, ...
│   ├── locations.json        # Model region names
│   ├── nodes_1.json          # Stage 1 demand nodes, fuel supply nodes, CO2 sinks
│   ├── time_data_1.json      # Stage 1 time settings
│   ├── demand_1.csv
│   ├── availability_1.csv
│   └── fuel_prices_1.csv
└── assets/
    └── assets_1/
        ├── <base fuel>_power.csv
        ├── vre.csv
        ├── electricity_stor.csv
        ├── hydropower.csv
        ├── mustrun.csv
        └── powerlines.csv

Later stages use the same names with their stage number. Individual files depend on the data and options used.

docs.title: Resource mapping highlights
docs.text:
GenX concept Macro output Existing_Cap_MW existing_capacity / discharge_existing_capacity (thermal, VRE, storage, hydro) Heat_Rate_MMBTU_per_MWh fuel_consumption = heat rate × 0.29307107 MWh/MMBtu CO2 emissions emission_rate = fuel CO2 content / 0.29307107, plus a co2_sink node Eff_Up / Eff_Down charge_efficiency / discharge_efficiency (storage, hydro) New_Build / Can_Retire can_expand / can_retire Line_Max_Flow_MW + reinforcement existing_capacity + max_capacity on a TransmissionLink VRE variability Resource columns in system/availability_<stage>.csv Demand data Demand_MW_z<zone> columns in system/demand_<stage>.csv and electricity nodes Fuel prices per-(fuel, region) supply node + system/fuel_prices_<stage>.csv CO2 caps CO2 sink node with CO2CapConstraint

The Macro writer is electricity-centric; it does not yet emit cross-sector hydrogen, liquid-fuel, or demand-side assets.

docs.title: Data Pipeline Flow
docs.text:
This page follows a run_powergenome execution from settings to output files. For component responsibilities, see Architecture Overview.

Settings and validation → DataManager → Gross demand → Generators and fuels
→ Net demand → Transmission and policies → Output writers

docs.title: Stage 1: Settings loading and validation
docs.text:
PowerGenome loads the settings directory's immediate .yml files. Top-level values replace one another rather than recursively merging, so avoid duplicate keys across files.

The scenario CSV, when configured, defines case/period combinations. Otherwise, the planning-year settings define one sequence of periods. Scenario swaps and year-keyed values resolve the configuration for each pass. Settings validation runs before data initialization; errors stop the pipeline.

Product: base settings plus resolved case/period settings. See Scenario Management for resolution rules and Validate Settings for validation coverage.

docs.title: Stage 2: DataManager initialization
docs.text:
DataManager creates tables or views over the configured sources, mapping settings keys to standard names such as generation, demand, and fuel_price. Data-dependent validation checks those sources against the settings.

At each case/period boundary, update_data_manager() refreshes configurations for the resolved settings, including row filters. It does not require each processing module to reopen and interpret filenames.

Product: standardized data access. See Configure Data Tables.

docs.title: Stage 3: Gross demand, generators, and fuels
docs.text:
When load processing is enabled, unrounded gross demand is constructed before generator clustering. It also supplies the denominator for existing-resource profile fallback checks.

GeneratorClusters.create_all_generators() then combines:

  • Existing units: label operating/retirement status, group by region and technology, cluster using the configured features and counts, and aggregate capacity and operating attributes. Non-operating units remain in cluster membership but do not contribute operating capacity.
  • New resources: select technology cost/performance rows, apply resource modifiers and renamed variants, and build renewable resources from the configured sites and profiles.

Fuel mappings, regional cost factors, startup costs, and other attributes are applied as required by the resource workflow.

Products: resource attributes (gen_data), hourly resource variability, and fuel-price inputs—not yet the final split GenX files.

docs.title: Stage 4: Net demand
docs.text:
make_final_load_curves() uses the earlier gross demand, including configured supplemental/flexible demand. Distributed generation is subtracted unless it is represented as an explicit resource with dg_as_resource.

Demand and variability profiles are written at the resolution of the input data, so the model sees every supplied hour.

Products: aligned demand and variability profiles.

docs.title: Stage 5: Transmission and policies
docs.text:
Transmission processing reads transmission_constraints, aggregates capacities to model regions, and adds costs/losses from transmission_cost. It then calculates expansion bounds and other model-facing network columns.

Policy processing assembles requirements and resource assignments from the configured policy tables and settings—for example, energy-share requirements, CO₂ constraints, capacity reserves, and minimum/maximum capacity requirements.

Products: network and policy DataFrames. See Transmission Settings and Resource Tags.

docs.title: Stage 6: Output formatting and writing
docs.text:
Model-specific formatting casts/rounds selected columns, checks resource tags, and arranges the processed DataFrames into files. The default GenX layout is:

<results_folder>/[<case_id>/]Inputs/Inputs_p<period>/
    system/       # Demand, fuel, network, and variability files
    resources/    # Resource-type files and policy assignments
    policies/     # Policy requirements
    extra_outputs/
    powergenome_case_settings.yml

The case subdirectory is used when running a scenario CSV; without one, Inputs is directly under the results folder. Resource files for empty types and files for unused features are omitted. old_genx_format: true selects legacy combined files. The saved settings record the resolved configuration for that period.

See Output File Schemas for the canonical layout and column definitions, and Macro Output for that writer's scope.

docs.title: Execution flags
docs.text:
Skip-stage flags are mainly useful for focused development and diagnostics:

Flag Skips --no-current-gens Existing generator clustering; new-build resources still run. --no-gens The entire generator stage. --no-load Load construction. --no-transmission Transmission and policy files.

Not every partial-stage combination produces complete model inputs. The default GenX writer expects generator data, so --no-gens alone may fail to produce a usable output. See the CLI Reference rather than using skip flags as a first-run recipe.

docs.title: Multi-Scenario Architecture
docs.text:
PowerGenome separates a study into cases (alternative assumptions) and planning periods (time within each case). It generates inputs for those case/year pairs; it does not run the capacity-expansion optimization.

This page explains why settings resolve as they do. Follow Run Multiple Scenarios for a runnable example, or use Scenario Management Settings for accepted shapes and parameter-specific patterns.

docs.title: Two types of variation
docs.text:
Use year-keyed values for changes over time, such as an increasing carbon tax within one case. Use scenario management for alternatives, such as comparing a tax with no tax. These mechanisms can be combined: a selected scenario swap can itself contain year-keyed values.

A year-keyed dictionary needs integer years, optionally a default fallback, and coverage of the planning years being resolved. It is not a scenario selector. all_years is instead a selector inside settings_management; it is not a fallback key for ordinary year-keyed values. See Year-Keyed Values.

docs.title: The scenario matrix
docs.text:
Each CSV row selects one case/year pair. Extra columns select named categories and levels in settings_management. The CSV is an explicit list of combinations, not a request to generate a Cartesian product. A case ID stays the same across its planning periods.

Duplicate case/year pairs are rejected. A complete case should contain every planning year, but completeness is not enforced automatically. Period numbers are assigned by counting each case in CSV row order, independently of year resolution. Thus a row for 2040 can be labeled period 1 if it precedes that case’s 2030 row. Chronological rows and correctly paired planning-year lists prevent this mismatch.

Execution order is different from period numbering: the runner groups rows by year in first-seen order, then processes cases within that year in CSV order. It executes sequentially. With a chronological matrix, all first-period cases run before any second-period cases.

docs.title: How settings are constructed for each case
docs.text:
Base settings loading and scenario swapping have different merge rules:

  • Loading a directory: immediate *.yml files are combined using shallow dictionary updates. A duplicate top-level key replaces the previous value; file order is not guaranteed. Splitting settings_management across files does not combine the mappings.
  • Applying a scenario: each row starts with an independent deep copy of the loaded base settings. Nested dictionaries in swaps merge recursively; scalar values and lists replace existing values.

For each CSV row, build_scenario_settings applies these stages:

  1. Assign the case ID and its row-derived period number.
  2. Apply settings_management.all_years.all_cases.
  3. Apply matching dimension/level swaps in settings_management.all_years, following the CSV column order.
  4. Apply settings_management.<year>.all_cases.
  5. Apply matching dimension/level swaps in settings_management.<year>, following the CSV column order.
  6. Resolve planning-year lists or periods to scalar start/end years, then resolve year-keyed dictionaries. Expand reserve and output-tag settings.

The entire all_years block is processed before the entire specific-year block. In particular, a year-specific all_cases value can override a value selected by a dimension under all_years. It is not true that all dimension selections always take precedence over all all_cases values.

docs.title: Deep merge behavior
docs.text:
Suppose a base resource modifier has both operating-cost fields:

resource_modifiers:
  batteries:
    technology: Utility-Scale Battery Storage
    tech_detail: Lithium Ion
    Var_OM_Cost_per_MWh: [add, 0.15]
    Var_OM_Cost_per_MWh_In: 0.15

A swap with the same short-name key can change just one field:

settings_management:
  all_years:
    storage_cost:
      higher:
        resource_modifiers:
          batteries:
            Var_OM_Cost_per_MWh: [add, 0.30]

The technology selectors and Var_OM_Cost_per_MWh_In survive. The list [add, 0.15] is replaced by [add, 0.30]; it is not extended. Similarly, setting new_resources replaces the entire candidate list, not just one entry. A dictionary swap needs an absent, null, or dictionary base value; it cannot merge into an existing scalar or list. When adding a year-keyed dictionary to a swap, give the base setting a compatible shape first.

Two selected dimensions in the same block cannot modify the same leaf setting, even to the same value. This conflict check restarts for the specific-year block and does not include all_cases, allowing the deliberate precedence described above. Use a combined dimension when two choices both need to replace the same list; do not rely on column order to break the conflict.

Each row starts afresh. A swap in 2030 does not carry forward to 2040. Use all_years or an explicit later-year swap when the change must persist.

docs.title: The all_cases selector
docs.text: all_cases contains setting/value pairs directly, without a dimension or level. It applies to every row covered by its enclosing block. It is useful for a shared year-specific assumption; a matching dimension in that same block may still override it. See the selector format for a compact example.

docs.title: Multi-period consistency
docs.text: Settings isolation lets different cases use different input tables. It does not make arbitrary between-period changes safe. For myopic multi-period studies, keep the same generation table in every period of a case so existing-generator cluster membership stays fixed. Retirement assumptions belong in that data’s retirement_year column, not in period-by-period table filtering. See Retirement filtering.

docs.title: Output folder structure
docs.text: With a scenario CSV, default GenX files go to results/<case_id>/Inputs/Inputs_pN/{resources,system,policies}/ when the results folder is named results. N is the row-derived period number, not a calendar year. The sibling powergenome_case_settings.yml records resolved settings for checking the generated inputs. See the how-to output tree for an example.

docs.title: Running without scenario definitions
docs.text:
Without scenario_definitions_fn, the runner creates an implicit case named Inputs and resolves settings for the configured planning years in list order. Year-keyed values still work, but settings_management swaps are not applied. There are no dimension selections, and --case-id is ignored.

The default GenX path omits the case-ID directory: results/Inputs/Inputs_pN/. Adding a scenario CSV is therefore not just another way to name the same output folder.

docs.title: Add Supplemental Hourly Demand
docs.text:
This guide explains how to inject additional hourly demand (e.g. data-center load forecasts, new industrial loads) into an existing PowerGenome scenario on top of the baseline demand profiles.

For the full parameter reference see Demand Settings.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Completed the Getting Started tutorial
  • Baseline demand already configured via demand_table

docs.title: Step 1: Create the supplemental demand file
docs.text:
Create a CSV (or Parquet) file with the additional load you want to add. At minimum you need three columns:

Column Description region Base region or model region name (see Step 5: Choose base or model regions) time_index Integer hour index (1-based) or the string all / all_hours load_mw MW of demand to add

Optional columns that PowerGenome will automatically use if present:

Column Description year Planning year; when present, rows are filtered to the current model_year scenario Scenario identifier; at most one non-null value may remain after filtering (see Step 3) weather_year Weather year; use all to apply to every weather year, a specific year (e.g. 2012) to apply only to that weather year, or a blank value to skip the row (see Step 4)

docs.title: Using all / all_hours
docs.text:
Setting time_index to all (or the equivalent all_hours) adds a flat increment to every hour in the load curves. This is the most common way to add a new constant load:

region,time_index,load_mw,year
WEST,all_hours,500,2035
EAST,all,200,2035

docs.title: Using specific hour indices
docs.text:
Supply an integer time_index when the extra load should only appear at certain hours:

region,time_index,load_mw,year
WEST,1,300,2035
WEST,2,310,2035
WEST,3,295,2035

docs.title: Mixing all_hours and specific hours
docs.text:
You can include both in the same file:

region,time_index,load_mw,year,scenario
WEST,all_hours,500,2035,high_data_center
EAST,1,200,2035,high_data_center

docs.title: Step 2: Point settings at the file
Data location is a folder
docs.text:
If data_location is a folder, place the file in that folder and reference it by name:

# settings/data.yml
data_location: /path/to/data_folder

supplemental_demand_table: supplemental_demand.csv

docs.title: Data location is a database file
docs.text:
You can place the CSV or Parquet file next to the database and reference it by filename. PowerGenome resolves it relative to the database's parent directory:

data_location: /data/pg_data.db

# resolved as /data/supplemental_demand.csv
supplemental_demand_table: supplemental_demand.csv

Alternatively, if the supplemental demand is stored as a table inside the database, reference it without an extension:

data_location: /data/pg_data.db

supplemental_demand_table: supplemental_demand  # table inside pg_data.db

docs.title: Step 3: Select a scenario (optional)
docs.text:
If more than one non-null scenario remains after filtering to the current planning year, you must select one. Otherwise, PowerGenome raises an error listing the available options.

Use the dictionary format:

supplemental_demand_table:
  table_name: supplemental_demand.csv
  scenario: high_data_center

PowerGenome will filter the table to rows where scenario = "high_data_center" before applying the demand additions.

Multi-scenario studies

You can vary the supplemental_demand_table scenario across runs using the scenario management system, just like any other settings value.

docs.title: Step 4: Handle multiple weather years
docs.text:
If your load curves span several weather years (e.g. three years of 8 760 hours = 26 280 hours total), the weather_year column controls which weather year a row is applied to:

Option A — apply to every weather year (most common)

Leave out the weather_year column entirely and use all / all_hours, or set weather_year to all. PowerGenome applies the row to every weather year present in the load data.

region,time_index,load_mw,year
WEST,all_hours,500,2035

region,time_index,load_mw,year,weather_year
WEST,all_hours,500,2035,all

Option B — apply only to a specific weather year

Give the row a specific weather_year value. An all / all_hours row then applies to every hour of only that weather year; a specific integer time_index applies to just that hour within the weather year.

region,time_index,load_mw,year,weather_year
WEST,all_hours,500,2035,2012
WEST,all_hours,300,2035,2013
WEST,3,400,2035,2013

The first two rows apply to every hour of their respective weather years; the last applies only to hour 3 of 2013.

Blank weather_year rows are skipped

A row with a blank/empty weather_year is not applied. Use weather_year: all when you want a row to apply across every weather year.

Coverage check

When the supplemental table includes weather_year and the load weather years are known from settings or the data, every weather year must be covered by a specific-year row or an all row. Otherwise PowerGenome raises an error. No coverage check runs when the column is absent.

How supplemental demand is added

In the standard load pipeline, supplemental demand is added before hours are renumbered and base regions are aggregated. Rows for the same region, weather year, and hour are summed. With user-supplied wide load profiles, specific weather years are not supported; omit the column or use all.

docs.title: Step 5: Choose base or model regions
docs.text:
The region column accepts either a base region name or a model region name:

  • Base region name — the row is mapped to the model region that contains that base region (as configured by region_aggregations), and its demand is added to the aggregate's load. If a base region is part of an aggregation, the added demand contributes to the aggregated model region.
  • Model region name — the row is applied as-is to the model region.

When the name is a base region that is part of a model-region aggregation, the supplemental demand is added to that one base region, and the aggregation then includes it in the model region. This is equivalent to adding it directly to the model region. Names that match neither a known base region nor a known model region are logged as a warning and ignored.

docs.title: Complete example
docs.text:
supplemental_demand.csv:

region,time_index,load_mw,year,scenario
WEST,all_hours,500,2030,base_data_center
WEST,all_hours,800,2035,base_data_center
EAST,all_hours,200,2030,base_data_center
EAST,all_hours,300,2035,base_data_center
WEST,all_hours,1000,2030,high_data_center
WEST,all_hours,1500,2035,high_data_center
EAST,all_hours,400,2030,high_data_center
EAST,all_hours,600,2035,high_data_center

settings/data.yml:

data_location: /data/pg_data.db

supplemental_demand_table:
  table_name: supplemental_demand.csv
  scenario: high_data_center

PowerGenome will:

  1. Load rows where scenario = "high_data_center"
  2. Filter to the current model_year (because the year column is present)
  3. Add the load_mw values to every hour in every matching region

docs.title: Add Custom Technologies
docs.text: This guide shows how to add new generation technologies, modify existing ones, and configure renewable resource clusters.

docs.title: Technology Sources
docs.text:
PowerGenome gets technology data from several sources:

  1. NREL ATB (Annual Technology Baseline): Standard new-build technologies
  2. Existing generators: From data tables (existing fleet)
  3. Additional technologies: Your own cost tables, stacked next to the ATB table in data.yml
  4. Modified resources: Variants of ATB technologies with adjusted parameters

docs.title: List Available Technologies
docs.text:
New resource names follow {Technology}_{TechDetail}_{CostCase}. The available names depend on the configured resource cost table and data vintage.

Common technologies:

  • NaturalGas_2-on-1 Combined Cycle (F-Frame)_Moderate: Combined cycle gas turbine
  • NaturalGas_Combustion Turbine (F-Frame)_Moderate: Combustion turbine (peaking)
  • UtilityPV_Class1_Moderate: Utility-scale solar PV
  • LandbasedWind_Class3_Moderate: Onshore wind
  • OffShoreWind_Class12_Moderate: Floating offshore wind
  • Utility-Scale Battery Storage_Lithium Ion_Moderate: Battery storage
  • Nuclear_Nuclear - Large_Moderate: Large nuclear power
  • Geothermal_HydroBinary_Moderate: Geothermal hydrothermal

Cost cases:

  • Conservative: High cost
  • Moderate: Mid cost
  • Advanced: Low cost (R&D success)

docs.title: Include in Model
docs.text:
Add technologies to new_resources:

new_resources:
  - [NaturalGas, 2-on-1 Combined Cycle (F-Frame), Moderate, 500]
  - [NaturalGas, Combustion Turbine (F-Frame), Moderate, 100]
  - [UtilityPV, Class1, Moderate, 100]
  - [LandbasedWind, Class3, Moderate, 1]
  - [Utility-Scale Battery Storage, Lithium Ion, Moderate, 1]

Specify unit sizes in new_resources (fourth element of each list):

new_resources:
  - [NaturalGas, 2-on-1 Combined Cycle (F-Frame), Moderate, 500]  # 500 MW per unit
  - [NaturalGas, Combustion Turbine (F-Frame), Moderate, 100]  # 100 MW per unit
  - [UtilityPV, Class1, Moderate, 1]
  - [LandbasedWind, Class3, Moderate, 1]
  - [Utility-Scale Battery Storage, Lithium Ion, Moderate, 1]
  - [Nuclear, Nuclear - Large, Moderate, 1000]

docs.title: Set Cost Case
docs.text:
Choose financial assumptions and cost trajectories:

resource_data_year: 2024  # Data vintage; must exist in the configured cost table
resource_financial_case: Market  # Market or R&D
resource_cap_recovery_years: 20  # Economic lifetime

Cost cases are specified per-technology in new_resources:

  • Conservative: High cost trajectory
  • Moderate: Mid cost trajectory
  • Advanced: Low cost trajectory (R&D success)

Example:

new_resources:
  - [UtilityPV, Class1, Conservative, 100]  # High cost
  - [UtilityPV, Class1, Moderate, 100]      # Mid cost
  - [UtilityPV, Class1, Advanced, 100]      # Low cost

docs.title: Assign Resource Tags
docs.text:
Define dispatch behavior:

model_tag_names:
  - THERM
  - VRE
  - STOR
  - MUST_RUN

model_tag_values:
  THERM:
    NaturalGas_: 1
  VRE:
    UtilityPV: 1
    LandbasedWind: 1
  STOR:
    Utility-Scale Battery Storage: 1
  MUST_RUN:
    Geothermal: 1

docs.title: Resource Modifiers
docs.text:
Adjust parameters of existing ATB technologies:

resource_modifiers:
  utility_pv:
    technology: UtilityPV
    tech_detail: Class1
    capex_mw: [mul, 1.2]  # Multiply by 1.2 (20% higher)
    Fixed_OM_Cost_per_MWyr: 18000  # Direct override to $18,000/MW-year

  landbased_wind:
    technology: LandbasedWind
    tech_detail: Class3
    capex_mw: [mul, 0.9]  # 10% cost reduction
    Var_OM_Cost_per_MWh: 0  # Zero variable O&M

  batteries:
    technology: Utility-Scale Battery Storage
    tech_detail: Lithium Ion
    capex_mw: [add, 55000]  # Add $55,000/MW
    Var_OM_Cost_per_MWh: [add, 0.15]
    Var_OM_Cost_per_MWh_In: 0.15  # Set directly (not in ATB)
    wacc_real: 0.04675  # Override the real WACC

resource_modifiers runs after O&M columns are renamed to their GenX names; modified_new_resources runs earlier and uses source names such as fixed_o_m_mw and variable_o_m_mwh.

Both published examples set battery variable O&M this way in settings/resources.yml: Var_OM_Cost_per_MWh: [add, 0.15] and Var_OM_Cost_per_MWh_In: 0.15.

Modifier behavior:

  • Operators in lists: [operator, value] format
  • [mul, 1.2]: Multiply by 1.2 (20% higher)
  • [add, 50000]: Add $50,000
  • [sub, 10000]: Subtract $10,000
  • [truediv, 2]: Divide by 2
  • Direct values: Set parameter directly (no operator)
  • Use for parameters not in ATB database
  • Use for absolute overrides

docs.title: Regional Cost Multipliers
docs.text:
Apply regional construction cost differences:

regional_cost_multipliers.csv:

technology,region,value
NaturalGas_2-on-1 Combined Cycle (F-Frame),p1,1.140882
NaturalGas_Combustion Turbine (F-Frame),p1,1.132064
LandbasedWind_Class3,p2,1.097588
Utility-Scale Battery Storage_Lithium Ion,p1,1.072245

Multipliers apply on top of resource_modifiers. Configure this file with regional_cost_factor_table; it must cover the technologies and regions in the study.

docs.title: Modified New Resources
docs.text:
Create renamed copies of ATB technologies with modified parameters:

modified_new_resources:
  # Hydrogen turbine based on natural gas combined cycle
  hydrogen_turbine:
    technology: NaturalGas
    tech_detail: 1-on-1 Combined Cycle (H-Frame)
    cost_case: Moderate
    size_mw: 100
    new_technology: hydrogen
    new_tech_detail: turbine
    new_cost_case: Moderate
    heat_rate: [mul, 1.1]  # 10% worse heat rate
    capex_mw: [add, 50000]  # Add $50k/MW for hydrogen infrastructure

  # High-cost solar variant
  utility_pv_high:
    technology: UtilityPV
    tech_detail: Class1
    cost_case: Moderate
    size_mw: 100
    new_technology: UtilityPV
    new_tech_detail: Class1_High
    new_cost_case: High
    capex_mw: [mul, 1.5]  # 50% more expensive

Required fields:

  • technology, tech_detail, cost_case: Source technology
  • new_technology, new_tech_detail, new_cost_case: New technology name
  • size_mw: Unit size

Optional modifiers: Use [operator, value] format same as resource_modifiers

The Texas example's only entry, hydrogen_turbine, shows the minimum required fields: a 100 MW copy of NaturalGas / 1-on-1 Combined Cycle (H-Frame) / Moderate renamed to hydrogen / 1-on-1 Combined Cycle (H-Frame), with no cost modifiers. See settings/resources.yml.

Assign tags:

model_tag_values:
  THERM:
    hydrogen: 1  # Matches new_technology name
  VRE:
    UtilityPV: 1
  Commit:
    hydrogen: 1
  New_Build:
    hydrogen: 1

docs.title: Renewable Resource Groups
docs.text:
Define renewable resource clustering using the renewables_clusters parameter:

renewables_clusters:
  - region: all  # Apply to all regions, or specify individual regions
    technology: landbasedwind
    filter:
      - feature: lcoe
        max: 75  # Maximum LCOE threshold
    bin:
      - feature: lcoe
        weights: capacity_mw  # Weight binning by capacity
        q: 2  # Create 2 bins based on quartiles

  - region: p1
    technology: utilitypv
    filter:
      - feature: lcoe_interconnect_adj
        max: 30
    bin:
      - feature: lcoe_interconnect_adj
        weights: capacity_mw
        mw_per_bin: 50000  # Create bins of 50 GW each
    cluster:
      - feature: cf  # Cluster within bins by capacity factor
        n_clusters: 2
        method: agg  # Agglomerative clustering

  - region: all
    technology: offshorewind
    turbine_type: floating
    pref_site: 0  # Match resource groups whose metadata has pref_site: 0
    bin:
      - feature: lcoe_interconnect_adj
        weights: capacity_mw
        q: 2

Common parameters:

  • region: Model region name or all
  • technology: Technology type (lowercase: landbasedwind, utilitypv, offshorewind)
  • filter: List of feature filters to exclude resources
  • feature: Attribute to filter on (lcoe, cf, lcoe_interconnect_adj)
  • max: Maximum value threshold
  • bin: List of binning operations
  • feature: Attribute to bin by
  • weights: Weight quantiles by a site-data column such as capacity_mw
  • q: Number of quantile bins
  • mw_per_bin: Fixed MW per bin
  • cluster: List of clustering operations within bins
  • feature: Attribute to cluster by (cf, profile, lcoe)
  • n_clusters: Number of clusters
  • method: Clustering method (agg for agglomerative)

Technology-specific parameters:

  • Offshore wind: turbine_type (fixed, floating), and optionally pref_site to match the corresponding resource-group metadata
  • Geothermal: type (egs, geohydrobinary)

docs.title: Advanced: Group Modifiers
docs.text:
Modify costs for specific resource groups:

renewables_clusters:
  - region: all
    technology: geothermal
    type: egs
    filter:
      - feature: class
        max: 6
    group:
      - class
    group_modifiers:
      - group: class
        group_value: 6
        Inv_Cost_per_MWyr: [add, 64820]  # Additional cost for class 6

Note: Renewable resource profiles and capacity data come from external datasets (NREL reV, ReEDS). PowerGenome does not generate these profiles—it clusters pre-existing resource sites based on cost and performance characteristics.

docs.title: Regional Restrictions
docs.text:
Legacy setting — not applied

new_gen_not_available is only validated for region-name consistency; it is not applied to exclude technologies. Non-renewable new_resources are built in every model region. Renewable resource clusters are scoped per region through renewables_clusters (each entry has a region key).

# Legacy — not applied in this version
new_gen_not_available:
  AZ:
    - OffShoreWind  # No offshore wind in Arizona
    - Nuclear
  CA_N:
    - Coal  # No new coal anywhere in California
  CA_S:
    - Coal

docs.title: Operating Constraints
docs.text: Configure minimum output and ramping in the operational constraints input table, not with min_cap_req, ramp_up_rates, or ramp_down_rates settings.

docs.title: Add a Technology With Its Own Cost Table
docs.text:
ATB will not have every technology you want to model. Rather than editing the ATB table, add your own cost and heat rate tables and list them next to the ATB tables in data.yml. Every table listed under a key is stacked into a single table before it is read, so a technology from your own file is indistinguishable from an ATB technology to the rest of the pipeline.

The walkthrough below adds a 300 MW advanced nuclear (SMR-300) resource. Each fragment matches the Texas 3-zone example system, where the steps were run end to end.

docs.title: 1. Create the Cost Table
docs.text:
New-build costs come from the resource_cost table, which is tidy: one row per technology, cost case, basis year, and parameter.

Column Description technology First element of the new_resources entry tech_detail Second element cost_case Third element basis_year Year the value applies to parameter capex_mw, fixed_o_m_mw, variable_o_m_mwh, capex_mwh and fixed_o_m_mwh (storage), or wacc_real parameter_value Value financial_case Must match resource_financial_case (default Market) data_year Data vintage; must match resource_data_year when it is set dollar_year Dollar year of the values, adjusted to target_usd_year cap_recovery_years Capital recovery period, usually resource_cap_recovery_years units Informational only

Write a capex_mw, fixed_o_m_mw, variable_o_m_mwh, and wacc_real row for every basis year in the modeling period, plus capex_mwh/fixed_o_m_mwh for storage.

data/custom_technology_costs.csv (abbreviated — the real file has four rows for each basis year from 2025 to 2045):

data_year,basis_year,cap_recovery_years,cost_case,financial_case,technology,tech_detail,parameter,parameter_value,units,dollar_year
2024,2025,20,Moderate,Market,AdvancedNuclear,SMR-300,capex_mw,6500000.0,,2024
2024,2025,20,Moderate,Market,AdvancedNuclear,SMR-300,fixed_o_m_mw,105000.0,,2024
2024,2025,20,Moderate,Market,AdvancedNuclear,SMR-300,variable_o_m_mwh,2.5,,2024
2024,2025,20,Moderate,Market,AdvancedNuclear,SMR-300,wacc_real,0.055,,2024
2024,2026,20,Moderate,Market,AdvancedNuclear,SMR-300,capex_mw,6418750.0,,2024

A planning period uses the average of the rows whose basis_year falls inside it, so a declining cost path is a normal way to write cost projections.

Mismatched keys drop rows silently

Costs are selected with an exact match on technology, tech_detail, cost_case, financial_case, and (when resource_data_year is set) data_year. A typo in one of those columns, or a data_year of 2022 in a system configured for 2024, leaves the technology with zero costs instead of raising an error.

docs.title: 2. Add Heat Rates for Thermal Technologies
docs.text:
data/custom_technology_heat_rates.csv (abbreviated):

technology,tech_detail,cost_case,basis_year,heat_rate,data_year
AdvancedNuclear,SMR-300,Moderate,2025,10.5,2024
AdvancedNuclear,SMR-300,Moderate,2026,10.5,2024
AdvancedNuclear,SMR-300,Moderate,2027,10.5,2024

Heat rates use the same keys as costs. Skip this table for VRE and storage technologies, which have no heat rate.

docs.title: 3. List Both Tables in data.yml
docs.text:
Table settings accept a list as well as a single filename. The entries are combined with a UNION ALL BY NAME, so they must have the same columns — and each entry can be either a filename or a full table configuration with its own columns, filters, or scenario.

settings/data.yml:

resource_cost_table:
  - technology_costs_atb_tx_3_zone.csv
  - custom_technology_costs.csv
resource_heat_rate_table:
  - technology_heat_rates_nrelatb.csv
  - custom_technology_heat_rates.csv

Both files are resolved in data_location. List entries are stacked in order, so your table can also be listed first if a later ATB entry should win. If all parts share the same scenario, filters, or columns, write them once as sibling keys and give table_name a list instead:

resource_cost_table:
  table_name:
    - technology_costs_atb_tx_3_zone.csv
    - custom_technology_costs.csv
  scenario: core

docs.title: 4. List and Tag the Technology
docs.text:
settings/resources.yml — the fourth element is the unit size in MW:

new_resources:
  - [Nuclear, Nuclear - Large, Moderate, 1000]
  - [AdvancedNuclear, SMR-300, Moderate, 300]

settings/fuels.yml — assign the fuel that tech_fuel_map gives the technology:

tech_fuel_map:
  AdvancedNuclear: uranium

If the fuel is not in the configured fuel price table, give it a price with user_fuel_price (see Fuels settings), e.g. user_fuel_price: {hydrogen: 16.0}.

settings/resource_tags.yml — tag names match as substrings of the technology name, ignoring case and underscores, and longer keys are applied last. The existing Nuclear entries already cover AdvancedNuclear, so the specific entries below mainly guard against Nuclear exclusions — without the New_Build entry the new technology inherits Nuclear: -1 and is not flagged as a new build:

model_tag_values:
  THERM:
    AdvancedNuclear: 1
  New_Build:
    AdvancedNuclear: 1
  CapRes_1:
    AdvancedNuclear: 0.9

docs.title: 5. Verify
docs.text:
run_powergenome --settings_file example_systems/TX-3-zone/settings --results_folder tx_test

The new resource shows up once per model region in tx_test/base/Inputs/Inputs_p1/resources/Thermal.csv and again, with the later planning period costs, in Inputs_p2:

Resource                              region  Cap_Size  Fixed_OM_Cost_per_MWyr  Var_OM_Cost_per_MWh  Heat_Rate_MMBTU_per_MWh  Fuel         basis_year  capex_mw  Model  New_Build
TX1_advancednuclear_smr300_moderate_0  TX1         300.0                 105000                 2.5                     10.5  TX1_uranium      2027.5   6296875      1          1
TX2_advancednuclear_smr300_moderate_0  TX2         300.0                 105000                 2.5                     10.5  TX2_uranium      2027.5   6296875      1          1
TX3_advancednuclear_smr300_moderate_0  TX3         300.0                 105000                 2.5                     10.5  TX3_uranium      2027.5   6296875      1          1

capex_mw is the average of the 2025–2030 rows, and basis_year is the midpoint of the years that were averaged.

Alternative: wide-format CSV via additional_technologies_fn

The additional_technologies_fn + additional_new_gen pair still works. It reads a wide CSV (one column per cost parameter, one row per planning year) from input_folder instead of the data tables, and only rows named in additional_new_gen are used. Prefer the data-table route above: the costs live with the rest of your data, a list entry can be filtered per scenario, and no extra settings key is needed.

docs.title: Regional Availability of New Resources
docs.text:
new_resources builds each listed non-renewable technology in every model region, so it cannot be used to keep a technology out of a single region. Renewable resources are scoped per region through renewables_clusters (each entry has a region key). The legacy new_gen_not_available key is only validated, not applied.

new_resources:
  - [LandbasedWind, Class3, Moderate, 100]

renewables_clusters:
  - region: CA_N
    technology: landbasedwind
    min_capacity: 25000
    cluster:
      - feature: cf
        n_clusters: 2
        method: agg

docs.title: Technology Not Appearing
docs.text:
Problem: Technology defined but not in output

Check:

  1. Technology in new_resources, or in additional_new_gen if it comes from an additional_technologies_fn CSV?
  2. Technology size given as the fourth list element (or as Cap_Size in that CSV)?
  3. Cost rows findable in the resource_cost table — same technology, tech_detail, cost_case, financial_case, and data_year?
  4. Tags defined in model_tag_values?
  5. For renewables, is a cluster definition present for the target region?

docs.title: Renewable Clustering Issues
docs.text:
Problem: No renewable resources in output

Solution:

  • Verify renewables_clusters parameter is configured
  • Check filter thresholds (e.g., max: 75 for LCOE)
  • Ensure renewable resource data is available in data source
  • Check that technology names match data (lowercase: landbasedwind, utilitypv, offshorewind)

docs.title: Cost Data Missing
docs.text:
Problem: KeyError: 'capex_mw'

Solution:

  • For ATB technologies: verify resource_data_year has that technology
  • For your own cost table: verify the file is listed under resource_cost_table and has one capex_mw, fixed_o_m_mw, variable_o_m_mwh, and wacc_real row per basis year
  • Check that technology, tech_detail, cost_case, financial_case, and data_year match the settings exactly — mismatched keys drop rows without an error
  • Thermal technologies also need rows in resource_heat_rate_table

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Start with the configured cost table: Prefer existing technologies when available
  2. Document assumptions: Comment custom cost adjustments
  3. Validate tags: Check resource classifications
  4. Test incrementally: Add one technology at a time
  5. Regional variation: Use regional_cost_factor_table for regional costs
  6. Version data: Track ATB year, profile vintage in documentation

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
