  • Settings Reference - New-Build Resources: Complete parameter documentation
  • Settings Reference - Resource Tags: Tag configuration

docs.title: Configure Capacity Reserve Requirements
docs.text: This guide shows how to specify capacity reserve credit values for different technologies and constraints in PowerGenome. It covers both simple and complex scenarios using the capacity_reserve_values and regional_capacity_reserves settings.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: regional_capacity_reserves specifies reserve margins by constraint and region; capacity_reserve_values specifies how much of each technology's capacity counts. PowerGenome expands the latter into regional_tag_values.

docs.title: Basic Setup: Uniform Technology Credits
docs.text:
For systems where technologies get the same credit values across all capacity reserve constraints, use the flat format:

regional_capacity_reserves:
  CapRes_1:
    p1: 0.164
    p2: 0.164
    p3: 0.164
  CapRes_2:
    p1: 0.090
    p2: 0.090
    p3: 0.090

capacity_reserve_values:
  Conventional Steam Coal: 0.9
  Natural Gas Fired Combined Cycle: 0.9
  Onshore Wind Turbine: 0.15
  Utility Solar Photovoltaic: 0.25
  Hydroelectric: 1.0
  Nuclear: 1.0

In this format:

  • Each listed technology receives its specified credit for every constraint
  • These values apply to all capacity reserve constraints in regional_capacity_reserves
  • Each region gets populated automatically with the technology credits

Result (internally):

regional_tag_values:
  p1:
    CapRes_1:
      Conventional Steam Coal: 0.9
      Natural Gas Fired Combined Cycle: 0.9
      Onshore Wind Turbine: 0.15
      Utility Solar Photovoltaic: 0.25
      Hydroelectric: 1.0
      Nuclear: 1.0
    CapRes_2:
      Conventional Steam Coal: 0.9
      Natural Gas Fired Combined Cycle: 0.9
      Onshore Wind Turbine: 0.15
      Utility Solar Photovoltaic: 0.25
      Hydroelectric: 1.0
      Nuclear: 1.0
  # p2 and p3 receive the same mappings.

docs.title: Advanced Setup: Multiple Constraints
docs.text:
For systems where technologies have different credit values depending on the constraint, use the nested format:

regional_capacity_reserves:
  CapRes_1:
    p1: 0.164
    p2: 0.164
    p3: 0.164
  CapRes_2:
    p4: 0.180
    p5: 0.180
    p6: 0.180
  CapRes_3:
    p1: 0.090
    p2: 0.090
    p3: 0.090
    p4: 0.090
    p5: 0.090
    p6: 0.090

capacity_reserve_values:
  CapRes_1:
    Conventional Steam Coal: 0.85
    Natural Gas Fired Combined Cycle: 0.85
    Onshore Wind Turbine: 0.05
    Hydroelectric: 1.0
    Nuclear: 1.0
  CapRes_2:
    Conventional Steam Coal: 0.95
    Natural Gas Fired Combined Cycle: 0.95
    Onshore Wind Turbine: 0.25
    Utility Solar Photovoltaic: 0.40
    Hydroelectric: 1.0
    Nuclear: 1.0
  CapRes_3:
    Conventional Steam Coal: 0.9
    Natural Gas Fired Combined Cycle: 0.9
    Onshore Wind Turbine: 0.15
    Utility Solar Photovoltaic: 0.25
    Hydroelectric: 1.0
    Nuclear: 1.0

In this format:

  • Each constraint has its own credit values for technologies
  • Constraints can have different requirements in different regions
  • Technologies can have different credits depending on the constraint

For example, p1 receives the CapRes_1 and CapRes_3 mappings, while p4 receives the CapRes_2 and CapRes_3 mappings.

docs.title: Published Examples
docs.text:
The two example systems bracket the range of setups.

CA/AZ applies a different constraint to each model region and uses the nested credit format. From settings/model_definition.yml:

regional_capacity_reserves:
  CapRes_1:
    CA: 0.164   # 16.4% planning reserve margin
  CapRes_2:
    AZ: 0.101   # 10.1%

and from settings/resources.yml (abridged; the real file lists every technology for both constraints):

capacity_reserve_values:
  CapRes_1:
    Natural Gas Fired Combined Cycle: 0.9
    Nuclear: 0.9
    LandbasedWind: 0.8
    UtilityPV: 0.8
    Battery: 0.95
  CapRes_2:
    # Identical credits here; list them again, not by reference.

Texas has one constraint for all three zones and assigns credits directly in model_tag_values, which needs no expansion:

regional_capacity_reserves:
  CapRes_1:
    TX1: 0.1375
    TX2: 0.1375
    TX3: 0.1375

model_tag_values:
  CapRes_1:
    Natural Gas Fired Combined Cycle: 0.9
    Nuclear: 0.9
    LandbasedWind: 0.8
    UtilityPV: 0.8
    Battery: 0.95

Pick one route per constraint. Expanded capacity_reserve_values land in regional_tag_values, which is applied after model_tag_values, so a regional entry wins if both cover the same region and technology.

docs.title: Mixing Automatic and Manual Configuration
docs.text:
You can mix the automatic expansion with manual regional_tag_values overrides for specific regions or constraints:

capacity_reserve_values:
  Tech1: 0.9
  Tech2: 0.9

regional_capacity_reserves:
  CapRes_1:
    p1: 0.164
    p2: 0.164

# Manual overrides for special cases
regional_tag_values:
  p1:
    CapRes_1:
      Tech1: 0.95  # Different credit for p1

Result (merged):

  • p1/CapRes_1/Tech1: 0.95 (explicit override)
  • p1/CapRes_1/Tech2: 0.9 (auto-expanded)
  • p2/CapRes_1/Tech1: 0.9 (auto-expanded)
  • p2/CapRes_1/Tech2: 0.9 (auto-expanded)

Explicit entries always take precedence over auto-generated values, allowing you to override specific cells while benefiting from automation elsewhere.

docs.title: Scenario-Specific Values
docs.text:
Use scenario-specific regional_tag_values to vary credits. For example, with p1 in CapRes_1:

settings_management:
  all_years:
    reserve_policy:
      conservative:
        regional_tag_values:
          p1:
            CapRes_1:
              Conventional Steam Coal: 0.8
      aggressive:
        regional_tag_values:
          p1:
            CapRes_1:
              Conventional Steam Coal: 1.0

Set reserve_policy to conservative or aggressive in the scenario CSV. Repeat the override for each affected region, using the same technology key as in the base credits. A shorter key such as Coal does not replace an existing Conventional Steam Coal entry; the longer matching key is applied last. When base settings use capacity_reserve_values, their expansion occurs during settings loading; those existing regional values take precedence over a later shorthand change.

docs.title: Technology Name Matching
docs.text:
Technology keys are matched as case-insensitive substrings of the generator's technology field, after underscores are removed. Check your actual data: longer matching keys override shorter ones. Examples include:

  • Conventional Steam Coal
  • Natural Gas Fired Combined Cycle
  • Natural Gas Fired Combustion Turbine
  • Onshore Wind Turbine
  • Utility Solar Photovoltaic
  • Distributed Solar Photovoltaic
  • Hydroelectric
  • Nuclear
  • Battery

You can also create custom new-build resources with their own names, which will work with capacity_reserve_values as long as the names match.

docs.title: Tips and Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Use the flat format for uniform credits: If all your technologies have the same credit values across all constraints, the flat format is simpler and easier to maintain.

  2. Use the nested format for varying credits: If technology credits differ by constraint, use the nested format to specify each constraint separately.

  3. Keep constraint names consistent: Use the naming scheme CapRes_1, CapRes_2, CapRes_3, etc. and stick with it throughout your settings.

  4. Document constraint meanings: Add comments explaining what each constraint represents:

regional_capacity_reserves:
  CapRes_1:  # Primary reserve requirement (MW)
    p1: 0.164
  1. Validate your values: Ensure technology credit values are between 0 and 1. Values represent the fraction of installed capacity that counts toward the reserve requirement:
  2. 1.0: Fully counts (e.g., baseload coal, nuclear)
  3. 0.5: Half credit (e.g., wind, which has low capacity factor)

  4. 0.0: Zero credit (doesn't contribute)

  5. Use scenario variations for sensitivity analysis: Vary the expanded regional_tag_values using matching technology keys, as shown above, rather than changing only capacity_reserve_values.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Settings not taking effect?

  • Check that capacity_reserve_values and regional_capacity_reserves are both present in your settings.
  • Verify that technology keys match the technology field; spaces and hyphens matter.
  • Ensure model_regions includes all regions referenced in regional_capacity_reserves.

Different constraints getting same credits unexpectedly?

  • This is the intended flat format behavior. Use nested format if constraints should have different credits per technology.

Explicit regional_tag_values being ignored?

  • Remember that explicit entries in regional_tag_values take precedence. If you want automatic values, don't specify them in regional_tag_values.

docs.title: Configure Data Tables
docs.text: Use this guide to point an existing study at source files and select rows from a multi-scenario dataset. It does not create or download the data. See Input Table Schemas for required columns and Data Tables Settings for complete syntax.

docs.title: 1. Set the search locations
docs.text:
Put paths in your settings, for example settings/data.yml:

data_location: data
input_folder: extra_inputs

With a settings directory, these paths resolve from its parent directory; with a single settings file, they resolve from that file's directory. This example expects data/, extra_inputs/, and settings/ alongside one another.

PowerGenome searches both locations. Each configured table must resolve in exactly one place; do not keep duplicate copies with the same table name in both. data_location can also be a list of locations or a SQLite/DuckDB file.

RESOURCE_GROUPS and RESOURCE_GROUP_PROFILES are the exception: they resolve from the process working directory, not from data_location or the settings folder. The published examples write them relative to the examples root (example_systems/TX-3-zone/resource_groups), which is why their instructions run every command from that root.

docs.title: 2. Name your source tables
docs.text:
Use exact settings keys and source filenames:

generation_table: generators.parquet
plant_region_table: plant_region.csv
demand_table: hourly_demand.parquet
fuel_price_table: fuel_prices.csv
transmission_constraints_table: transmission_capacity.csv
transmission_cost_table: network_costs.csv

These are illustrative filenames, not a complete study. Keep the other table settings and processing parameters your workflow needs. For a database backend, use database table names without file extensions.

docs.title: Published example
docs.text:
The Texas settings/data.yml maps the same keys to real files:

data_location: data
RESOURCE_GROUPS: example_systems/TX-3-zone/resource_groups
RESOURCE_GROUP_PROFILES: example_systems/TX-3-zone/resource_profiles

generation_table: reeds_generators_tx_3_zone.csv
plant_region_table: plant_region_map_tx_3_zone.csv
demand_table: reeds_load_tx_3_zone.csv
fuel_price_table: fuel_prices_tx_3_zone.csv
transmission_constraints_table: transmission_capacity_tx_3_zone.csv
transmission_cost_table: network_costs_tx_3_zone.csv
regional_cost_factor_table: regional_cost_multipliers_tx_3_zone.csv

It also configures heat-rate, cost, operational-constraint, dollar-year, and distributed-generation tables. The CA/AZ example uses the same keys with plain names (generators.csv, demand_load.csv, fuel_prices.csv) because its data folder holds a single study. The filenames are yours to choose; the setting keys are not.

docs.title: Combining tables
docs.text:
A table setting can also be a list. The entries are stacked with UNION ALL BY NAME, which is how you add your own data to a published table instead of editing it:

resource_cost_table:
  - technology_costs_atb_tx_3_zone.csv
  - custom_technology_costs.csv

Every part needs the same columns and resolves independently, so mixed CSV and database parts are allowed. See Add a Technology With Its Own Cost Table for a working example.

If all parts share the same scenario, filters, or columns, keep them as sibling keys and give table_name a list instead of repeating each part:

resource_cost_table:
  table_name:
    - technology_costs_atb_tx_3_zone.csv
    - custom_technology_costs.csv
  scenario: core

docs.title: 3. Select a demand scenario
docs.text:
Suppose hourly_demand.parquet contains multiple scenarios and planning years. Replace its string setting with a dictionary:

demand_table:
  table_name: hourly_demand.parquet
  scenario: high_ev
  filters:
    - - [region, 'in', [p1, p2, p3, p4]]
      - [year, 'in', [2030, 2040]]

This selects high_ev rows for the four base regions and both planning years. Use names and years present in your own data. Demand processing selects the requested planning year; do not accidentally filter out later periods.

The two conditions in one group are ANDed. Separate groups are ORed; see the filter reference for that syntax and the interaction with scenario.

Keep generation membership stable

For myopic multi-period models, point every planning period at the same generation data. Per-period filters can change cluster membership. Also, retirement_year > 2030 removes blank retirement years, although blank means no planned retirement. Let the generator workflow label operating capacity.

docs.title: 4. Validate and inspect
docs.text:
Run from your study directory:

validate_powergenome --settings_file settings

Fix missing paths, unknown regions, missing columns, and coverage warnings before using the inputs for analysis. Then run your study and inspect the saved powergenome_case_settings.yml to confirm the intended table configuration was used in each period.

Problem Check Table not found Exact filename/table name, recognized setting key, and configured locations. Duplicate table match Remove the duplicate source or give sources distinct names. Required column missing Source schema and any columns projection. Omit columns unless you know all downstream requirements. Wrong rows or empty result Filter nesting, data types, scenario spelling, and required region/year coverage.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Data Tables Settings: mappings, database sources, filters, and renewable path settings.
  • Run Multi-Scenario Studies: swap sources between cases.
  • Use Year-Keyed Settings: change a configuration by planning year when the source requires it.

docs.title: Configure Renewable Resource Clusters
docs.text: Use this guide to turn candidate wind or solar sites into buildable model resources, with explicit choices about screening, cost tiers, and profile similarity. For a runnable exercise using the published Texas example, follow Working with Renewable Resources.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
A resource group is an input dataset: a JSON definition connects a technology to site metadata and generation profiles. A resource cluster is an output: one candidate resource representing one or more sites within a model region. The setting group is different again: it separates sites by categorical metadata, such as county.

Choose the simplest representation that preserves the differences your study needs. More clusters increase model size; fewer can hide cost or temporal variation. Compare results at different resolutions rather than choosing counts from the number of model regions alone.

Need Setting Effect Keep every eligible site Omit group, bin, and cluster One resource per site Aggregate all eligible sites One bin with q: 1 One resource per model region Separate cost or performance tiers bin One resource per nonempty bin unless further split Preserve categorical boundaries group Separate resources for observed categories Preserve differences within tiers/categories cluster Cluster within each nonempty combination Exclude candidates outside the study scope filter Removes sites before aggregation

docs.title: Required Data Files
docs.text:
Set RESOURCE_GROUPS to a directory of JSON definitions (or a list of such directories). This is the published Texas wind definition, example_systems/TX-3-zone/resource_groups/onshorewind_group.json:

{
  "technology": "landbasedwind",
  "metadata": "onshorewind_lcoe_tx_3_zone.csv",
  "profiles": "onshorewind_profiles_tx_3_zone.csv",
  "site_map": "onshorewind_site_map_tx_3_zone.csv"
}

Metadata paths resolve relative to the JSON file. Profiles are sought under RESOURCE_GROUP_PROFILES, if supplied, then alongside the JSON. In the flexible clustering path, site_map resolves alongside the resolved profiles file. Keep that map with profiles if you move them to a separate directory.

site_map is optional. The CA/AZ example omits it for both technologies because its profile files already use cpa_id values in site_id. That example also points RESOURCE_GROUPS and RESOURCE_GROUP_PROFILES at the same directory, so metadata and profiles stay together.

Relative RESOURCE_GROUPS and RESOURCE_GROUP_PROFILES paths resolve from the current working directory. The published Texas settings require running from the examples root, not inside example_systems/TX-3-zone/. By contrast, data_location and input_folder resolve relative to the parent of the settings directory.

docs.title: Required Columns
docs.text:
These requirements describe flexible site clustering, not legacy preclustered resource trees. Column names are normalized to snake case when loaded; for example, CPA_ID becomes cpa_id.

Input Requirement and units cpa_id Unique candidate-site identifier region or metro_region Region matching a model region or its base regions in region_aggregations capacity_mw or cpa_mw Available site capacity, MW; nonpositive-capacity rows are dropped Filter/bin/cluster features Actual metadata columns; no automatic creation of cf, lcoe, latitude, etc. lcoe, if used Input screening/binning metric, typically $/MWh; verify its definition and dollar year cf, if used Capacity factor as a fraction, not percent; a metadata feature, not recomputed from profiles Interconnection costs, if supplied interconnect_capex_mw in $/MW or interconnect_annuity in $/MW-year

Other feature units come from your dataset. Do not treat capacity_factor as an alias for cf, or assume county and coordinate columns exist. Check data coverage and cost definitions before changing regional aggregations.

docs.title: Generation Profiles
docs.text:
Use CSV or Parquet with tidy columns site_id, time_index, value, and optionally weather_year. Values are generation per unit of capacity. IDs match cpa_id directly, or map through site_map: its first column is the candidate ID and its second column the profile ID (the Texas example uses cpa_id,profile_id). Check mapping completeness; candidates missing from a supplied map are dropped.

Set weather_year to select the intended year(s), and utc_offset to align profiles with demand. Wide profiles with site IDs as columns are deprecated and cannot be filtered by weather_year. Without a profiles file, the flexible path uses constant availability of 1; that is not a realistic wind or solar profile.

docs.title: 1. Match the technology and edit one settings definition
docs.text:
Include the matching cost-table technology in the existing new_resources list:

new_resources:
  - [LandbasedWind, Class3, Moderate, 1]

Each entry is [technology, tech_detail, cost_case, unit_size], with unit size in MW. Keep the other technologies your study needs; replacing this list removes them. technology: landbasedwind in a cluster entry is the resource-group identifier mapped from the new-build technology, not the full cost-table name. For offshore wind, also match turbine_type: fixed or floating to the selected technology detail and resource JSON.

Edit existing definitions rather than adding an override file with duplicate top-level keys. A settings directory loads only its immediate .yml files, uses shallow top-level replacement, and has no reliable override order. Lists and nested dictionaries are not merged across files.

docs.title: 2. Apply one filter/bin/cluster recipe
docs.text:
The following uses features in the Texas wind metadata and preserves the example's solar definition. Replace the existing renewables_clusters list in the study's resource settings:

renewables_clusters:
  - region: all
    technology: landbasedwind
    filter:
      - feature: lcoe
        max: 75
    bin:
      - feature: lcoe
        q: 2
        weights: capacity_mw
    cluster:
      - feature: profile
        method: agglomerative
        n_clusters: 2
  - region: all
    technology: utilitypv
    filter:
      - feature: lcoe
        max: 60

Here 75 retains the Texas example's illustrative wind screening assumption; it is not a recommended economic cutoff. A high-LCOE site can still be valuable because of its location or output timing. Omit the filter if all candidates belong in the study, and document any exclusion you do use. Filter bounds are inclusive, but the implementation ignores min: 0 and max: 0.

The same illustrative screens appear in both published systems: max: 75 for wind and max: 60 for solar in Texas, and max: 130 for wind and max: 50 for solar in CA/AZ. The different numbers reflect different candidate datasets, not a recommendation; screen on your own metadata's cost distribution.

Processing order is:

  1. Select sites in each model region, including its aggregated base regions.
  2. Apply all filters, then optional min_capacity selection.
  3. Bin numeric features across filtered sites in that model region.
  4. Separate categorical groups, if requested.
  5. Cluster within each nonempty bin/group combination.
  6. Sum site capacity and capacity-weight profiles and supported cost columns.

In this recipe, two capacity-weighted LCOE tiers are each split into up to two profile clusters: at most four new wind resources per model region. Weighted quantiles aim for similar MW, not exactly equal capacity; indivisible sites and duplicate values can produce unequal or fewer bins. Aggregation averages profiles; it does not select a single representative site.

docs.title: 3. Set regional scope deliberately
docs.text:
Use region: all for a common definition. To vary it, add a complete entry for an exact model-region name, such as TX2; it replaces the all definition for the same resource identifiers in that region. It does not inherit omitted filters or bin settings. Avoid duplicate entries for the same region/resource.

Use a categorical group only to preserve a boundary inside a model region; model regions are already processed separately. Scoping cluster entries is not a general mechanism for excluding technologies. In particular, new_gen_not_available is validated but not applied; do not rely on it to enforce a regional technology restriction.

docs.title: Calculating Total Cluster Count
docs.text:
For one binning and one clustering step, the approximate upper bound per model region is observed category combinations × bins × requested clusters. Empty combinations, duplicate bin edges, and too few sites reduce the count.

  • No group, bin, or cluster: each retained site remains a resource.
  • group and/or bin, without cluster: one resource per nonempty combination.
  • bin: [{feature: lcoe, q: 1}]: aggregate all retained sites into one resource.
  • cluster only: up to n_clusters resources per region.

Do not filter sites merely to meet a resource-count target: that changes the candidate supply. First reduce bin/cluster counts or unnecessary groups, then compare capacity, cost ranges, profile diversity, runtime, and model outcomes.

docs.title: Run and inspect the result
docs.text:
For the Texas example, run from the examples root (use settings_wind instead of settings if following the tutorial's separate-settings exercise):

validate_powergenome --settings_file example_systems/TX-3-zone/settings
run_powergenome \
  --settings_file example_systems/TX-3-zone/settings \
  --results_folder renewable_test

The first planning period's default GenX outputs are:

  • renewable_test/base/Inputs/Inputs_p1/resources/Vre.csv: resource attributes.
  • renewable_test/base/Inputs/Inputs_p1/system/Generators_variability.csv: profiles named by Resource, aligned with modeled time steps.
  • renewable_test/base/Inputs/Inputs_p1/extra_outputs/: site-to-cluster assignment CSVs for checking membership.

Other studies can use different case-directory names. The legacy flat generator layout is not the default; see Output Format.

Check new-build wind separately from existing wind. Compare Max_Cap_MW totals with eligible site capacity, count resources by region, and inspect Inv_Cost_per_MWyr ($/MW-year), not just the metadata's screening lcoe. Profile columns must match the written Resource names. A simple mean over the written hours is not an annual capacity factor when the profile covers only a sample of hours. See the tutorial's output checks.

docs.title: Caching for speed
docs.text:
The generator workflow defaults both controls to true; the published Texas example explicitly sets both to false. To enable reads and writes, use:

cache_resource_clusters: true
use_resource_clusters_cache: true

Caches live under input_folder/cluster_assignments/, in a resource-path-specific subfolder. Reading and writing are separate: set use_resource_clusters_cache to false to recompute; cache_resource_clusters: false only disables writes.

Keys include region, technology, cluster settings, timezone, weather year, and metadata/profile file hashes. The site-map file is not separately hashed. After changing a site map, remove the affected cache files before regenerating them; disabling reads alone recomputes but does not overwrite existing same-key files.

docs.title: Binning Methods
docs.text:
Use one bin-count option per entry; provide a numeric feature column:

Option Behavior q: 3 Three quantile bins; add weights: capacity_mw to balance by MW rather than site count bins: 3 Three equal-width feature ranges; weights has no effect bins: [0, 30, 50, 75] Explicit feature-value edges q: [0, 0.5, 1] Explicit quantile edges mw_per_bin: 10000 Equal-width count from total MW divided by this value, truncated, minimum one mw_per_q: 10000 Quantile count from the same calculation

Explicit outer bin edges are expanded to cover the data range, with warnings; bin edges are not screening thresholds. Multiple bin entries subdivide sites sequentially, before categorical grouping. Keep one dimension until you have checked its effect.

docs.title: Clustering on Generation Profiles
docs.text:
Use feature: profile with agglomerative (aliases agg, hierarchical) as in the main recipe. For metadata instead of profiles:

  • Agglomerative clustering accepts one scalar numeric feature, such as cf.
  • kmeans accepts a list of numeric columns, even for one feature, such as feature: [cf]; features are standardized. Latitude/longitude can be included only if present in your metadata. Use agglomerative for profile clustering.
  • Set n_clusters explicitly, or use mw_per_cluster to derive a count from capacity within each bin/group (truncated, minimum one).

docs.title: Modify Costs by Group
docs.text:
Group modifiers are optional, after aggregation. For example, if your metadata has county, put group: [county] in the same cluster definition and add:

group_modifiers:
  - group: county
    group_value: Example_County
    Inv_Cost_per_MWyr: [mul, 1.1]

Use only documented cost adjustments. The group must appear in group so its value enters the cluster label. Matching is by case-insensitive substring of that label: inspect matches carefully. Scalars replace values; two-item lists support add, sub, mul, and truediv.

Annual technology investment costs have already been calculated here. Modify Inv_Cost_per_MWyr to change that component; changing capex_mw alone does not recalculate it. interconnect_annuity is a separate site-cost component added later. Avoid double counting it. To modify technology capital cost before annualization, use resource_modifiers with exact technology and tech_detail selectors, as described in New-Build Resources.

docs.title: Selecting a limited candidate supply
docs.text:
min_capacity retains the lowest-lcoe sites up to the first site meeting the requested MW, after filters. It is not a minimum build requirement, and can overshoot because sites are indivisible. It requires an lcoe column. Use it only when deliberately limiting candidate supply, not to choose cluster size.

The legacy precluster_renewables/max_clusters/max_lcoe resource-tree workflow is separate from this guide. Do not mix its keys into the flexible recipe.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Check first No resource group matches JSON technology/other identifiers, matching new_resources, file paths, and current working directory No or missing sites Region names, nonpositive capacity, filters, site-map coverage, and requested weather years Far more resources than expected Omitting all aggregation settings preserves individual sites; use one bin to aggregate Fewer clusters than requested Empty category combinations, duplicate feature/bin values, or fewer sites than requested clusters Unexpected cost or location Inspect site assignments and inputs; expensive sites can be valuable, so do not automatically tighten screening Changed mappings have no effect Recompute and remove affected stale cache entries; see caching above

docs.title: Related Settings
docs.text:
• New-Build Resources: cost technologies, modifiers, and renewable settings.
  • Resource Tags: model classifications.
  • Regions: regional aggregation.
  • Data Tables: source-table configuration.

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text: Run the Texas wind tutorial, then test a second aggregation resolution while holding candidate supply fixed. Record which differences matter for your study before adding groups or more features.

docs.title: Configure Settings Files
docs.text: This guide shows how to organize and structure settings files for PowerGenome projects.

docs.title: Settings Folder Structure
docs.text:
PowerGenome loads settings from a folder containing multiple YAML files:

my_project/
├── settings/
│   ├── model_definition.yml
│   ├── regions.yml
│   ├── generators.yml
│   ├── new_build.yml
│   ├── fuels.yml
│   ├── transmission.yml
│   ├── demand.yml
│   ├── scenario_management.yml
│   └── data.yml
└── extra_inputs/
    └── emission_policies.csv

Loading behavior:

  • A directory loads its .yml files; a single YAML file can also be loaded.
  • Duplicate top-level keys replace the entire earlier value. File order is not guaranteed, so define each top-level setting in only one file.
  • Split settings logically across files for maintainability.

docs.title: Published Example Systems
docs.text:
The PowerGenome-examples repository contains complete studies whose settings you can copy and adapt:

  • TX-3-zone: three ERCOT model zones (TX1, TX2, TX3) aggregated from seven ReEDS balancing areas.
  • CA_AZ: California (CA) and Arizona (AZ) aggregated from eight ReEDS balancing areas.

The Texas settings folder shows how the files in this guide fit together:

example_systems/TX-3-zone/settings/
├── model_definition.yml   # regions, years, capacity reserves, output columns
├── resources.yml          # existing fleet, new build, renewable clusters
├── resource_tags.yml      # model_tag_names and model_tag_values
├── fuels.yml              # fuel prices, assignments, carbon tax
├── demand.yml
├── distributed_gen.yml
├── transmission.yml
├── startup_costs.yml
├── time_clustering.yml
├── data.yml               # source tables and data paths
├── extra_inputs.yml       # policy and scenario files
├── scenario_management.yml
└── env.yml

The CA/AZ study uses the same layout with different values. Both are small demonstration datasets rather than calibrated studies, but each runs end to end and is a working reference for every file described here. The Getting Started tutorial downloads a pinned snapshot and runs the Texas study.

docs.title: Copy Example System
docs.text:
Use the PowerGenome System Design tool to generate a starting settings folder for your study area. The tool walks you through selecting regions, technologies, and policies, then produces a settings folder you can download and modify.

See the System Design tool documentation for a walkthrough of each step.

docs.title: Minimal Settings
docs.text:
These fragments illustrate the structure; they are not a complete runnable configuration. Start with a generated configuration or a published example for the required tables and other settings.

settings/model_definition.yml:

# Planning horizon
model_periods: [[2026, 2030]]

# Currency
target_usd_year: 2023

# Alternatively, define the planning horizon using model_year and model_first_planning_year:
# model_year: [2030]
# model_first_planning_year: 2030

# Data location
data_location: /path/to/data

# Model tags
model_tag_names:
  - THERM
  - VRE
  - STOR

model_tag_values:
  THERM:
    NaturalGas: 1
  VRE:
    UtilityPV: 1

settings/regions.yml:

# Model regions
model_regions:
  - CA_N
  - CA_S

# Region aggregations (if using base regions)
region_aggregations:
  CA_N: [CA_N]
  CA_S: [CA_S]

docs.title: By Category (Recommended)
docs.text:
Split settings by functional area:

model_definition.yml: Planning years, model regions and aggregations, tags, execution control regions.yml: Regional configuration, aggregations, reserves generators.yml: Existing generator clustering, retirement new_build.yml: New-build technologies, costs, renewable clusters fuels.yml: Fuel prices, emissions, carbon pricing transmission.yml: Network constraints, expansion costs demand.yml: Load profiles, growth, distributed generation scenario_management.yml: Multi-scenario definitions

How you group these is a project choice. Both published examples keep existing generators, new-build resources, and renewable clusters in resources.yml, and model tags in resource_tags.yml.

docs.title: By Model Year
docs.text:
For multi-period models with year-specific parameters, you now have two options:

  • Year-keyed values: Best for by-year changes without full scenario matrices.
  • settings_management: Best for multi-case studies with scenario dimensions.

docs.title: Advanced: Year-Keyed Values Across Any Settings Section
docs.text:
Year-keyed values are an advanced pattern that can be used for any settings parameter value (including nested values):

carbon_tax:
  2030: 25
  2040: 50

Resolution behavior:

  1. Exact year match
  2. default fallback

If a year-keyed dictionary does not cover all planning years and has no fallback, PowerGenome raises a validation error.

See Use Year-Keyed Settings Values for step-by-step usage and Year-Keyed Values (Reference) for full rules.

docs.title: Scenario Management For Multi-Case Workflows
docs.text:
Use settings_management when you need parameter swaps across multiple scenario dimensions:

settings/
├── base.yml                    # Core configuration
├── regions.yml                 # Regional definition
└── scenario_management.yml     # Year-specific overrides
extra_inputs/
└── scenario_definitions.csv    # Case definitions

base.yml:

# Planning periods
model_periods:
  - [2020, 2030]
  - [2031, 2040]
  - [2041, 2050]
target_usd_year: 2023

model_regions:
  - CA_N
  - CA_S

scenario_management.yml:

settings_management:
  all_years:
    policy:  # Column name from scenario_definitions.csv
      high:
        carbon_tax: 100
      low:
        carbon_tax: 25
  2030:
    all_cases:  # Applied to ALL scenarios in 2030
      weather_year: 2012
  2040:
    all_cases:  # Applied to ALL scenarios in 2040
      weather_year: 2012
  2050:
    all_cases:  # Applied to ALL scenarios in 2050
      weather_year: 2012

scenario_definitions_fn: scenario_definitions.csv

scenario_definitions.csv:

case_id,year,policy
high_policy,2030,high
high_policy,2040,high
high_policy,2050,high
low_policy,2030,low
low_policy,2040,low
low_policy,2050,low

In this example:

  • all_cases selects the weather year for each planning year
  • policy varies carbon tax across scenarios
  • Both are applied together for each case/year combination

docs.title: By Scenario
docs.text:
For scenario studies, use settings_management:

settings/
├── base.yml                    # Base configuration
└── settings_management.yml     # Parameter swaps
extra_inputs/
└── scenario_definitions.csv    # Scenario matrix

See Run Multiple Scenarios for details.

docs.title: Local Paths
docs.text:
Create data.yml for machine-specific paths (add to .gitignore):

settings/data.yml:

# Data paths (local machine)
data_location: /Users/me/powergenome_data
RESOURCE_GROUP_PROFILES: /Users/me/nrel_profiles
input_folder: extra_inputs

Relative data_location and scalar input_folder paths resolve from the parent of the settings directory (or the directory containing a settings file). Resource group paths are relative to the process working directory.

RESOURCE_GROUPS and RESOURCE_GROUP_PROFILES accept either a single path or a list of paths, so data can be split across multiple folders:

RESOURCE_GROUPS:
  - /Users/me/resource_groups/onshore
  - /Users/me/resource_groups/offshore
RESOURCE_GROUP_PROFILES:
  - /Users/me/nrel_profiles/wind
  - /Users/me/nrel_profiles/solar

settings/.gitignore:

data.yml

Team members create their own data.yml without committing it.

docs.title: Shared Paths
docs.text:
For shared data locations (HPC cluster, cloud storage), commit paths:

settings/data_paths.yml:

# Shared data paths (committed to repo)
data_location: /shared/powergenome/v2_data
RESOURCE_GROUP_PROFILES: /shared/nrel/generation_profiles

docs.title: Parameter Override
docs.text:
Avoid defining the same top-level parameter in multiple files. For example, these two files conflict:

settings/01_base.yml:

resource_modifiers:
  utilitypv:
    technology: UtilityPV
    tech_detail: Class1
    capex_mw: [mul, 1.0]
carbon_tax: 25

settings/02_overrides.yml:

resource_modifiers:
  utilitypv:
    capex_mw: [mul, 0.9]

The whole resource_modifiers dictionary is replaced, not recursively merged; the surviving entry lacks the required technology and tech_detail keys. Since directory iteration order is not guaranteed, do not rely on either file winning. Keep all entries for a top-level key together.

docs.title: List Merging
docs.text:
Lists are replaced, not merged:

settings/technologies.yml:

new_resources:
  - [NaturalGas, 2-on-1 Combined Cycle (F-Frame), Moderate, 500]
  - [UtilityPV, Class1, Moderate, 100]
  - [LandbasedWind, Class3, Moderate, 100]

settings/more_technologies.yml:

new_resources:
  - [Utility-Scale Battery Storage, Lithium Ion, Moderate, 100]

Result: One entire list replaces the other; which one wins is not guaranteed.

Solution: Keep lists in one file or use complete lists in later files:

new_resources:
  - [NaturalGas, 2-on-1 Combined Cycle (F-Frame), Moderate, 500]
  - [UtilityPV, Class1, Moderate, 100]
  - [LandbasedWind, Class3, Moderate, 100]
  - [Utility-Scale Battery Storage, Lithium Ion, Moderate, 100]

docs.title: Dictionary Merging
docs.text:
Nested dictionaries are not merged across files:

settings/tags.yml:

model_tag_values:
  THERM:
    NaturalGas: 1

settings/more_tags.yml:

model_tag_values:
  VRE:
    UtilityPV: 1

Result: One entire model_tag_values dictionary replaces the other. Combine the tag entries in a single file instead. The Python Settings.update() and Settings.load_settings() methods also update top-level keys rather than deep-merging them.

docs.title: Check Settings Load
docs.text:
Verify settings load correctly:

from powergenome.settings import load_settings
from pathlib import Path

settings = load_settings(Path("settings"))
print(settings.get("model_periods"))
print(settings.get("model_regions"))

docs.title: Validate Required Parameters
docs.text:
Check for settings used in the example above:

from powergenome.settings import load_settings
from pathlib import Path

settings = load_settings(Path("settings"))

required = [
    "model_periods",
    "target_usd_year",
    "model_regions",
]

missing = [p for p in required if p not in settings]
if missing:
    print(f"Missing required parameters: {missing}")

docs.title: Test Data Loading
docs.text:
Verify data tables are accessible:

from powergenome.settings import load_settings
from powergenome.database import initialize_data_manager
from pathlib import Path

settings = load_settings(Path("settings"))
data_location = settings.get("data_location")

initialize_data_manager(settings, data_location)

# Test table loading
from powergenome.database import get_data_manager
dm = get_data_manager()
print(dm.list_tables())

docs.title: Regional Cost Multipliers
docs.text:
Apply regional construction cost differences:

settings/regional_costs.yml:

regional_cost_factor_table: regional_multipliers.csv
cost_multiplier_region_map:
  PCA_WECC: [CA_N, CA_S, AZ]

extra_inputs/regional_multipliers.csv:

technology,region,value
UtilityPV_Class1,PCA_WECC,1.2
LandbasedWind_Class3,PCA_WECC,1.15
NaturalGas_2-on-1 Combined Cycle (F-Frame),PCA_WECC,1.1

docs.title: Technology Restrictions
docs.text:
Prohibit technologies in specific regions:

Legacy setting — not applied

new_gen_not_available is only validated for region-name consistency; it is not applied to exclude technologies. Non-renewable new_resources are built in every model region; renewable resource clusters are scoped per region through renewables_clusters.

settings/tech_availability.yml:

# Legacy — not applied in this version
new_gen_not_available:
  AZ:
    - OffshoreWind_*  # No offshore wind in Arizona
  CA_N:
    - Coal_*  # No new coal in California

docs.title: Custom Technology Costs
docs.text:
Modify costs for specific technologies:

settings/custom_costs.yml:

resource_modifiers:
  utility_pv:
    technology: UtilityPV
    tech_detail: Class1
    capex_mw:
      2030: [mul, 1.1]  # 10% higher than source data
    Fixed_OM_Cost_per_MWyr:
      2030: 15000  # Override source value

modified_new_resources:
  utility_pv_high:
    technology: UtilityPV
    tech_detail: Class1
    cost_case: Moderate
    size_mw: 100
    new_technology: UtilityPV
    new_tech_detail: Class1_High
    new_cost_case: High
    capex_mw:
      2030: [mul, 1.3]

Add entries for every planning year or a default to the year-keyed values.

docs.title: Emission Policies
docs.text:
Configure renewable portfolio standards:

settings/policies.yml:

emission_policies_table: emission_policies.csv

See Energy Share Requirements for the policy table format.

docs.title: Settings Not Loading
docs.text:
Problem: Settings folder not recognized

Solution: Pass an existing settings directory or YAML file:

# Correct
run_powergenome --settings_file settings --results_folder results

# Also supported: a single YAML file
run_powergenome --settings_file settings/model.yml --results_folder results

docs.title: Parameter Not Found
docs.text:
Problem: KeyError: 'model_periods'

Solution: Check parameter spelling and ensure it's in one of the YAML files:

# Search for parameter in settings
grep -r "model_periods" settings/

docs.title: Override Not Working
docs.text:
Problem: Parameter value not updating from later file

Solution: Check for duplicate top-level keys and combine their values in one file. Renaming files does not establish a guaranteed override order.

docs.title: Path Not Found
docs.text:
Problem: FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '/path/to/data'

Solution: Use absolute paths in data_location:

# Use absolute path
data_location: /Users/me/powergenome_data

The loader does not expand ~; use the full home-directory path.

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Split logically: Organize by functional area (generators, transmission, etc.)
  2. Use data.yml: Keep machine-specific paths out of version control
  3. Comment generously: Explain non-obvious parameter choices
  4. Version control: Commit settings folder (except data.yml) to Git
  5. Test incrementally: Validate after major changes
  6. Document assumptions: Note data sources, policy assumptions, cost adjustments
  7. Start from a generated configuration: Use the System Design tool to produce a working settings folder for your region

docs.title: Where to look first
docs.text:
1. Run validate_powergenome --settings_file settings from your study directory.
  2. Read the first error and its preceding warnings in <results_folder>/log.txt.
  3. Check the resolved powergenome_case_settings.yml in the affected period's output folder, not just the original YAML. Scenario swaps may have changed it.

The log contains DEBUG messages; the terminal shows INFO and above. A run that completes with warnings may still have unsuitable inputs. See Validate Settings for coverage and limitations.

docs.title: Common errors
docs.text:
Symptom Likely cause and next check Missing settings key, such as model_year Check the exact parameter name, type, and planning-period configuration in Model Definition. Table creation fails or table is missing Check the source exists, the setting key is correct, and the table resolves in exactly one configured location. For files, include .csv or .parquet; for databases, use a table name. FileNotFoundError Check relative-path rules below and whether the command was run from the intended study directory. Planning-year list lengths differ Use valid model_periods, or one matching entry in each legacy year list per period. Requested case IDs are not in scenario inputs Compare --case-id values with the CSV's case_id column. Omit the flag to run all cases. Scenario years do not match settings CSV year values must match the planning-period end years. Unknown or missing region Compare case-sensitive names in tables, model_regions, and region_aggregations. Missing fuel prices or zero fuel costs Check fuel/scenario/base-region/year coverage and the selected data vintage. Do not assume a zero price is intentional. Zero new-build costs Check resource identifiers and whether cost-table basis_year values cover each planning window.

Use the exact keys in Data Tables Settings. For example, generation_table is recognized; a similar-looking key such as generators does not configure that table.

docs.title: Check paths and settings loading
docs.text:
• A settings directory loads its immediate *.yml files, not nested folders or *.yaml files. Avoid duplicate top-level keys across files: loading performs shallow replacement, not a recursive merge.
  • Relative data_location and input_folder paths resolve from the settings directory's parent, or from a single settings file's containing directory.
  • Relative RESOURCE_GROUPS and RESOURCE_GROUP_PROFILES paths resolve from the process working directory instead.
  • Configured tables are searched in both data_location and input_folder; duplicate matches are an error.

The published examples split the two rules on purpose. Their Texas settings use data_location: data, which resolves to example_systems/TX-3-zone/data, but RESOURCE_GROUPS: example_systems/TX-3-zone/resource_groups, which only resolves when you run from the examples repository root. Running the same command from inside example_systems/TX-3-zone silently looks for resource groups that are not there.

See Configure Settings for organization and Run Multi-Scenario Studies for override behavior.

docs.title: Generator clustering produces unexpected groups
docs.text:
Check the logged number of units per region and technology, then inspect:

  • num_clusters and alt_num_clusters: existing technologies omitted from both are not included merely because they appear in the generation table.
  • tech_groups, tech_fuel_map, and model tags: matching rules differ between settings. Do not assume every technology field uses the same substring rules.
  • Operating/retirement years and source filters. Blank retirement_year means no planned retirement; filtering it with > 2030 drops blank values.

For myopic multi-period runs, use the same generation source in every period so cluster membership stays consistent. See Existing Generators.

docs.title: Demand or generation profiles are missing
docs.text:
Check that source rows cover every required base region/site, planning year, weather year, and time step. Confirm filters have not removed needed rows and that profile identifiers match resource metadata. For aggregated demand regions, supply the constituent base regions, not just an aggregate label.

Review Demand Settings and Configure Renewable Clusters.

docs.title: Resource files are empty or absent
docs.text:
Default GenX outputs are split into resources/Thermal.csv, Vre.csv, and other resource types. Files for empty types are omitted. Inspect the output layout before assuming a missing legacy Generators_data.csv indicates failure.

If expected resources are missing, check source coverage, filters, existing-unit cluster settings, and model tags. A legacy setting passing validation does not prove it affects output; for example, new_gen_not_available is not applied.

docs.title: Inspect settings and tables in Python
docs.text:
For deeper diagnostics, load the settings from the study directory:

from pathlib import Path

from powergenome.settings import load_settings
from powergenome.database import initialize_data_manager, list_tables

settings = load_settings(Path("settings"))
print(settings.get("model_year"))
print(settings.get("model_regions"))
initialize_data_manager(settings, settings["data_location"])
print(list_tables())

This inspects base settings. Compare them with the saved case/period settings when investigating scenario-specific behavior.

docs.title: Getting help
docs.text:
Share the command, PowerGenome version, first relevant error, and a minimal reproducible configuration on GitHub or groups.io. Redact credentials, private paths, and sensitive data from settings and logs before sharing.

The System Design tool provides starting settings, not a guarantee that your local data covers them.

docs.title: Configure Energy Share Requirements
docs.text:
Energy Share Requirements (ESR) are constraints that require a minimum fraction of load to be served by eligible resources. They are how PowerGenome models Renewable Portfolio Standards (RPS) and Clean Energy Standards (CES).

This guide walks through setting up ESR constraints and assigning resource eligibility.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• A working PowerGenome settings folder (see Getting Started)
  • An extra_inputs folder referenced by input_folder in settings

docs.title: How ESR constraints work
docs.text:
An ESR constraint says: "At least X% of load in zone Z must be served by eligible resources for constraint N."

Two inputs define each constraint:

  1. emission_policies.csv — sets the minimum fraction per zone per constraint
  2. model_tag_values (ESR tags) — marks which resources are eligible for which constraint

PowerGenome writes these to Energy_share_requirement.csv (zone requirements) and Resource_energy_share_requirement.csv (resource eligibility) in the GenX output.

docs.title: Step 1: Create the emission policies CSV
docs.text:
In your extra_inputs folder, create emission_policies.csv with case_id, year, region, and policy columns. case_id may be omitted when every row applies to the current case, but include it when using copy_case_id.

Column naming:

  • ESR_<N> — energy share requirement constraint N (fraction, e.g. 0.5 = 50%)
  • CO_2_Cap_Zone_<N> — marks zone as part of CO₂ cap constraint N (1 = included)
  • CO_2_Max_Mtons_<N> — CO₂ cap in million metric tons for constraint N

docs.title: Single-region example (RPS applied to all zones equally)
docs.text:
case_id,year,region,ESR_1
all,2030,all,0.50
all,2040,all,0.70
all,2050,all,0.90

A single policy row for a case and year applies its values to every model region. Here all makes that intent clear.

docs.title: Published multi-region example
docs.text:
The CA/AZ example uses two model regions with a different RPS and CES in each:

case_id,year,region,ESR_1,ESR_2,ESR_3
base,2030,CA,0.20,0.25,0
base,2030,AZ,0.087,0.087,0
base,2045,CA,0.15,0.15,0
base,2045,AZ,0.087,0.087,0

The region names match model_regions (CA and AZ), not the ReEDS base regions behind them. The Texas example has the same shape for TX1-TX3 but leaves every ESR column at 0, which is a useful starting point when you want the table structure without a binding policy.

docs.title: Multi-case example
docs.text:
Use case_id = all as a fallback for cases with no explicit rows. Use a specific case_id to vary policies across scenarios:

case_id,year,region,ESR_1
all,2030,all,0.50
high_policy,2030,all,0.70
low_policy,2030,all,0.30

The fallback is selected only when the case ID is absent from the entire policy table, not separately for each year or region. Include every needed year for an explicit case.

docs.title: Copy policies from another case
docs.text:
Use copy_case_id to reuse another case's policies rather than duplicating rows:

case_id,year,region,copy_case_id,ESR_1
baseline,2030,all,,0.50
alternative,2030,all,baseline,

alternative copies the policy values from baseline for the same year and region. Keep case_id, year, and region as the first three columns.

docs.title: Step 2: Point settings to the file
docs.text:
# settings/policies.yml
input_folder: extra_inputs
emission_policies_table: emission_policies.csv

emission_policies_table is loaded through the DataManager, so the value may use any supported DataManager table configuration rather than only a CSV path. The legacy emission_policies_fn key is still accepted as an alias; both published examples currently use it.

docs.title: Step 3: Define which resources are eligible
docs.text:
In model_tag_values in settings, add ESR tags. The tag names must match the column names in your CSV (ESR_1, ESR_2, etc.):

model_tag_names:
  - THERM
  - VRE
  - MUST_RUN
  - STOR
  - HYDRO
  - ESR_1    # RPS: renewable energy requirement
  - ESR_2    # CES: clean energy standard

model_tag_values:
  ESR_1:
    LandbasedWind: 1
    OffShoreWind: 1
    UtilityPV: 1
    ResPV: 1
    Hydroelectric: 1
    Geothermal: 1
    NaturalGas: 0
    Coal: 0
    Nuclear: 0

  ESR_2:
    LandbasedWind: 1    # Eligible for CES
    OffShoreWind: 1
    UtilityPV: 1
    Nuclear: 1          # Nuclear counts as clean
    NaturalGas_CCS: 1   # Gas with CCS may count as clean
    NaturalGas: 0
    Coal: 0

Only resources with tag value 1 count toward the corresponding constraint. Both published examples use this split: ESR_1 covers renewables, ESR_2 adds nuclear and CCS, and ESR_3 stays at zero.

Tag keys in model_tag_values are included even if they are absent from model_tag_names. Check the resource technology names in your data and adjust the examples above to match.

docs.title: Step 4: Clean Energy Standard (CES) credits
docs.text: PowerGenome's GenX output validates ESR_* resource tags as binary values. It does not calculate emission-rate-based fractional CES credits from an ESR_CES_numerator setting. Use binary eligibility or configure a different policy mechanism in the downstream model.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
After running PowerGenome, check the output:

policies/Energy_share_requirement.csv — should have one row per zone and one ESR_<N> column with the fraction you specified.

resources/policy_assignments/Resource_energy_share_requirement.csv — should have one row per resource with ESR_<N> = 1 for eligible resources and 0 for others.

Cross-check that the technologies you expect to be eligible are marked 1.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
ESR columns missing from output

Confirm emission_policies_table is set in settings and the file is in input_folder. If the CSV has no ESR_* columns, no ESR output is produced.

Resources not marked as eligible

Check that each key in model_tag_values is a substring of the resource technology field. Matching is case-insensitive and ignores underscores. Inspect the resource CSVs and adjust the keys accordingly.

Wrong fraction applied to a region

If a case/year has only one policy row, PowerGenome applies it to every zone, regardless of its region value. Use multiple per-region rows when zones need different fractions.

docs.title: Modify Generator Attributes with Custom Formulas
docs.text: This guide shows how to apply custom formulas to existing generator attributes, such as increasing fixed O&M costs based on plant age.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The resource_attr_modifiers parameter allows you to define custom formulas that modify generator attributes based on other data fields. This is useful for:

  • Age-based cost adjustments: Increase O&M costs as plants get older
  • Capacity-based modifications: Scale costs with unit size
  • Custom adjustments: Combine a rate and a column from the generator data

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
resource_attr_modifiers:
  <technology_name>:
    - attribute: <column_to_modify>
      formula:
        op: <operation>  # "add", "mul", "sub", "truediv", or "replace"
        rate: <numeric_value>
        multiplier: <column_name>

Parameters:

  • <technology_name>: Technology to modify (case-insensitive substring match)
  • attribute: Column in generator dataframe to modify
  • formula.op: Operation to apply (see below)
  • formula.rate: Numeric rate/coefficient
  • formula.multiplier: Column name containing values to multiply by rate

docs.title: Operations
docs.text: Operation Behavior Formula add Add to existing value new_value = old_value + (rate × multiplier) mul Multiply existing value new_value = old_value × (rate × multiplier) sub Subtract from existing value new_value = old_value - (rate × multiplier) truediv Divide existing value new_value = old_value / (rate × multiplier) replace Replace existing value new_value = rate × multiplier

docs.title: Increase O&M with Plant Age
docs.text:
Increase fixed O&M costs by $126/MW-yr for each year of plant age:

resource_attr_modifiers:
  conventional steam coal:
    - attribute: fom_per_mwyr
      formula:
        op: add
        rate: 126  # $/MW-yr per year of age
        multiplier: age

How it works:

  1. Matches all generators with "conventional steam coal" in technology name
  2. For each matched generator: fom_per_mwyr = fom_per_mwyr + (126 × age)
  3. Example: 20-year-old plant adds $2,520/MW-yr to base O&M

This exact block is in settings/resources.yml in both the Texas and CA/AZ example systems, so it is a safe reference for the expected format.

docs.title: Multiple Attributes for One Technology
docs.text:
Apply multiple formulas to the same technology:

resource_attr_modifiers:
  natural gas fired combined cycle:
    - attribute: fom_per_mwyr
      formula:
        op: add
        rate: 50  # $/MW-yr per year
        multiplier: age
    - attribute: heat_rate_mmbtu_mwh
      formula:
        op: add
        rate: 0.005  # MMBtu/MWh per year of age
        multiplier: age

This increases both fixed O&M and heat rate as plants age.

docs.title: Replace Instead of Add
docs.text:
Set a value based entirely on a formula (ignoring existing value):

resource_attr_modifiers:
  biomass:
    - attribute: fom_per_mwyr
      formula:
        op: replace
        rate: 100  # Illustrative coefficient
        multiplier: capacity_mw

With replace, the original fom_per_mwyr value is ignored and replaced by 100 × capacity_mw. Check units and input columns for your own formula.

docs.title: Multiple Technologies
docs.text:
Modify different technologies with different formulas:

resource_attr_modifiers:
  conventional steam coal:
    - attribute: fom_per_mwyr
      formula:
        op: add
        rate: 126
        multiplier: age
  natural gas:
    - attribute: fom_per_mwyr
      formula:
        op: add
        rate: 75
        multiplier: age
  nuclear:
    - attribute: fom_per_mwyr
      formula:
        op: add
        rate: 200
        multiplier: age

Each technology gets its own age-based adjustment rate.

docs.title: Available Attributes
docs.text:
Common attributes you can modify:

Attribute Description Units fom_per_mwyr Fixed O&M cost $/MW-yr vom_per_mwh Variable O&M cost $/MWh heat_rate_mmbtu_mwh Heat rate MMBtu/MWh minimum_load_mw Minimum load MW

Available multiplier columns depend on your data schema. Common ones:

  • age: Plant age in years
  • capacity_mw: Nameplate capacity
  • operating_year: Year plant started operation
  • Custom columns from your data tables

Column Requirements

Both the attribute and multiplier columns must exist in the generator dataframe. If either is missing, PowerGenome will raise a KeyError.

docs.title: Technology Matching
docs.text:
Technology names are matched case-insensitively using substring matching:

resource_attr_modifiers:
  coal:  # Matches "Conventional Steam Coal", "Coal IGCC", etc.
    - attribute: fom_per_mwyr
      formula:
        op: add
        rate: 126
        multiplier: age

Matching rules:

  • Case-insensitive: "Coal" matches "conventional steam coal"
  • Substring: "gas" matches "Natural Gas Fired Combined Cycle"
  • Underscores ignored, but spaces are not: "natural_gas" matches "NaturalGas", not "Natural Gas"
  • Keys are regular expressions; escape regex metacharacters when matching them literally.
  • An unmatched technology does not raise an error; it changes no rows.

Be specific enough to avoid unintended matches. For example:

  • ✅ "conventional steam coal": Matches only coal steam plants
  • ⚠️ "coal": Matches all coal technologies (steam, IGCC, etc.)
  • ❌ "steam": Matches coal steam AND gas steam turbines

docs.title: Execution Order
docs.text: resource_attr_modifiers is applied to individual rows immediately after loading the generation table and calculating age as the model year minus operating_year. It runs before region mapping and clustering, so later cluster-averaged values and region mapping columns are not available.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
PowerGenome validates formulas at runtime:

Missing attribute:

resource_attr_modifiers:
  coal:
    - attribute: nonexistent_column  # ❌ KeyError
      formula:
        op: add
        rate: 100
        multiplier: age

Missing multiplier:

resource_attr_modifiers:
  coal:
    - attribute: fom_per_mwyr
      formula:
        op: add
        rate: 100
        multiplier: nonexistent_column  # ❌ KeyError

Invalid operation:

resource_attr_modifiers:
  coal:
    - attribute: fom_per_mwyr
      formula:
        op: multiply  # ❌ Should be "mul"
        rate: 2
        multiplier: age

Missing keys:

resource_attr_modifiers:
  coal:
    - formula:  # ❌ Missing "attribute" key
        op: add
        rate: 100
        multiplier: age

All errors raise exceptions during pipeline execution.

docs.title: Complete Example
docs.text:
Full configuration applying age-based degradation to multiple technologies:

# Existing generator settings
num_clusters:
  Conventional Steam Coal: 3
  Natural Gas Fired Combined Cycle: 5
  Nuclear: 1

tech_groups:
  Combined Cycle:
    - Natural Gas Fired Combined Cycle
    - Natural Gas Steam Turbine

# Age-based cost adjustments
resource_attr_modifiers:
  conventional steam coal:
    - attribute: fom_per_mwyr
      formula:
        op: add
        rate: 126  # $/MW-yr per year of age
        multiplier: age
    - attribute: heat_rate_mmbtu_mwh
      formula:
        op: add
        rate: 0.003  # MMBtu/MWh per year of age
        multiplier: age

  natural gas fired combined cycle:
    - attribute: fom_per_mwyr
      formula:
        op: add
        rate: 75
        multiplier: age
    - attribute: heat_rate_mmbtu_mwh
      formula:
        op: add
        rate: 0.002  # MMBtu/MWh per year of age
        multiplier: age

  nuclear:
    - attribute: fom_per_mwyr
      formula:
        op: add
        rate: 200  # Higher aging costs for nuclear
        multiplier: age

Result: Older plants have higher O&M costs and worse heat rates, reflecting maintenance needs and efficiency degradation over time.

docs.title: Debugging
docs.text:
To verify formula application:

  1. Check generator output: Examine the relevant resources/*.csv file for modified values (Generators_data.csv with old_genx_format: true)
  2. Compare with/without modifiers: Run with resource_attr_modifiers commented out
  3. Validate formulas: Test with simple cases before complex scenarios

Example validation:

import pandas as pd
from powergenome.generators import apply_custom_gen_formula

gens = pd.DataFrame({
    "technology": ["Conventional Steam Coal"],
    "age": [20],
    "fom_per_mwyr": [10000],
})
modifiers = {
    "coal": [{
        "attribute": "fom_per_mwyr",
        "formula": {"op": "add", "rate": 126, "multiplier": "age"},
    }],
}
print(apply_custom_gen_formula(gens, modifiers)["fom_per_mwyr"])

The result is 12520 $/MW-yr.
