docs.title: Run Multiple Scenarios
docs.text:
Compare cases by adding one scenario CSV and one settings swap to a working configuration. This guide uses the published Texas three-zone example to compare base with a carbon_50 case in the 2030 and 2045 planning periods.

Use this page for the practical workflow. For supported shapes and combinations, see Scenario Management Settings. For precedence and execution order, see Multi-Scenario Architecture.

docs.title: 1. Download a working system
docs.text:
The published examples live in a separate PowerGenome-examples repository, so no PowerGenome source checkout is involved. Download the same pinned Texas snapshot that Getting Started uses:

mkdir scenario-study
cd scenario-study
curl --fail --location \
  https://codeload.github.com/PowerGenome/PowerGenome-examples/tar.gz/7e34f714469e68fca173cdb849f74c47be779420 \
  --output powergenome-examples.tar.gz
tar -xzf powergenome-examples.tar.gz --strip-components=1
rm powergenome-examples.tar.gz

That archive is under 1 MB. Choose another folder name if scenario-study already exists, and run every command below from the new folder.

Stay at the top of scenario-study/ and address the study as example_systems/TX-3-zone/; do not change into that folder. Its data_location and input_folder resolve from the settings folder's parent, but its published RESOURCE_GROUPS and RESOURCE_GROUP_PROFILES paths resolve from your working directory.

The example is demonstration data (240 synthetic profile time steps), not a production study. If you only need values to change over time within one case, use year-keyed settings instead.

Its example_systems/TX-3-zone/settings/model_definition.yml already defines:

model_regions: [TX1, TX2, TX3]
region_aggregations:
  TX1: [p60, p61, p62]
  TX2: [p63, p64]
  TX3: [p65, p67]
model_year: [2030, 2045]
model_first_planning_year: [2025, 2031]

These are existing values, not settings to add again. The first planning period is 2025–2030 and the second is 2031–2045. Keep the two planning-year lists in corresponding chronological order; they are paired by position, not sorted automatically.

docs.title: 2. Create Scenario Definitions
docs.text:
Replace the contents of example_systems/TX-3-zone/extra_inputs/scenario_inputs.csv with:

case_id,year,carbon_policy
base,2030,unchanged
carbon_50,2030,tax_50
base,2045,unchanged
carbon_50,2045,tax_50

The published file has a single base case and no dimension column; this version keeps base and adds the carbon_50 case. case_id and year are mandatory. Keep the same case ID across periods: each row is one case/year, not a new independent case. carbon_policy is a dimension name you choose; its values select the swaps in the next step.

Include every planning year for each complete case, chronologically within that case. Duplicate case/year pairs fail, but incomplete cases are not automatically rejected. Period numbers follow row order within each case, so a missing or out-of-order row can put a year in the wrong Inputs_pN directory.

docs.title: Add policy rows for the new case
docs.text:
The study's emission policy table is keyed by case_id (the published rows all use base), so a case with no matching rows stops the run with a KeyError such as ('carbon_50', 2030). Two mechanisms share one set of values across cases.

case_id: all treats a row as belonging to whichever case is running: rows whose case_id is all (any capitalization) are read as the requested case whenever that case has no rows of its own. Replace the contents of example_systems/TX-3-zone/extra_inputs/emission_policies.csv with:

case_id,year,region,ESR_1,ESR_2,ESR_3
all,2030,TX1,0,0,0
all,2030,TX2,0,0,0
all,2030,TX3,0,0,0
all,2045,TX1,0,0,0
all,2045,TX2,0,0,0
all,2045,TX3,0,0,0

Both base and carbon_50 then read these six rows, and adding another case needs no new policy rows. The substitution is decided per case, not per row: as soon as a case has even one row of its own, its all rows are left unused, so a case with 2030 rows but no 2045 rows fails on 2045.

copy_case_id is the alternative when each case needs its own rows, with values copied from a source case:

case_id,year,region,ESR_1,ESR_2,ESR_3,copy_case_id
base,2030,TX1,0,0,0,
base,2030,TX2,0,0,0,
base,2030,TX3,0,0,0,
base,2045,TX1,0,0,0,
base,2045,TX2,0,0,0,
base,2045,TX3,0,0,0,
carbon_50,2030,TX1,,,,base
carbon_50,2030,TX2,,,,base
carbon_50,2030,TX3,,,,base
carbon_50,2045,TX1,,,,base
carbon_50,2045,TX2,,,,base
carbon_50,2045,TX3,,,,base

The copy_case_id entries reuse the base values for carbon_50, so the cases carry identical policies and only one set of values needs maintenance. Duplicating the six base rows under case_id,carbon_50 works too. Every ESR_* value here is zero, so this step only satisfies the per-case lookup; real policies would need the values you intend for each case.

docs.title: 3. Configure Settings Management
docs.text:
Replace the contents of example_systems/TX-3-zone/settings/scenario_management.yml with:

scenario_definitions_fn: scenario_inputs.csv

settings_management:
  all_years:
    carbon_policy:
      unchanged: {}  # Keep the base settings
      tax_50:
        carbon_tax: 50

The published file is settings_management: {}, so replace it rather than adding a second mapping.

This is one swap: tax_50 sets carbon_tax to 50 USD per metric tonne of CO₂ for both years. The tax is added to fuel costs using fuel CO₂ content; it is not an emissions-cap setting. The policies from the previous step are unchanged and serve both cases, whichever mechanism you used.

The published settings/extra_inputs.yml already sets input_folder: extra_inputs and scenario_definitions_fn: scenario_inputs.csv, and it also names this study's emission policy table (emission_policies_fn: emission_policies.csv) from the previous step. scenario_definitions_fn is relative to input_folder, so it resolves to example_systems/TX-3-zone/extra_inputs/scenario_inputs.csv. The scenario_definitions_fn line in the block above therefore only repeats a value that is already set.

Keep each top-level setting in one file

A settings directory loads only its immediate *.yml files, not subfolders or .yaml files. These files are combined with shallow updates and no reliable file order. Do not add a second settings_management block in a different file: it could replace the whole mapping. Edit the existing block.

Configured relative data_location and input_folder paths are rooted at the parent of the settings directory (example_systems/TX-3-zone/). Relative RESOURCE_GROUPS and RESOURCE_GROUP_PROFILES paths instead use the working directory, which is why the commands stay at the top of scenario-study/.

docs.title: Validate Scenario Definitions
docs.text:
First validate the settings and source data:

validate_powergenome --settings_file example_systems/TX-3-zone/settings

This is not a substitute for checking the complete scenario matrix. To check the CSV and inspect the actual resolved swaps before generating files, run:

from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd

from powergenome.settings import build_scenario_settings, load_settings

settings = load_settings(Path("example_systems/TX-3-zone/settings"))
scenarios = pd.read_csv(
    Path(settings["input_folder"]) / settings["scenario_definitions_fn"]
)
years = settings["model_year"]
assert {"case_id", "year"}.issubset(scenarios.columns)
assert not scenarios.duplicated(["case_id", "year"]).any()
for case_id, rows in scenarios.groupby("case_id", sort=False):
    assert rows["year"].tolist() == years, case_id

resolved = build_scenario_settings(settings, scenarios)
for year in years:
    for case_id, case_settings in resolved[year].items():
        print(year, case_id, case_settings.get("carbon_tax", 0))

Expected values are 0 for base and 50 for carbon_50 in 2030 and 2045. Unknown dimension/level selections warn and leave settings unchanged; an explicit {} means intentionally keep the base value without a missing-selection warning. The example also emits warnings about unassigned model resource tags, resources missing from the operational-constraints table, missing transmission investment costs, and a hydro resource without a variable profile. Review these before adapting it for a real study.

docs.title: Test Single Scenario
docs.text:
Generate both periods of the base case first:

run_powergenome \
  --settings_file example_systems/TX-3-zone/settings \
  --results_folder base_check \
  --case-id base

Inspect base_check/log.txt and the two period folders before running both cases. PowerGenome generates model inputs; it does not solve the GenX model.

docs.title: Run the scenario set
docs.text:
run_powergenome \
  --settings_file example_systems/TX-3-zone/settings \
  --results_folder results

With default GenX output, the directory layout is:

results/
├── log.txt
├── base/
│   └── Inputs/
│       ├── Inputs_p1/
│       │   ├── resources/
│       │   ├── system/
│       │   ├── policies/
│       │   └── powergenome_case_settings.yml
│       └── Inputs_p2/
└── carbon_50/
    └── Inputs/
        ├── Inputs_p1/
        └── Inputs_p2/

Each period has the same subdirectory layout. Confirm the resolved carbon_tax, model_year, and model_first_planning_year in powergenome_case_settings.yml. Paying 50 USD per tonne of CO₂ raises the delivered price of emitting fuels, which you can check in system/Fuels_data.csv: in this example the first period goes from 3.16 to 5.82 USD/MMBtu for natural gas and from 2.07 to 6.84 for coal, and the second period from 4.86 to 7.51 and from 2.13 to 6.91. Read the row labeled with Time_Index 1; row 0 holds the CO₂ content per MMBtu.

docs.title: Running Scenarios Sequentially
docs.text:
PowerGenome runs sequentially, grouped by year in the order years first appear in the CSV, then by case order within each year. This example runs both 2030 cases before both 2045 cases. There is no scenario --num_workers option; clustering_n_jobs controls renewable clustering, not case execution.

Monitor a run from another terminal in scenario-study/:

tail -f results/log.txt

docs.title: Selective Execution
docs.text:
Select one or more existing case IDs; each selection includes all its CSV years:

run_powergenome \
  --settings_file example_systems/TX-3-zone/settings \
  --results_folder selected_results \
  --case-id base carbon_50

Use --case-id with a hyphen. See the CLI Reference for flags such as --no-current-gens, --no-load, and --sort-gens. For MacroEnergy output alongside GenX, add --macro; for Macro-only output, add --macro --no-genx. See Macro Output Settings.

docs.title: Resume Failed Runs
docs.text: There is no automatic resume or skip-completed behavior. Check the log, then rerun only the affected case IDs into a new results folder, using the same --case-id pattern. Do not delete successful outputs to retry a failed case.

docs.title: Extend the study
docs.text:
Keep the first addition small: one dimension and one expected output change. Use the reference rather than duplicating a large matrix of combinations:

  • Technology Costs: ATB cost cases and numeric resource modifiers.
  • Technology Availability: complete replacement lists and region limitations.
  • Fuel prices and demand: matching source-data scenarios rather than unsupported growth settings.
  • Retirement assumptions: change source data between cases, not periods within a myopic case.
  • Transmission and regional reserves: reinforcement limits and nested reserve-margin shapes.
  • Multi-period combinations and merge precedence: combine year-keyed values, all_years, and year-specific swaps deliberately.
  • Copy Case Policies: reuse policy rows without copying an entire scenario.

docs.title: Scenario Not Running
docs.text: Check that the filename resolves under input_folder, required CSV columns are present, the selected case ID exists, and each case has all its planning years. A scenario CSV must be enabled with scenario_definitions_fn; without it, settings_management swaps are not applied.

docs.title: Parameter Not Changing
docs.text: Check dimension and level spelling, YAML value types, and the applicable year block. Inspect the resolved case settings, not just the base YAML. Scenario swaps deep-merge nested dictionaries but replace lists entirely. Two selected dimensions cannot modify the same leaf setting within one year block; see conflict rules.

docs.title: Use Year-Keyed Settings Values
docs.text:
This guide shows how to set values by planning year directly in settings files.

Use this pattern when you want different values in different model years without building a full scenario matrix.

docs.title: Before You Start
docs.text:
You should already have:

  • A working settings folder
  • Planning years defined (e.g., model_periods)
  • A parameter you want to vary by year

If you need full multi-case scenario logic, use Run Multi-Scenario Studies.

docs.title: 1. Start With A Working Baseline
docs.text:
Example planning years:

model_periods:
  - [2020, 2030]
  - [2031, 2040]

docs.title: 2. Convert A Scalar Value To A Year-Keyed Value
docs.text:
Suppose you currently have:

carbon_tax: 25

Convert it to year-keyed form:

carbon_tax:
  2030: 25
  2040: 50

PowerGenome will resolve one value per planning year when building case settings. Use unquoted integer year keys between 1900 and 2200; default is optional.

Both published example systems leave carbon_tax: 0 as a scalar in settings/fuels.yml, so they are a realistic place to start this conversion: the value already exists and you only change its shape.

docs.title: 3. Use Fallback Values With default
docs.text:
Use a fallback when you do not want to list every year explicitly.

carbon_tax:
  2030: 25
  default: 40

Behavior:

  • Year 2030 uses 25 (exact year match).
  • Any other planning year uses 40 (default fallback).

docs.title: 4. Apply Year-Keyed Values In Nested Settings
docs.text:
You can use this pattern inside nested dictionaries too. Resolution traverses dictionaries, not dictionaries inside lists. It skips settings_management itself, but resolves selected swaps after applying them.

resource_modifiers:
  utility_pv:
    technology: UtilityPV
    tech_detail: Class1
    capex_mw:
      2030: [mul, 0.90]
      2040: [mul, 0.80]

docs.title: 5. Validate Coverage Rules
docs.text:
For each year-keyed dictionary, PowerGenome expects either:

  • Explicit entries for all planning years, or
  • A default fallback key

If only some years are covered and no fallback exists, PowerGenome raises a ValueError. With a scenario CSV, coverage is checked against the years in the selected rows.

Example that fails for planning years [2030, 2040]:

capex_mw:
  2030: [mul, 0.95]

Fix by adding missing years or a fallback:

capex_mw:
  2030: [mul, 0.95]
  default: [mul, 1.0]

docs.title: 6. Keep settings_management For Scenario Dimensions
docs.text:
Year-keyed values handle variation by planning year.

Use settings_management when you need differences across scenario columns (policy, fuel case, technology assumptions, and so on).

A common pattern:

  • Baseline year variation via year-keyed values
  • Scenario-specific deltas via settings_management

docs.title: Validate Settings Before Running
docs.text:
Run validation from your study directory before generating inputs:

validate_powergenome --settings_file settings

run_powergenome also validates automatically. Standalone validation helps you find configuration problems without waiting for generator clustering and output writing.

Validation is not exhaustive

Passing validation does not establish that inputs are complete, scientifically appropriate, or ready for optimization. Review the logs and generated files, especially for a new study or dataset.

docs.title: Validate a known-good configuration first
docs.text:
To confirm the validator itself works, run it against a published example from the root of a clone of PowerGenome-examples rather than from inside the example system folder. Check out the same pinned snapshot the Getting Started tutorial uses, so the exercise keeps validating the configuration it was written for even as the default branch moves on:

git clone https://github.com/PowerGenome/PowerGenome-examples.git
cd PowerGenome-examples
git checkout 7e34f714469e68fca173cdb849f74c47be779420
validate_powergenome --settings_file example_systems/TX-3-zone/settings

Remove nothing and change nothing: these settings are expected to load and pass the settings phase. If this run reports errors, check your installation and the data download before debugging your own settings. Swap in example_systems/CA_AZ/settings to exercise a two-region setup with two capacity reserve constraints.

docs.title: Understand the result
docs.text:
• Errors stop the pipeline. Fix them before running again.
  • Warnings allow the pipeline to continue, but can identify consequential problems such as missing fuel prices or technology costs becoming zero.

The standalone command groups issues by severity and category. The pipeline writes them to the terminal and <results_folder>/log.txt. Use each issue's Detail values to locate the affected regions, fuels, resources, or years.

Reported issue What to check Missing required key Add the key with the correct type; see Model Definition. Inconsistent planning years Use valid model_periods, or equally sized model_year and model_first_planning_year lists. Missing path or table Check path resolution, exact setting keys, and unique source filenames; see Configure Data Tables. Unknown region Compare spelling and base/model-region roles in settings and tables. Missing fuel-price coverage Supply every required fuel, scenario, base region, and year; check fuel_scenarios against the table. Missing new-resource cost years Provide cost rows whose basis_year overlaps each planning window. Missing model tags Ensure each new resource matches the appropriate model_tag_values; inspect the written resource files too.

Do not suppress a warning merely to obtain a successful exit code. For example, missing fuel prices may become $0/MMBtu, materially changing a model's choices.

docs.title: Choose the scope
docs.text:
# Settings-only checks, without loading source tables
validate_powergenome --settings_file settings --skip-data-checks

# Force fresh settings and data checks
validate_powergenome --settings_file settings --no-validation-cache
Flag Purpose --settings_file PATH Settings folder or single YAML file; required. --skip-data-checks Check settings structure and consistency only. --no-validation-cache Ignore cached results; alias --force-validation. --no-fail Report errors but exit with code 0. Use only when your automation handles the reported failures separately.

docs.title: What is checked
docs.text:
Validation has two phases:

  1. Settings: required keys, planning-year shapes, paths, region-keyed settings, fuel definitions, and new-resource tag coverage.
  2. Settings against data: configured tables, regional coverage, transmission region names, fuel-price coverage, and new-resource cost-year coverage.

In run_powergenome, Phase 1 errors stop execution before DataManager initialization; Phase 2 errors also stop the run. The standalone validator can attempt Phase 2 even if Phase 1 reports errors. A table-loading exception can therefore still require fixing the settings before a complete report is possible.

docs.title: Skipping validation when nothing changed
docs.text:
Results are cached under <input_folder>/validation_cache/ when input_folder is configured. Unchanged settings, validation code, and source fingerprints allow checks to be replayed rather than recomputed. Cached warnings still print; cached errors still fail.

Use --no-validation-cache on either CLI whenever you need a fresh check. To turn caching off for a study, set:

use_validation_cache: false

docs.title: ATB Technology Names
docs.text:
PowerGenome uses technology names from NREL's Annual Technology Baseline (ATB) for new-build generation resources. This page documents the valid technology and tech_detail names for each ATB version.

Technology Naming Convention

Each new_resources entry supplies separate technology, tech_detail, cost_case, and size_mw values. For example, Class3 is a detail and Moderate is a cost case.

docs.title: Cost Scenarios
docs.text:
Most ATB technologies support three cost scenarios:

  • Conservative: High-cost projection
  • Moderate: Mid-range cost projection
  • Advanced: Low-cost projection with optimistic technology improvements

The cost scenario is selected per resource in the new_resources list, where the third element of each entry is the cost case (e.g., Moderate, Advanced, or Conservative). Set the case for each entry. There is no standalone atb_cost_case setting. Available names and cases depend on the actual cost and heat-rate tables configured for the chosen vintage.

# Specify ATB data year

  - [UtilityPV, Class1, Advanced, 100]
  - [NaturalGas, 1-on-1 Combined Cycle (H-Frame), Moderate, 500]
  - [Utility-Scale Battery Storage, Lithium Ion, Moderate, 100]

Each entry has the format [technology, tech_detail, cost_case, size_mw].

docs.title: Command Line Interface
docs.text:
PowerGenome provides two commands:

Command Purpose run_powergenome Execute the full data pipeline and write model input files (GenX and/or Macro) validate_powergenome Check settings and data for configuration mistakes without running the pipeline

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text: run_powergenome --settings_file SETTINGS_PATH --results_folder OUTPUT_PATH

docs.title: --settings_file / -sf
docs.text:
Path to a settings file or a directory containing settings files.

Type: String (path) Default: example_settings.yml Example: --settings_file settings

Note

Directory mode loads immediate *.yml files only, not subdirectories or .yaml files. Avoid duplicate top-level keys across files: later files replace whole values, and file order is not a configuration interface.

docs.title: --results_folder / -rf
docs.text:
Directory where output files will be saved. Created if it does not exist; its parent directory must already exist.

Type: String (path) Default: A timestamp, for example 2026-01-15 14.30.00 Example: --results_folder my_study_outputs

docs.title: --case-id / -c
docs.text:
Run only the specified case IDs from scenario_definitions_fn. Without a scenario definitions file, this selection is ignored with a warning.

Type: One or more case IDs, separated by spaces Default: Run all cases Example: --case-id baseline high_demand

run_powergenome -sf settings -rf output --case-id baseline high_demand

docs.title: --sort-gens
docs.text:
Sort generator resources alphabetically within each region. Existing and new-build resources remain in separate groups.

Type: Boolean flag Default: False Example: --sort-gens

Useful for:

  • Comparing outputs across runs
  • Version control (reduces diff noise)
  • Easier manual inspection

docs.title: --no-current-gens
docs.text:
Skip existing generator clustering. Only new-build resources will be included.

Type: Boolean flag Default: False (existing generators are clustered) Example: --no-current-gens

Use when:

  • Building greenfield scenarios
  • Testing new-build resource configurations
  • Debugging new resource issues

docs.title: --no-load
docs.text:
Skip demand profile generation. Load files must be provided manually.

Type: Boolean flag Default: False (load profiles are generated) Example: --no-load

Use when:

  • Testing generator configurations
  • Load profiles are pre-generated
  • Debugging non-demand issues

docs.title: --macro
docs.text:
Write a MacroEnergy.jl (Macro) case in the simpleCSVinputs format, in addition to the default GenX output — a single run writes both formats. Can also be enabled with the macro_output: true setting. Set genx_output: false (or pass --no-genx) to write Macro inputs only.

Type: Boolean flag Default: False Example: --macro

Note

Writing both formats in one run reuses all the intermediate data processing and is faster than running PowerGenome once per model.

docs.title: --genx
docs.text:
Write GenX Inputs files (the default output when no output flag or output setting is set). Can be combined with --macro to explicitly request both formats in a single run. Can also be controlled with the genx_output: true setting.

Type: Boolean flag Default: False (GenX is written by default regardless; this flag is explicit) Example: --genx

docs.title: --no-genx
docs.text:
Do not write GenX Inputs files. A hard override that wins over both --genx and an explicit genx_output: true setting. Combine with --macro (or macro_output: true) to write Macro inputs only from the command line, without editing a settings file.

Type: Boolean flag Default: False Example: --no-genx

# Write Macro inputs only
run_powergenome -sf settings -rf output --macro --no-genx

docs.title: --no-validation-cache / --force-validation
docs.text:
Always run the Phase 1/2 validation checks, ignoring any cached results. By default, validation results are replayed from a cache keyed on the settings and a fingerprint (size, modification time, and deterministic content samples) of the data files backing the configured tables, so a re-run with unchanged inputs skips the check computation. Equivalent to use_validation_cache: false in settings.

Type: Boolean flag Default: Not set (follows use_validation_cache; caching is enabled by default) Example: --force-validation

run_powergenome -sf settings --no-validation-cache

docs.title: --no-gens
docs.text: Skip generator processing entirely, including existing and new-build resources. This does not disable demand or transmission processing.

docs.title: --no-transmission
docs.text: Skip transmission processing and network output.

docs.title: --multi-period / -mp and --no-multi-period
docs.text:
Multi-period output is enabled by default. These two flags are mutually exclusive and only make the choice explicit:

  • --multi-period / -mp enables it.
  • --no-multi-period disables it.

Disabling omits the Min_Retired_* retirement requirements and the multi-stage transmission fields. It does not change which planning years are processed; use model_year and model_first_planning_year for that.

docs.title: --help / -h
docs.text:
Display help message with all available flags.

run_powergenome --help

docs.title: Basic run
docs.text:
run_powergenome \
    --settings_file my_study/settings \
    --results_folder my_study/results

docs.title: Run specific scenarios
docs.text:
run_powergenome \
    -sf settings \
    -rf output \
    --case-id baseline high_renewable low_cost

docs.title: Greenfield with sorted output
docs.text:
run_powergenome \
    -sf settings \
    -rf output \
    --no-current-gens \
    --sort-gens

docs.title: Debug new resources only
docs.text:
run_powergenome \
    -sf settings \
    -rf output \
    --no-current-gens \
    --no-load

docs.title: Output organization
docs.text:
With a scenario definitions file, results are organized by case and planning period:

results_folder/
├── log.txt
├── case_id_1/
│   └── Inputs/
│       ├── Inputs_p1/
│       │   ├── resources/
│       │   ├── system/
│       │   └── policies/
│       └── Inputs_p2/
└── case_id_2/
    └── Inputs/
        └── Inputs_p1/

Without scenario_definitions_fn, period folders are directly under results_folder/Inputs/, for example results_folder/Inputs/Inputs_p1/.

  • Inputs/Inputs_p#/: GenX input folders resources/, system/, and policies/ by default; old_genx_format: true selects legacy flat CSVs (written unless --no-genx)
  • Macro case: written when --macro/macro_output: true is enabled; see Output File Format for its layout
  • log.txt: One detailed execution log at the results root, not per case

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: Code Meaning 0 Success 1 General error (check log for details) 2 Invalid arguments

docs.title: validate_powergenome
docs.text: Validates your settings for common configuration mistakes without running the full pipeline. See Validate Settings Before Running for a full guide.

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text: validate_powergenome --settings_file SETTINGS_PATH

docs.title: --settings_file / -sf
docs.text: Required. Path to the folder containing your settings YAML files (same value you pass to run_powergenome).

docs.title: --skip-data-checks
docs.text:
Only run Phase 1 (settings-only checks). DataManager is not initialized, so no data files need to be present.

Default: Both phases run.

validate_powergenome -sf settings --skip-data-checks

docs.title: --no-fail
docs.text:
Exit with code 0 even when errors are found. Errors are still logged at ERROR level. Useful in scripts or CI pipelines where you want to review the output without triggering a failure.

Default: Exit with code 1 when any ERROR-level issue is found.

validate_powergenome -sf settings --no-fail

docs.title: --no-validation-cache / --force-validation
docs.text:
Always run the checks, ignoring any cached validation results. By default, results are replayed from a cache keyed on the settings and a fingerprint (size, modification time, and deterministic content samples) of the data files, so unchanged inputs skip the checks — and Phase 2 skips loading the DataManager entirely. See Skipping validation when nothing changed.

Default: Cache enabled (unless use_validation_cache: false is set in settings).

validate_powergenome -sf settings --no-validation-cache

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: Code Meaning 0 No errors found (warnings may still be present) 1 One or more ERROR-level issues found

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
PowerGenome respects these environment variables (legacy, prefer settings YAML):

  • RESOURCE_GROUPS: Path to renewable resource group definitions
  • RESOURCE_GROUP_PROFILES: Path to generation profiles
  • EFS_DATA: Path to NREL EFS electrification data
  • DISTRIBUTED_GEN_DATA: Legacy distributed-generation data path

DATA_LOCATION is not a supported environment-variable substitute for the data_location YAML setting.

Environment variables are always single paths. When using settings YAML, RESOURCE_GROUPS and RESOURCE_GROUP_PROFILES may instead be a list of paths (split across multiple folders).

Deprecated

Using environment variables for paths is deprecated. Use settings YAML parameters instead:

data_location: /path/to/data
RESOURCE_GROUPS: /path/to/groups
RESOURCE_GROUP_PROFILES: /path/to/profiles

docs.title: Logging
docs.text:
PowerGenome uses Python's logging module. Logs show:

  • Data loading progress
  • Clustering operations
  • Missing data warnings
  • Regional mismatches
  • Cost calculations

Example log output:

INFO:powergenome.run_powergenome:Loading settings from settings
INFO:powergenome.database:Initializing DataManager
INFO:powergenome.generators:Clustering 145 generators into 12 clusters
WARNING:powergenome.generators:Region p5 not found in fuel price data
INFO:powergenome.GenX:Writing output files to results/case1/Inputs/Inputs_p1/

docs.title: Programmatic usage
docs.text:
run_powergenome can also be called from Python:

from powergenome.run_powergenome import main

main(
    settings_file="path/to/settings",
    results_folder="path/to/results",
    case_id=["case1", "case2"],
)

main() still parses the process command line before applying these keyword arguments. In notebooks or applications with their own arguments, prefer calling the CLI in a subprocess with an explicit argument list. This is an internal entry point, not a separate stable Python API.

docs.title: Settings folder not found
docs.text:
Error: Settings path 'settings' does not exist

Solution: Provide absolute path or path relative to current directory

docs.title: No scenario definitions file
docs.text: A scenario CSV is optional. Without one, PowerGenome runs the configured planning years as a single case. If you intended to use cases, set scenario_definitions_fn to a CSV under input_folder, with case_id and year columns.

docs.title: Permission denied writing output
docs.text:
PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: 'results/case1'

Solution: Ensure write permissions on output directory or choose different location

See Debugging for more troubleshooting tips.

docs.title: Input Table Schemas
docs.text:
PowerGenome reads source data from files (CSV or Parquet) or a database. The DataManager maps each settings key to a standardized internal table name. This page describes the required columns and data types for each table.

Finding your data files

Set data_location in your settings YAML to the folder containing these files. See Configure Data Tables for the full configuration syntax, including column projection and row filtering.

docs.title: Table reference
docs.text:
Settings key Internal name Typical file generation_table generation generators.csv plant_region_table plant_region plant_region_map.csv resource_cost_table resource_cost technology_costs.csv resource_heat_rate_table resource_heat_rate technology_heat_rates.csv operational_constraints_table operational_constraints operational_constraints.csv transmission_constraints_table transmission_constraints transmission.csv transmission_cost_table transmission_cost network_costs.csv fuel_price_table fuel_price fuel_prices.csv dollar_year_table dollar_year cpi_data.csv regional_cost_factor_table regional_cost_factor regional_cost_multipliers.csv demand_table demand load_curves.csv supplemental_demand_table supplemental_demand supplemental_demand.csv emission_policies_table emission_policies emission_policies.csv demand_segments_table demand_segments demand_segments.csv distributed_capacity_table distributed_capacity distributed_capacity.csv distributed_profiles_table distributed_profiles distributed_profiles.csv

distributed_profile_table is also accepted for distributed_profiles. See Configure Data Tables for aliases and configuration options.

docs.title: Existing generators (generation)
docs.text:
Contains one row per generator unit. Matched to model regions via the plant_region table.

Column Type Required Notes technology string Yes EIA technology name (e.g. Natural Gas Fired Combustion Turbine) plant_id integer Yes EIA plant ID generator_id string Recommended Identifies the unit in cluster-assignment outputs capacity_mw float Yes Nameplate capacity in MW capacity_mwh float Yes Storage energy capacity in MWh; values may be blank for non-storage operating_year integer Yes Year plant came online; used to calculate age retirement_year integer No Year the unit leaves service; controls capacity listed in Min_Retired_*_Cap_MW and if a unit contributes to the characteristics (heat rate, unit size, etc.) of a resource. A blank value (or a missing column) means the unit has no planned retirement, so it operates through the whole horizon historical_capacity_factor float No Source-data attribute heat_rate_mmbtu_mwh float Yes Average heat rate; supply appropriate values for thermal generators vom_per_mwh float Yes Variable O&M cost ($/MWh) fom_per_mwyr float Yes Fixed O&M cost ($/MW-year) energy_source_code string No Source fuel code (e.g. NG, BIT, SUN) minimum_load_mw float No Source-data attribute; operational constraints set Min_Power

docs.title: Plant–region map (plant_region)
docs.text:
Maps EIA plant IDs to model regions. Only plants listed here will be included in the model.

Column Type Required Notes plant_id integer Yes EIA plant ID; must match generation table region string Yes Base region or unaggregated model region name

docs.title: New-build technology costs (resource_cost)
docs.text:
Long-format table of cost and financial parameters for new-build resources. Each parameter is its own row.

Column Type Required Notes technology string Yes ATB technology name tech_detail string Yes Technology detail (e.g. Lithium Ion) cost_case string Yes ATB cost case (e.g. Advanced, Moderate, Conservative) financial_case string Yes Financial assumption set (e.g. R&D, Market) parameter string Yes Cost parameter name (e.g. capex_mw, fixed_o_m_mw, wacc_real) parameter_value float Yes Value for this parameter units string No Units string for reference data_year integer Yes ATB vintage year basis_year integer Yes Technology deployment year costs apply to cap_recovery_years integer No Source attribute; the new-build workflow uses the corresponding settings dollar_year integer Yes Dollar-year for cost figures

docs.title: Technology heat rates (resource_heat_rate)
docs.text:
Heat rate by technology used for new-build thermal resources.

Column Type Required Notes technology string Yes ATB technology name tech_detail string Yes ATB detail variant cost_case string Yes ATB cost case basis_year integer Yes Deployment year data_year integer Yes ATB vintage year heat_rate float Yes Heat rate in MMBtu/MWh

docs.title: Operational constraints (operational_constraints)
docs.text:
Per-technology or per-resource overrides for GenX operational parameters. Matching values are applied to generator rows before output formatting.

Column Type Required Notes Resource string Yes Resource name or technology name pattern region string No Model region or all for all regions; omitted means all regions Min_Power float No Minimum power output fraction Self_Disch float No Storage self-discharge rate Eff_Up float No Charging efficiency Eff_Down float No Discharging efficiency Min_Duration float No Minimum storage duration (hours) Max_Duration float No Maximum storage duration (hours) Ramp_Up_Percentage float No Maximum ramp-up rate (fraction of capacity per hour) Ramp_Dn_Percentage float No Maximum ramp-down rate Up_Time integer No Minimum up-time (hours) Down_Time integer No Minimum down-time (hours)

Non-null parameter values are applied to matching rows. The v6 output writer then splits those rows into resource files and may omit empty columns.

docs.title: Transmission constraints (transmission_constraints)
docs.text:
Existing inter-regional transfer capacities. Used to build Network.csv.

Column Type Required Notes region_from string Yes Source IPM or base region region_to string Yes Destination IPM or base region firm_ttc_mw float Yes Firm total transfer capacity in MW notes string No Optional description

docs.title: Transmission costs (transmission_cost)
docs.text:
Capital costs for new inter-regional transmission lines.

Column Type Required Notes start_region string Yes Model region at one end of the line dest_region string Yes Model region at the other end total_interconnect_cost_mw float Yes Total build cost ($/MW) total_interconnect_annuity_mw float Yes Annualized build cost ($/MW-year) total_line_loss_frac float No Fractional line loss start_id integer No Source node ID dest_id integer No Destination node ID dollar_year integer Yes Dollar-year for cost figures mw-km_per_mw float No Route length in MW-km per MW of capacity notes string No Optional description

docs.title: Fuel prices (fuel_price)
docs.text:
Time series of fuel prices by fuel type and region.

Column Type Required Notes year integer Yes Planning year fuel string Yes Fuel name; must match tech_fuel_map values in settings region string Yes Fuel price region price float Yes Fuel price (typically $/MMBtu) scenario string No Fuel price scenario; can be filtered in the table configuration data_year integer Yes Data vintage; include even for one vintage dollar_year integer For inflation adjustment Dollar-year for price figures

docs.title: Dollar-year / CPI (dollar_year)
docs.text:
Conversion factors for adjusting costs between dollar years.

Column Type Required Notes year integer Yes Calendar year period string No Period label (legacy column, may be omitted) value float Yes CPI index value

docs.title: Regional cost multipliers (regional_cost_factor)
docs.text:
Adjustments to capital costs by technology and region.

Column Type Required Notes technology string Yes ATB technology name region string Yes Model region value float Yes Multiplier (1.0 = no adjustment)

docs.title: Demand / load profiles (demand)
docs.text:
Hourly load time series. One row per hour per region.

Column Type Required Notes time_index integer Yes Hour index within the source profile region string Yes Base region or unaggregated model region load_mw float Yes Load in MW year integer Yes Planning year weather_year integer No Meteorological year for the profile

docs.title: Supplemental demand (supplemental_demand)
docs.text: Adds hourly load before region aggregation. It uses region, time_index, and load_mw; optional year and weather_year select the applicable planning and weather years. See Add Supplemental Demand for coverage and aggregation rules.

docs.title: Emission policies and demand segments
docs.text:
emission_policies uses year, region, optional case_id and copy_case_id, and policy columns such as CO_2_Cap_Zone_1 and CO_2_Max_Mtons_1. If case_id is omitted, the current case is used; an all case can provide fallback values.

demand_segments contains GenX demand-curtailment inputs, such as Voll, Demand_Segment, Cost_of_Demand_Curtailment_per_MW, and Max_Demand_Curtailment. These columns are included in the demand output.

docs.title: Distributed capacity (distributed_capacity)
docs.text:
Installed distributed generation capacity by region and year.

Column Type Required Notes region string Yes Base region or unaggregated model region year integer Yes Planning year capacity_mw float Yes Total installed DG capacity in MW

docs.title: Distributed generation profiles (distributed_profiles)
docs.text:
Normalized capacity factor profiles for distributed generation.

Column Type Required Notes time_index integer Yes Hour index within the source profile region string Yes Base region or unaggregated model region weather_year integer Yes Meteorological year for the profile value float Yes Capacity factor (0–1)

When regions are aggregated, provide component-region capacities and profiles. See Distributed Generation for interpolation and aggregation behavior.

docs.title: Output File Schemas
docs.text:
PowerGenome generates a folder of CSV files for each scenario/year case. These files conform to the GenX input format.

Macro output

When Macro output is enabled (see Output Formats), PowerGenome also writes a MacroEnergy.jl simpleCSVinputs case alongside the GenX files. This page documents the GenX layout; the Macro layout and its GenX-to-Macro mapping are described in the Output File Format explanation.

v6 vs legacy format

The default is the split v6 layout. Set old_genx_format: true for the legacy layout, which puts Generators_data.csv and Load_data.csv directly in the period folder.

results/<case_id>/Inputs/Inputs_p<N>/
├── system/
│   ├── Demand_data.csv
│   ├── Fuels_data.csv
│   ├── Generators_variability.csv
│   ├── Network.csv
│   └── Operational_reserves.csv
├── resources/                               # One file per resource type
│   ├── Thermal.csv
│   ├── Vre.csv
│   ├── Storage.csv
│   ├── Must_run.csv
│   ├── Flex_demand.csv
│   ├── Hydro.csv
│   └── policy_assignments/
│       ├── Resource_energy_share_requirement.csv
│       ├── Resource_capacity_reserve_margin.csv
│       ├── Resource_minimum_capacity_requirement.csv
│       └── Resource_maximum_capacity_requirement.csv
└── policies/
    ├── Energy_share_requirement.csv
    ├── Capacity_reserve_margin.csv
    ├── CO2_cap.csv
    ├── Minimum_capacity_requirement.csv
    └── Maximum_capacity_requirement.csv

Without scenario definitions, the period folder is results/Inputs/Inputs_p<N>/. Files that are empty or correspond to disabled features are omitted.

docs.title: Settings Reference
docs.text:
This section documents all configuration parameters that control PowerGenome's behavior.

Settings are defined in YAML files. When given a directory, PowerGenome reads its immediate .yml files, not nested folders or .yaml files. Avoid defining the same top-level setting in multiple files: their iteration order is not guaranteed, and a later value replaces the entire earlier value.

docs.title: Organization
docs.text:
Settings are grouped by functional area:

  • Model Definition

    Core parameters defining planning years, currency conversion, and run scope.

    Parameters: model_periods, model_tag_names, etc.

  • Year-Keyed Values

    Advanced pattern for resolving parameter values automatically by planning year.

    Works across settings sections, including nested values and cost modifiers.

  • Regional Configuration

    Region definitions, aggregations, and base-to-model region mapping.

    Parameters: model_regions, region_aggregations, cogen_tech, etc.

  • Existing Generators

    Clustering parameters, technology groupings, cost overrides.

    Parameters: num_clusters, tech_groups, tech_fuel_map, etc.

  • New-Build Resources

    Technology costs, new resource definitions, regional availability, capacity limits.

    Parameters: new_resources, resource_modifiers, modified_new_resources, etc.

  • Fuels

    Fuel price sources, emission factors, regional price adjustments.

    Parameters: fuel_scenarios, fuel_price_table, fuel_emission_factors, tech_fuel_map, etc.

    Simplified Workflow

    PowerGenome now uses a simplified fuel workflow by default. Provide a complete fuel price table with all base regions instead of using legacy AEO mapping parameters.

  • Transmission

    Network topology, line limits, expansion costs, loss percentages.

    Parameters: transmission_constraints_table, tx_expansion_per_period, etc.

  • Demand

    Load profile sources, distributed generation, time weighting.

    Parameters: demand_table, distributed_capacity_table, etc.

  • Resource Tags

    GenX-specific tags controlling dispatch, storage, flexibility, must-run status.

    Parameters: regional_tag_values, model_tag_values, THERM, VRE, STOR, etc.

  • Data Tables

    Input data source configuration with filtering and scenario selection.

    Parameters: generation_table, demand_table, fuel_price_table, etc.

  • Scenario Management

    Multi-scenario execution, parameter swapping, case definitions.

    Parameters: scenario_definitions_fn, settings_management, input_folder, etc.

  • Output Formats

    Which model input format(s) to write (GenX and/or Macro simpleCSVinputs) and Macro model-run settings.

    Parameters: macro_output, genx_output, macro_discount_rate, etc.

docs.title: Basic Value Types
docs.text:
# Scalars
model_year: 2030
target_usd_year: 2023
old_genx_format: false

# Lists
model_regions: [CA_N, CA_S, AZ]
new_resources:
  - [NaturalGas, 1-on-1 Combined Cycle (H-Frame), Moderate, 500]
  - [UtilityPV, Class1, Moderate, 100]

# Dictionaries
region_aggregations:
  CA_N: [CA_IID, CA_LADWP, CA_BANC]
  CA_S: [CA_SCE, CA_SDGE]

docs.title: Table Configurations
docs.text:
Simple (just filename):

generation_table: "generators.csv"

Advanced (with filters):

demand_table:
  table_name: demand_timeseries.parquet
  scenario: HighEV
  filters:
    - - [region, '=', 'CA']
      - [year, '>=', 2030]
  columns: [time_index, weather_year, region, load_mw, year]

Filter logic uses DNF (Disjunctive Normal Form):

  • Inner lists are AND conditions
  • Outer list elements are OR'd together

Example: filters: [[[A, =, 1], [B, =, 2]], [[C, =, 3]]] → (A=1 AND B=2) OR (C=3)

docs.title: Multi-Level Dictionaries
docs.text:
Many settings use technology → parameter structure:

tech_groups:
  Combined Cycle:
    - Natural Gas Fired Combined Cycle
    - Natural Gas Steam Turbine
  Coal:
    - Conventional Steam Coal
    - Coal Integrated Gasification Combined Cycle

alt_num_clusters:
  CA_N:
    Conventional Steam Coal: 5
    Natural Gas Fired Combined Cycle: 10

Access pattern in code:

combined_cycle_techs = settings["tech_groups"]["Combined Cycle"]
clusters = settings["alt_num_clusters"]["CA_N"]["Conventional Steam Coal"]

docs.title: Regional Parameters
docs.text:
Regional settings can use model region names as keys:

regional_tag_values:
  CA_N:
    THERM:
      NaturalGas: 1
  AZ:
    THERM:
      NaturalGas: 2

# Legacy — only validated, not applied
new_gen_not_available:
  CA_N: [Coal_new]
  AZ: [OffshoreWind]

docs.title: Parameter Modifiers
docs.text:
Cost and technology modifiers use nested dictionaries:

resource_modifiers:
  solar_adjusted:
    technology: UtilityPV
    tech_detail: Class1
    capex_mw: [mul, 0.9]  # 10% cost reduction
    fixed_o_m_mw: [mul, 0.95]  # 5% O&M reduction

These apply changes to base technology costs using operators like mul, add, sub.

docs.title: Technology Matching
docs.text:
Matching depends on the setting. Resource tags use case-insensitive substring matching (ignoring underscores), whereas tech_groups requires exact input technology names:

model_tag_values:
  THERM:
    NaturalGas: 1

Region names are case-sensitive and must match exactly.

docs.title: Loading Mechanism
docs.text:
PowerGenome can load a settings folder or an individual YAML file:

from powergenome.settings import load_settings
from pathlib import Path

settings = load_settings(Path("my_study/settings"))
# Alternatively: load_settings(Path("my_study/settings.yml"))

Load Order:

  1. Immediate .yml files in the folder are read without a guaranteed order.
  2. Duplicate top-level keys replace previous values, including nested dictionaries.
  3. Keep each top-level setting in one file to avoid order-dependent results.

Example structure:

settings/
├── model_definition.yml
├── regions.yml
└── generators.yml

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
PowerGenome validates settings at runtime:

  • Missing required parameters: Raises KeyError
  • Type mismatches: May raise errors during execution
  • Invalid table names: Logged as warnings
  • Missing data files: Errors during DataManager initialization

Use .get(key, default) for optional parameters:

# Required (error if missing)
year = settings["model_year"]

# Optional (use default)
macro = settings.get("macro_output", False)

docs.title: Environment Variables (Deprecated)
docs.text:
Older versions used .env files for data paths:

# Legacy approach (still works but discouraged)
PUDL_DB=/path/to/pudl.sqlite
PG_DB=/path/to/powergenome.sqlite

Modern approach uses settings YAML:

data_location: /path/to/data_folder
RESOURCE_GROUP_PROFILES: /path/to/generation_profiles

docs.title: Override Priority
docs.text:
When the same parameter appears in multiple places:

Scenario-specific settings_management swaps update the loaded settings; code defaults apply where values are absent. Individual command-line options have their own precedence rules and do not generally override arbitrary settings.

docs.title: Data Tables Settings
docs.text: DataManager exposes configured CSV, Parquet, SQLite, and DuckDB sources under standard internal names. For a setup walkthrough, see Configure Data Tables. For column types, units, and coverage requirements, use Input Table Schemas.

docs.title: data_location
docs.text:
Type: path or list of paths. Required for the data pipeline.

A location can be a directory of CSV/Parquet files or a SQLite/DuckDB database:

data_location:
  - data
  - /shared/powergenome_data.duckdb
input_folder: extra_inputs

Relative data_location and input_folder paths resolve from the settings folder's parent directory, or a single settings file's directory. Configured tables are searched across these locations and input_folder. Every table must resolve in exactly one location; duplicate matches are rejected.

For flat files, include .csv or .parquet in the table setting. Extension auto-detection exists, but explicit filenames are clearer. For databases, name the table without a file extension. SQLite (.db, .sqlite) and DuckDB (.duckdb) sources are supported.

docs.title: Simple Configuration
docs.text:
generation_table: generators.parquet
demand_table: hourly_demand.csv

docs.title: Advanced Configuration
docs.text:
demand_table:
  table_name: hourly_demand.parquet
  scenario: high_ev
  filters:
    - - [year, 'in', [2030, 2040]]
      - [region, 'in', [p1, p2, p3, p4]]
Field Type Meaning table_name string, or list of strings Source filename or database table name. A list stacks several sources into one table; see below. scenario scalar Convenience equality filter on the source scenario column. filters nested lists Row predicates; see below. columns list of strings Source columns to expose. Omit to retain all columns.

docs.title: Combined Configuration
docs.text:
Any table setting also accepts a list of entries, each a filename or its own advanced configuration. The parts are stacked with UNION ALL BY NAME, so every part must have the same columns. This is how a study adds its own technology costs next to the ATB tables:

resource_cost_table:
  - technology_costs_atb_tx_3_zone.csv
  - table_name: custom_technology_costs.csv
    filters:
      - - [scenario, '=', high_nuclear]
resource_heat_rate_table:
  - technology_heat_rates_nrelatb.csv
  - custom_technology_heat_rates.csv

Parts load in list order, and each part is resolved separately, so they may live in different data_location entries. An empty list is treated like an unset setting.

These examples configure table access, not a complete runnable study. Source columns must match downstream schemas; DataManager does not rename them to repair an incompatible dataset.

docs.title: Shared Configuration Across Parts
docs.text:
When every part shares filters, columns, or scenario, write those keys once and give table_name as a list instead of repeating a configuration per file:

demand_table:
  table_name:
    - demand_west.parquet
    - demand_east.parquet
  scenario: high_ev
  filters:
    - - [year, '>=', 2030]

This is the same combined table as the list form: each source becomes a part, and the shared keys are applied to every part, so scenario: high_ev filters both files. Use the list form when parts need different filters or columns — entries in a table_name list must be plain filenames or table names, and an empty table_name list raises an error rather than silently skipping the table.

docs.title: Filter Syntax
docs.text:
Filters are an OR of AND groups (disjunctive normal form):

filters:
  - - [year, '=', 2030]
    - [region, '=', p1]  # Both conditions must match.
  - - [year, '=', 2040]
    - [region, '=', p2]  # Or both conditions in this group.

Each condition is [column, operator, value]. Supported operators: =, ==, !=, >, >=, <, <=, in, and not in. Membership operators require a list value. Match value types to source types; quote operators.

docs.title: Scenario Convenience Filter
docs.text: scenario: high_ev adds scenario = high_ev to each AND group that has no existing condition on scenario. A group already containing a scenario condition keeps that condition rather than receiving another one. With no explicit filters, the convenience setting creates the scenario filter itself. The source must have a scenario column.

docs.title: Column Selection
docs.text: columns limits the exposed source columns. Retain all fields required by processing, custom modifiers, and output generation—not just fields displayed in a short schema example. An incomplete projection can load successfully and fail later. Omit columns unless the workflow's requirements are known.

docs.title: Multi-period and scenario use
docs.text:
Use year-keyed values or scenario swaps when a source configuration genuinely must differ by period or case. Retain coverage for every requested planning year when sharing a multi-year demand or cost source.

For myopic multi-period models, use the same generation source across periods to preserve cluster membership. Do not filter units out by retirement year: blank retirement_year means no planned retirement, but ordinary comparison filters exclude blank values.

docs.title: Standard Table Mappings
docs.text:
Every setting below accepts a single configuration or a list of them.

Setting Internal name Contents generation_table generation Existing generator units. plant_region_table plant_region Plant-to-base-region assignments. resource_heat_rate_table resource_heat_rate New-resource heat rates. resource_cost_table resource_cost New-resource capital and operating costs. operational_constraints_table operational_constraints Technology operating parameters. transmission_constraints_table transmission_constraints Base-region transmission capacities. transmission_cost_table transmission_cost Inter-regional costs and losses. fuel_price_table fuel_price Fuel prices by scenario, region, year, and data vintage. dollar_year_table dollar_year CPI values for dollar-year conversion. regional_cost_factor_table regional_cost_factor Regional construction multipliers. demand_table demand Hourly demand. supplemental_demand_table supplemental_demand Additional demand profiles. emission_policies_table emission_policies Regional policy requirements. demand_segments_table demand_segments Demand segmentation and unserved-energy costs. distributed_capacity_table distributed_capacity Distributed capacity by model region and year. distributed_profiles_table distributed_profiles Distributed generation profiles.

distributed_profile_table is also accepted for distributed_profiles. Legacy emission_policies_fn and demand_segments_fn alias their corresponding *_table keys; the modern key takes precedence when both are supplied.

See Input Table Schemas for all table fields. In particular, fuel prices require data_year even for a single vintage; regional coverage and cost-year coverage matter beyond merely loading a table.

docs.title: Renewable Resource Tables
docs.text: Renewable resource groups use JSON definitions and referenced metadata/profile files rather than additional standard table settings. See Configure Renewable Clusters for their schemas and configuration.

docs.title: RESOURCE_GROUPS
docs.text:
Type: directory path or list of directory paths.

All .json group definitions are discovered recursively under these folders. Unlike data_location, relative paths resolve from the process working directory.

RESOURCE_GROUPS: example_systems/TX-3-zone/resource_groups

This is the published Texas example's path when running from the examples root, as in Getting Started. Use your own group directory for another study.

docs.title: RESOURCE_GROUP_PROFILES
docs.text:
Type: directory path or list of directory paths; optional override.

Profile filenames come from the group definitions; they are not required to follow a particular naming pattern. When directories are listed, profile lookup searches them in order, then the environment-variable location if set, before falling back to the group JSON's folder. Relative paths resolve from the working directory. Tidy profiles contain site_id, time_index, value, and optionally weather_year; weather-year selection requires tidy profiles.

docs.title: Other input files
docs.text: Not every file setting is a DataManager table. For example, capacity_limit_spur_fn names a legacy capacity-limit/spur CSV under input_folder. See New-build settings for that workflow and the preferred direct interconnect_capex_mw setting.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• Missing table: verify the setting key, filename/database table, and locations.
  • Missing column: check the canonical schema and remove incomplete projections.
  • Unexpected rows: check AND/OR nesting, scenario conditions, and value types.
  • Incomplete period coverage: inspect the resolved case settings and source years; a successful load does not prove every period has data.

Run validation after changing sources, then inspect the generated outputs and warnings.

docs.title: Demand Settings
docs.text: These parameters control electricity demand data sources for the model.

docs.title: demand_table
docs.text:
Type: String or dictionary Required: Yes Example: See below

Table containing hourly electricity demand projections for all model regions and planning periods.

Simple:

demand_table: load_curves.csv

Advanced (with scenario selection):

demand_table:
  table_name: demand_timeseries.parquet
  scenario: high_electrification

Required columns:

  • region: Base region name, or a model region that is not aggregated
  • time_index: Hour index
  • load_mw: Demand in MW
  • year: Planning year

Optional columns:

  • scenario: Demand scenario identifier (reference, high_ev, high_electrification, etc.)
  • weather_year: Weather data vintage year

Format: Tidy/long format with one row per region-time-year observation.

Example demand CSV:

time_index,weather_year,region,load_mw,year,scenario
1,2012,CA_N,15234.5,2030,reference
2,2012,CA_N,14123.2,2030,reference
3,2012,CA_N,13890.4,2030,reference
1,2012,CA_S,12450.8,2030,reference
...
1,2012,CA_N,16890.2,2040,reference
2,2012,CA_N,15678.9,2040,reference
...

Multi-Period Coverage

The demand_table should contain hourly demand projections for all future modeling periods. For example, if your model runs from 2030 to 2050 in 5-year increments, the table should include demand data for 2030, 2035, 2040, 2045, and 2050.

docs.title: Demand Scenarios
docs.text:
Use the scenario column to manage different demand futures:

demand_table:
  table_name: demand_projections.parquet
  scenario: high_electrification  # Options: reference, high_ev, high_electrification

Common scenarios:

  • reference: Base case load growth
  • high_ev: Increased electric vehicle adoption
  • high_electrification: Widespread building/industrial electrification
  • low_growth: Slower demand growth with efficiency improvements

docs.title: supplemental_demand_table
docs.text:
Type: String or dictionary Required: No Example: See below

Optional table of additional hourly demand (e.g. data-center forecasts, new industrial loads) to add on top of the baseline demand profiles.

How it is applied: Supplemental demand is joined into the base load data stage inside make_load_curves — in long format, one row per (region × hour), before per-weather-year hours are renumbered to 1..N and before base regions are aggregated into model regions. Rows sharing the same (region, weather_year, time_index) are summed with the base load, so no block-tiling is used and weather years of unequal length (e.g. an 8 784-hour leap year next to a normal 8 760-hour year) are handled correctly. A weather_year: all row expands to one copy for each weather year actually present in the load data, rather than tiling a fixed block size.

Simple (file in data_location folder, or co-located with a database):

supplemental_demand_table: supplemental_demand.csv

Advanced (with scenario selection):

supplemental_demand_table:
  table_name: supplemental_demand.csv
  scenario: high_data_center

Required columns:

  • region: Base region or model region name. Base region names are mapped to the aggregated model region that contains them (per region_aggregations); model region names are used as-is. Names matching neither a known base region nor a model region are logged as a warning and ignored.
  • time_index: Integer hour index (1-based) or the strings all / all_hours
  • load_mw: MW of demand to add

Optional columns:

  • year: When present, rows are filtered to the current model_year
  • scenario: Scenario identifier; when present, exactly one scenario must remain after loading. If multiple scenarios are found and none has been selected, PowerGenome raises a descriptive error listing the available scenario names and showing how to select one (see below).
  • weather_year: When present, controls which weather-year the row applies to: all applies the row to every weather year present in the load data, a specific value (e.g. 2012) applies it only to that weather year, and a blank value causes the row to be skipped. There is no fixed block size: an all row expands to one copy for each weather year actually present, and weather years of different lengths are supported. When the load data spans multiple weather years (its weather years are known via the weather_year setting), every weather year must be covered by either a specific-value row or an all row; a missing weather year raises an error naming the uncovered years. A specific weather_year that does not match any weather year in the load data raises a descriptive error telling you to set the weather_year setting. No coverage check is performed when this column is absent.

time_index values:

  • all / all_hours – adds the demand increment to every hour of the weather year(s) selected by weather_year (flat load addition). For each selected weather year, one copy is added per hour actually present in that weather year.
  • Integer – adds the demand increment only to the hour with that index; with weather_year set to all, it is applied to that hour in every weather year.

Scenario handling:

If the supplemental demand file contains multiple scenarios and no scenario is specified, PowerGenome raises:

ValueError: The supplemental_demand table contains multiple scenarios
('baseline', 'high_data_center') but no scenario has been selected.
Specify which scenario to use in your settings file, for example:

    supplemental_demand_table:
      table_name: supplemental_demand.csv
      scenario: baseline

File co-located with a database:

When data_location points to a database file (.db, .duckdb), a filename with a .csv or .parquet extension is resolved relative to the database's parent directory:

data_location: /data/pg_data.db
supplemental_demand_table: supplemental_demand.csv  # → /data/supplemental_demand.csv

Example supplemental demand CSV:

region,time_index,load_mw,year,scenario
WEST,all_hours,500,2030,base_data_center
WEST,all_hours,800,2035,base_data_center
EAST,all_hours,200,2030,base_data_center
EAST,1,300,2030,base_data_center
WEST,all_hours,1000,2030,high_data_center
WEST,all_hours,1500,2035,high_data_center
EAST,all_hours,400,2030,high_data_center

For a step-by-step guide see Add Supplemental Hourly Demand.

docs.title: Existing Generators Settings
docs.text: These parameters control how existing power plants are processed, clustered, and configured for the model.

docs.title: num_clusters
docs.text:
Type: Dictionary (technology → number or null) Required: Yes Example: See below

Default number of clusters per technology in each region. Use alt_num_clusters for regional overrides. Technologies omitted from both mappings are excluded.

Global defaults (per technology, across regions):

num_clusters:
  Conventional Steam Coal: 3
  Nuclear: 1
  Natural Gas Fired Combined Cycle: ~ # Does not cluster plants

Regional (different per region):

alt_num_clusters:
  CA_N:
    Conventional Steam Coal: 5
    Natural Gas Fired Combined Cycle: 10
    Onshore Wind Turbine: 3
  CA_S:
    Natural Gas Fired Combined Cycle: 8

How it works:

  • K-means clustering, by default on heat rate and fixed O&M
  • Each cluster represents a group of similar generators
  • Reduces thousands of plants to manageable number of resources
  • "None" (~) skips clustering and returns individual generators

Practical guidance (ReEDS/IPM-scale regions)

  • Start with one cluster per technology in small regions
  • Use alt_num_clusters to split very large or heterogeneous fleets (e.g., >3–4 GW of combustion turbines with a wide heat-rate IQR)
  • The generated thermal inputs include heat rate inter-quartile range and standard deviation columns. Check those to decide where an extra cluster is warranted.

docs.title: alt_num_clusters
docs.text:
Type: Dictionary (region → technology → number) Required: No Example: See below

Overrides num_clusters for specific region/technology combinations.

num_clusters:
  Nuclear: 2  # Default

alt_num_clusters:
  CA_N:
    Nuclear: 1  # Each nuclear plant is unique
    Biomass: 2  # Only 2 biomass clusters needed

This allows fine-grained control without repeating all technologies in the main num_clusters parameter.

docs.title: generator_cluster_columns
docs.text:
Type: List of strings Required: No Default: ["heat_rate_mmbtu_mwh", "fom_per_mwyr"] Example: See below

Columns (features) used for k-means clustering. By default, generators are clustered based on heat rate and fixed O&M costs.

Default behavior (uses heat rate and fixed O&M implicitly):

generator_cluster_columns:
  - heat_rate_mmbtu_mwh
  - fom_per_mwyr

Custom features:

generator_cluster_columns:
  - heat_rate_mmbtu_mwh
  - capacity_mw
  - operating_year

Use cases:

  • Add capacity_mw to keep large/small plants separate
  • Add operating_year to segregate old vs. new plants
  • Add minimum_load_mw for minimum load constraints
  • Use only heat_rate_mmbtu_mwh for thermal efficiency clustering

Available columns depend on your generation data schema. Common options:

  • heat_rate_mmbtu_mwh: Thermal efficiency
  • capacity_mw: Plant size
  • fom_per_mwyr: Fixed O&M costs
  • vom_per_mwh: Variable O&M costs
  • operating_year: Plant age proxy
  • minimum_load_mw: Minimum stable operation level

Clustering Quality

Clustering features should be normalized or on similar scales for best results. PowerGenome uses the scikit-learn StandardScaler() method to normalize features.

docs.title: existing_resource_profile_fallback_max_demand_fraction
docs.text:
Type: Number in [0, 1] (not a boolean) Required: No Default: 0.005

Maximum combined operating existing-generator capacity with missing availability profiles in each model region, as a fraction of that region's mean hourly demand before distributed-generation subtraction. Demand uses the scenario's planning and weather years, regional aggregation, and supplemental/flexible demand additions, before rounding. Multiple weather years are weighted by their number of modeled hours.

existing_resource_profile_fallback_max_demand_fraction: 0.005  # 0.5% of mean demand
# Use 0 to forbid fallback for any positive operating capacity.

At or below this limit, PowerGenome warns, preserves the affected generators and capacity, and assigns availability 1.0 in every modeled hour. Above it, PowerGenome stops with affected resources, reasons, demand, and allowed MW in the error. Missing or invalid demand cannot authorize positive-capacity fallback, including with --no-load (demand is loaded lazily when needed).

The limit combines all affected clusters and technologies, including hydro, wind, and solar; it is not a separate allowance for each technology. Absent resource groups, absent regional metadata, missing sites, and empty/incomplete hourly coverage enter the same check. Partial coverage charges the whole failing cluster, using its actual existing capacity, not resource-group metadata capacity. Retired/zero operating capacity consumes no budget. Explicitly profile-free groups (group.profiles is None) and unsupported dispatchable technologies remain exempt. New-build behavior is unchanged. Malformed inputs, ambiguous group matches, and unavailable weather years remain errors.

This is a modeling approximation, not a reliability guarantee: constant availability can overstate generation. Fix coverage rather than increasing the tolerance by default.

docs.title: tech_groups
docs.text:
Type: Dictionary (group name → list of technologies) Required: No Example: See below

Combines multiple similar technologies into a single group before clustering. Useful for technologies that are functionally equivalent.

tech_groups:
  Peaker:
    - Natural Gas Fired Combustion Turbine
    - Natural Gas Steam Turbine
  Biomass:
    - Biomass
    - Municipal Solid Waste
    - Landfill Gas

Benefits:

  • Reduces cluster count for minor technology variations
  • Groups functionally similar resources
  • Simplifies output analysis

Matching: Group members must match the input technology names exactly.

docs.title: resource_attr_modifiers
docs.text:
Type: Dictionary (technology → list of modifier dictionaries) Required: No Example: See below

Apply custom formulas to modify generator attributes based on other data fields. Useful for age-based cost adjustments, regional scaling, or custom business logic.

resource_attr_modifiers:
  conventional steam coal:
    - attribute: fom_per_mwyr
      formula:
        op: add
        rate: 126  # $/MW-yr per year of age
        multiplier: age

Structure:

Each technology can have multiple modifiers. Each modifier requires:

  • attribute: Column name to modify (e.g., fom_per_mwyr, heat_rate_mmbtu_mwh)
  • formula: Dictionary with operation details
  • op: Operation type (add, mul, sub, truediv, or replace)
  • rate: Numeric rate/coefficient
  • multiplier: Column name containing values to multiply by rate

Operations:

Operation Formula Example add new = old + (rate × multiplier) Add age-based O&M mul new = old × (rate × multiplier) Scale by efficiency sub new = old - (rate × multiplier) Reduce value truediv new = old / (rate × multiplier) Divide value replace new = rate × multiplier Ignore old value

Example for another technology:

resource_attr_modifiers:
  natural gas fired combined cycle:
    - attribute: fom_per_mwyr
      formula:
        op: add
        rate: 75
        multiplier: age

Multiple technologies:

resource_attr_modifiers:
  conventional steam coal:
    - attribute: fom_per_mwyr
      formula:
        op: add
        rate: 126
        multiplier: age
  nuclear:
    - attribute: fom_per_mwyr
      formula:
        op: add
        rate: 200
        multiplier: age

Technology matching: Case-insensitive substring matching (e.g., "coal" matches "Conventional Steam Coal").

Common attributes:

  • fom_per_mwyr: Fixed O&M cost ($/MW-yr)
  • vom_per_mwh: Variable O&M cost ($/MWh)
  • heat_rate_mmbtu_mwh: Heat rate (MMBtu/MWh)
  • capex_mw: Capital cost ($/MW)
  • minimum_load_mw: Minimum load (MW)
  • ramp_rate_mw_per_min: Ramp rate (MW/min)

Common multipliers:

  • age: Plant age in years
  • capacity_mw: Nameplate capacity
  • operating_year: Year plant started operation

Column Requirements

Both attribute and multiplier columns must exist in the generator dataframe. Missing columns raise KeyError.

Execution Order

Applied to individual generator rows before grouping and clustering, after the age column is calculated.

See Modify Generator Attributes How-To Guide for detailed examples and validation.

docs.title: generation_table
docs.text:
Type: String or dictionary Required: Yes Example: See below

Source of existing generator data. Can be a simple filename or advanced configuration with filters.

Simple:

generation_table: generators_2030.csv

Advanced:

generation_table:
  table_name: generators.parquet
  filters:
    - - [operating_year, '<=', 2030]

See Data Tables for full filter syntax. Filtering directly on retirement_year can discard units with no planned retirement. Let PowerGenome apply its period-specific retirement logic instead.

docs.title: plant_region_table
docs.text:
Type: String or dictionary Required: Yes Example: "plant_regions.csv"

Mapping of plants to base regions.

plant_region_table: plant_region_map.csv

Expected columns:

  • plant_id: Plant identifier
  • region: Region name (matching model_regions)

docs.title: Example Configuration
docs.text:
Complete existing generator settings for a regional model:

# Clustering
num_clusters:
  Conventional Steam Coal: 3
  Nuclear: 2
  Hydroelectric Pumped Storage: 2
  Peaker: 1

alt_num_clusters:
  CA_N:
    Nuclear: 1
    Hydroelectric Pumped Storage: 1
  CA_S:
    Nuclear: 1

# Technology grouping
tech_groups:
  Peaker:
    - Natural Gas Fired Combustion Turbine
    - Natural Gas Steam Turbine

# Data source
generation_table:
  table_name: generators.parquet
  filters:
    - - [operating_year, '<=', 2030]
