docs.title: Fuel Settings
docs.text: These parameters control fuel price sources, emission factors, and regional fuel price mappings.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
PowerGenome supports two fuel pricing workflows:

  1. Simplified (Recommended): Provide a fuel price table with prices for all model regions and fuels. PowerGenome automatically constructs fuel names and calculates aggregated region prices.

  2. Legacy (Larger fuel regions): Use raw AEO data with mapping parameters to create regional fuel prices.

Most users should use the simplified workflow with a complete fuel price table containing all base regions.

docs.title: Required Settings
docs.text:
These settings select a supplied fuel table and map fuels to generators:

# Assign scenario names to fuels
fuel_scenarios:
  coal: reference
  naturalgas: reference
  uranium: reference

# Map technologies to fuels
tech_fuel_map:
  Conventional Steam Coal: coal
  Natural Gas Fired Combined Cycle: naturalgas
  Nuclear: uranium

# Point to your fuel price table
fuel_price_table: fuel_prices.csv
fuel_data_year: 2025

You can select different scenarios for different fuels if those scenarios are present in the table.

docs.title: Fuel Price Table Format
docs.text:
Your fuel price table must include prices for every base region in your model:

Required columns:

  • fuel: Fuel name (coal, naturalgas, distillate, uranium, etc.)
  • region: Base region name (must match regions in your model)
  • year: Calendar year
  • price: Price ($/MMBtu)
  • scenario: Scenario identifier matching fuel_scenarios
  • data_year: Data vintage year (include even for one vintage)

Optional columns:

  • dollar_year: Price year (for inflation adjustment)

Example fuel_prices.csv:

fuel,region,year,price,scenario,data_year,dollar_year
coal,CA_N,2030,2.5,reference,2025,2024
coal,CA_S,2030,2.6,reference,2025,2024
naturalgas,CA_N,2030,4.2,reference,2025,2024
naturalgas,CA_S,2030,4.3,reference,2025,2024
uranium,CA_N,2030,0.8,reference,2025,2024
uranium,CA_S,2030,0.8,reference,2025,2024

Important: The table must contain prices for all base regions (e.g., CA_N, CA_S). PowerGenome will automatically average base region prices to create prices for aggregated regions defined in region_aggregations.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
PowerGenome automatically:

  1. Constructs full fuel names as {region}_{scenario}_{fuel} (e.g., CA_N_reference_coal)
  2. Averages prices for aggregated regions (e.g., if CA = [CA_N, CA_S], then CA prices = average of CA_N and CA_S)
  3. Assigns fuels to generators using tech_fuel_map

No mapping parameters (fuel_series_* or fuel_region_map) are needed.

docs.title: Legacy Workflow (AEO Direct)
docs.text: If you're working directly with EIA AEO data, you'll need additional mapping parameters.

docs.title: fuel_scenarios
docs.text:
Type: Dictionary (fuel → scenario name) Required: Yes Example: See below

Maps fuels to price scenario names.

fuel_scenarios:
  coal: reference
  naturalgas: reference
  uranium: reference
  distillate: high_resource

Scenario names must match keys in fuel_series_scenario_names (legacy workflow) or the scenario column in your fuel price table (simplified workflow).

docs.title: fuel_data_year
docs.text:
Type: Integer Required: Only if your fuel price table has multiple data years Example: 2025

Specifies which data year to use if your fuel price table contains multiple vintages.

fuel_data_year: 2025

Selects the vintage when the table contains multiple data_year values. Include the column even for a single vintage; without fuel_data_year, the loader checks the number of unique values in that column.

docs.title: Legacy Mapping Parameters (Optional)
docs.text:
Legacy Parameters

The parameters below are only needed for the legacy AEO direct workflow. If your fuel price table already contains prices for all base regions with the fuel/scenario names you want, skip this entire section.

These parameters map region, fuel, and scenario codes in a supplied fuel price table.

docs.title: fuel_series_scenario_names
docs.text:
Type: Dictionary (user scenario → AEO scenario code) Required: No (legacy workflow only) Example: See below

Maps user-friendly scenario names to official EIA AEO scenario codes.

fuel_series_scenario_names:
  reference: REF2025
  no_111d: NOCAA111
  low_price: LOWPRICE
  high_price: HIGHPRICE
  high_resource: HIGHOGS
  low_resource: LOWOGS

AEO scenario codes change with each AEO release. Check EIA OpenData for current codes.

docs.title: fuel_series_names
docs.text:
Type: Dictionary (fuel name → AEO fuel code) Required: No (legacy workflow only) Example: See below

Maps fuel names to EIA AEO fuel codes.

fuel_series_names:
  coal: STC  # Steam coal
  naturalgas: NG
  distillate: DFO
  uranium: U

docs.title: fuel_series_region_names
docs.text:
Type: Dictionary (region name → AEO region code) Required: No (legacy workflow only) Example: See below

Maps region names to EIA AEO region codes.

fuel_series_region_names:
  mountain: MTN
  pacific: PCF
  west_south_central: WSC

docs.title: fuel_region_map
docs.text:
Type: Dictionary (AEO region → list of model regions) Required: No (legacy workflow only) Example: See below

Maps EIA AEO fuel price regions to model regions. Only used in legacy workflow to create modified copies of base region prices.

fuel_region_map:
  pacific: [CA_N, CA_S]
  mountain: [AZ, NM]
  west_south_central: [TX_N]

Simplified Workflow Alternative

In the simplified workflow, you don't need fuel_region_map. Instead, provide prices for all base regions directly in your fuel price table. PowerGenome will automatically average base region prices for aggregated regions.

AEO fuel regions (common names):

  • pacific: Pacific
  • mountain: Mountain
  • west_south_central: West South Central
  • east_north_central: East North Central
  • west_north_central: West North Central
  • new_england: New England
  • middle_atlantic: Middle Atlantic
  • south_atlantic: South Atlantic
  • east_south_central: East South Central

See EIA documentation for complete region definitions.

docs.title: fuel_emission_factors
docs.text:
Type: Dictionary (fuel → number) Required: For emissions modeling Example: See below

CO₂ emission factors by fuel type (tonnes CO₂ per MMBtu).

fuel_emission_factors:
  coal: 0.09552
  naturalgas: 0.05306
  distillate: 0.07315
  uranium: 0.0
  biomass: 0.0

Values are based on fuel carbon content and combustion chemistry.

Common factors (tonnes CO₂/MMBtu):

  • Bituminous coal: 0.0955
  • Sub-bituminous coal: 0.0972
  • Natural gas: 0.0531
  • Diesel: 0.0732
  • Biomass: 0.0 (policy-dependent)

docs.title: fuel_price_table
docs.text:
Type: String or dictionary Required: For custom fuel prices Example: See below

Custom fuel price time series (alternative to AEO).

Simple:

fuel_price_table: fuel_prices.csv
fuel_data_year: 2025

Advanced:

fuel_price_table:
  table_name: fuel_prices.parquet
  scenario: high_gas
  filters:
    - - [year, '>=', 2025]

Expected columns:

  • fuel: Fuel name (coal, naturalgas, etc.)
  • region: Region name
  • year: Calendar year
  • price: Price ($/MMBtu)

docs.title: user_fuel_price
docs.text:
Type: Dictionary (fuel → price or region → price) Required: No Example: See below

Supply prices for user-defined fuels. Values can be scalar across regions or specified by model region; use fuels not already assigned in fuel_scenarios.

user_fuel_price:
  hydrogen: 16.0  # $/MMBtu in every region
  biomass:
    CA_N: 5.0
    CA_S: 6.0

Use year-keyed values or scenario management for prices that change by planning period. user_fuel_usd_year optionally maps fuel names to the dollar year of each user-supplied price.

docs.title: tech_fuel_map
docs.text:
Type: Dictionary (technology → fuel) Required: For assigning fuels to generators Example: See below

Maps technology-name substrings to fuels in fuel_scenarios or user_fuel_price. Matching is case-insensitive.

tech_fuel_map:
  NaturalGas: naturalgas
  Conventional Steam Coal: coal
  Nuclear: uranium
  Biomass: biomass

docs.title: regional_fuel_adjustments
docs.text:
Type: Dictionary (region → fuel → value or modifier) Required: No Example: See below

Regional price adjustments, either relative to base prices or as a relacement value.

regional_fuel_adjustments:
  CA_N:
    naturalgas: [add, 1.5]  # Add $1.5/mmbtu to gas prices in CA_N
  CA_S: [mul, 0.9] # Multiply all fuel costs in CA_S by 0.9
  AZ:
    coal: 2.0  # $2/mmbtu fuel cost in AZ (dollar year must match target_usd_year)

Accounts for regional market conditions, transportation costs, or local policies.

docs.title: carbon_tax
docs.text:
Type: Float or dictionary (year → $/tonne) Required: No Example: See below

Carbon price ($/tonne CO₂) added to fuel costs.

Single value:

carbon_tax: 50  # $/tonne CO₂

Carbon costs are calculated as:

carbon_cost_per_mmbtu = carbon_tax * fuel_emission_factors[fuel]

docs.title: Simplified Workflow Example
docs.text:
Complete fuel pricing with custom fuel price table:

# Fuel price table location
fuel_price_table: fuel_prices.csv

# Map scenario names to fuels
fuel_scenarios:
  coal: reference
  naturalgas: reference
  uranium: reference

# Map technologies to fuels
tech_fuel_map:
  Conventional Steam Coal: coal
  Natural Gas Fired Combined Cycle: naturalgas
  Natural Gas Fired Combustion Turbine: naturalgas
  Nuclear: uranium

# Emission factors (tonnes CO2 per MMBtu)
fuel_emission_factors:
  coal: 0.09552
  naturalgas: 0.05306
  distillate: 0.07315
  uranium: 0.0

# CCS fuel mapping
ccs_fuel_map:
  NaturalGas_CCS90: naturalgas_ccs90
  Coal_CCS90: coal_ccs90

ccs_capture_rate:
  naturalgas_ccs90: 0.9
  coal_ccs90: 0.9

ccs_disposal_cost: 10  # $/tonne CO2

Your fuel_prices.csv must contain all base regions:

fuel,region,year,price,scenario,data_year,dollar_year
coal,CA_N,2030,2.5,reference,2025,2024
coal,CA_S,2030,2.6,reference,2025,2024
coal,AZ,2030,2.4,reference,2025,2024
naturalgas,CA_N,2030,4.2,reference,2025,2024
naturalgas,CA_S,2030,4.3,reference,2025,2024
naturalgas,AZ,2030,3.8,reference,2025,2024
uranium,CA_N,2030,0.8,reference,2025,2024
uranium,CA_S,2030,0.8,reference,2025,2024
uranium,AZ,2030,0.8,reference,2025,2024

docs.title: Legacy Workflow Example (AEO Direct)
docs.text:
If using EIA AEO data directly:

# AEO fuel prices
fuel_data_year: 2025

fuel_series_scenario_names:
  reference: REF2025
  high_resource: HIGHOGS
  low_price: LOWPRICE

fuel_series_names:
  coal: STC
  naturalgas: NG
  distillate: DFO
  uranium: U

fuel_series_region_names:
  pacific: PCF
  mountain: MTN

fuel_scenarios:
  coal: reference
  naturalgas: reference
  uranium: reference
  distillate: high_resource

fuel_region_map:
  pacific: [CA_N, CA_S]
  mountain: [AZ, NM]

# Emission factors
fuel_emission_factors:
  coal: 0.09552
  naturalgas: 0.05306
  distillate: 0.07315
  uranium: 0.0
  biomass: 0.0

# Regional adjustments
regional_fuel_adjustments:
  CA_N:
    naturalgas: [mul, 1.2]
  CA_S:
    naturalgas: [mul, 1.2]

# Carbon pricing
carbon_tax:
  2030: 50
  2040: 75
  2050: 100

docs.title: Data Sources
docs.text: Prepare an AEO-derived table separately, then configure it with fuel_price_table.

docs.title: Custom Data Tables
docs.text:
Alternative to AEO, provide complete fuel price time series:

fuel_prices.csv:

fuel,region,year,price,scenario,data_year,dollar_year
naturalgas,CA_N,2030,4.5,reference,2025,2024
naturalgas,CA_S,2030,4.7,reference,2025,2024
naturalgas,CA_N,2040,5.2,reference,2025,2024
naturalgas,CA_S,2040,5.4,reference,2025,2024

Configure:

fuel_price_table: fuel_prices.csv
fuel_data_year: 2025

docs.title: Fuel Cost Calculation
docs.text:
Final fuel cost per MMBtu:

total_fuel_cost = base_price
                  × regional_adjustment
                  + (carbon_tax × emission_factor)

Example (natural gas in CA_N, 2030):

base_price = 4.00 $/MMBtu (from AEO)
regional_adjustment = 1.2
carbon_tax = 100 $/tonne
emission_factor = 0.05306 tonnes/MMBtu

total_cost = 4.00 × 1.2 + (100 × 0.05306)
          = 4.80 + 5.31
          = 10.11 $/MMBtu

This cost is combined with heat rates to calculate fuel costs per MWh for each generator.

docs.title: Macro Output Settings
docs.text:
PowerGenome can write model-case inputs for two capacity expansion models: GenX (the default) and MacroEnergy.jl (Macro), in Macro's simpleCSVinputs format. This page documents the settings that control which format(s) are written.

GenX is written by default. Enabling Macro output adds the Macro simpleCSVinputs files in addition to (not instead of) the GenX inputs, so a single run_powergenome call can produce both formats at once. Writing both formats in one run reuses all the intermediate data processing, which is faster than running PowerGenome once per model. To write only Macro inputs, disable GenX (see genx_output).

The same options are available as command-line flags to run_powergenome: --macro, --genx, and --no-genx. Flags and settings values are combined per format (either one enables that format). CLI flag names and the macro_output/genx_output values are case-insensitive (--Macro, "TRUE", etc.). Use actual YAML booleans (true/false) for the other Macro boolean settings; quoted strings are not parsed as booleans there.

docs.title: macro_output
docs.text:
Type: bool Default: false CLI equivalent: --macro

When true, write a Macro simpleCSVinputs case (only the simpleCSV inputs format — not the Macro JSON format) at the results root, or under its case-ID folder when using scenario definitions, matching the structure of the Macro examples (e.g. macroenergy/MacroEnergyExamples.jl/examples/multisector_3zone_simpleCSVinputs). The semantic mapping of generators, transmission, demand, fuel supply, and CO2 caps follows the GenX-to-Macro converter (EmilDimanchev/GenX_to_Macro; multistage runs follow the lb/multistage branch). Thermal CCS resources are supported; broader cross-sector hydrogen and liquid-fuel assets are not emitted.

GenX output is not disabled by this setting — see genx_output.

docs.title: genx_output
docs.text:
Type: bool Default: true CLI equivalents: --genx (enable), --no-genx (disable)

Controls whether PowerGenome writes the standard GenX Inputs/Inputs_pN files. GenX is the default output format, so this key is only needed to turn GenX off (for example, to write Macro inputs only) or to state it explicitly.

  • genx_output: false with macro_output: true → Macro inputs only.
  • genx_output: true with macro_output: true → both formats in one run.
  • --genx forces GenX output on, and --no-genx forces it off — each flag overrides the settings value. Because --no-genx is a hard override, run_powergenome --macro --no-genx writes Macro inputs only without editing any settings file.
# Macro inputs only (settings-file approach)
macro_output: true
genx_output: false

docs.title: Macro model-run settings
docs.text:
The following settings configure the Macro output beyond format selection. They are respected only when Macro output is enabled; existing behavior is unchanged when these keys are absent.

Setting Type Default Writes to Description macro_discount_rate float 0.045 settings/case_settings.json Annual discount rate applied across stages. macro_solution_algorithm str "Monolithic" settings/case_settings.json Solution algorithm for Macro. macro_period_lengths list[int] derived settings/case_settings.json PeriodLengths, one entry per stage. Derived from PowerGenome's planning-period definitions (model_periods, or the paired model_first_planning_year/model_year); an explicit value overrides the derived one. macro_constraint_scaling bool true settings/macro_settings.json Scale constraints for solver numerics. macro_write_subcommodities bool true settings/macro_settings.json Write sub-commodity accounting rows. macro_auto_create_nodes bool false settings/macro_settings.json Let Macro automatically create missing nodes. macro_auto_create_locations bool true settings/macro_settings.json Let Macro automatically create missing locations. macro_default_max_nsd float 1.0 NSD fallback Default non-served-demand quantity when no demand_segments_voll.csv is provided. macro_default_voll float 10000 NSD fallback Default value of lost load ($/MWh) when no demand_segments_voll.csv is provided. macro_default_fuel_price float 0.0 fuel price fallback Fallback fuel price when a fuel is missing from the fuel price table.

See Output File Format for the resulting Macro simpleCSVinputs folder layout, and the CLI Reference for the command-line flags.

docs.title: Model Definition Settings
docs.text: These core parameters define the overall model scope, planning periods, and currency adjustments.

docs.title: model_periods
docs.text:
Type: List of 2-element lists [[first_year, last_year], ...] Required: Yes, unless using model_year and model_first_planning_year

Defines planning periods as pairs of [first_year, last_year]. The last year is used for demand profiles and technology cost vintages; costs are averaged over the full span of each period.

# Single period
model_periods:
  - [2025, 2030]

# Multi-period study
model_periods:
  - [2025, 2030]
  - [2031, 2040]
  - [2041, 2050]

This creates planning periods:

  • 2025–2030 (6 years)
  • 2031–2040 (10 years)
  • 2041–2050 (10 years)

How periods are used

  • Demand: Uses the last year of each period (e.g., 2030 demand for 2025–2030)
  • New-build costs: Averaged across the full period (e.g., 2025–2030 capital costs are mean values over those years)
  • Retirements: A generator is retired at period end if its retirement year is on or before that period's final year

docs.title: Legacy format
docs.text:
Planning periods can also be defined as two separate parallel lists:

model_year: [2030, 2040, 2050]
model_first_planning_year: [2025, 2031, 2041]

Each position in model_year is paired with the corresponding entry in model_first_planning_year. model_periods is preferred because it defines each period in one place, which reduces the risk of list-length mismatches.

docs.title: target_usd_year
docs.text:
Type: Integer Required: Yes Example: 2023

All monetary values are converted to this base year USD using CPI data.

target_usd_year: 2023

Configure dollar_year_table to point to a CPI table in data_location. Applicable technology and fuel costs are converted using that table.

docs.title: utc_offset
docs.text:
Type: Integer Required: No Default: 0 Example: -8

Hour offset applied when shifting input time profiles to the model timezone.

utc_offset: -8  # Pacific Time (UTC-8)

US time zones:

  • Pacific: -8
  • Mountain: -7
  • Central: -6
  • Eastern: -5

docs.title: Example Configuration
docs.text:
Complete model definition for a multi-period study:

# Planning horizon
model_periods:
  - [2025, 2030]
  - [2031, 2040]
  - [2041, 2050]

# Currency
target_usd_year: 2023

# Time zone
utc_offset: -8

docs.title: New-Build Resources Settings
docs.text: These parameters control technology costs, new resource definitions, regional availability, and capacity constraints for candidate generators.

docs.title: new_resources
docs.text:
Type: List of lists Required: For ATB-based technologies Example: See below

List of technologies from NREL Annual Technology Baseline (ATB) to include as new-build candidates. Each item is a list: [technology, tech_detail, cost_case, size_mw].

new_resources:
  - [NaturalGas, 1-on-1 Combined Cycle (H-Frame), Moderate, 500]
  - [NaturalGas, Combustion Turbine (F-Frame), Moderate, 100]
  - [Utility-Scale Battery Storage, Lithium Ion, Moderate, 100]
  - [UtilityPV, Class1, Moderate, 100]
  - [LandbasedWind, Class3, Moderate, 100]
  - [OffShoreWind, Class3, Moderate, 100]
  - [Nuclear, Nuclear - Large, Moderate, 1000]

Format: [technology, tech_detail, cost_case, size_mw]

  • technology: Technology type (e.g., NaturalGas, UtilityPV)
  • tech_detail: Specific variant (e.g., 1-on-1 Combined Cycle (H-Frame), Class1)
  • cost_case: Cost trajectory (Conservative, Moderate, Advanced)
  • size_mw: Unit size in MW

These examples use 2024 ATB names. Names vary by data vintage and must match the configured cost and heat rate tables exactly; * is not a wildcard. The three keys are compared as text, so [Wind, 1, Moderate, 100] and [Wind, "1", Moderate, 100] are equivalent. YAML still rewrites some unquoted values (1.50 becomes 1.5), so quote values that must match exactly.

docs.title: resource_data_year
docs.text:
Type: Integer Required: No Default: No data-year filter Example: 2023

Which year's ATB data to use for technology costs.

resource_data_year: 2023

ATB is updated annually with revised cost projections. Specify the data vintage for reproducibility.

docs.title: resource_financial_case
docs.text:
Type: String Required: No Default: "Market" Example: "Market"

ATB financial assumptions case. Options:

  • Market: Market-based financing
  • R&D: Optimistic R&D case with policy support
resource_financial_case: Market

docs.title: resource_cap_recovery_years
docs.text:
Type: Integer Required: Yes Example: 20

Default capital recovery period (economic lifetime) for new generators, used to calculate annualized capital costs.

resource_cap_recovery_years: 20

docs.title: alt_resource_cap_recovery_years
docs.text:
Type: Dictionary (technology → years) Required: No Example: See below

Override capital recovery period for specific technologies (matched using string contains).

alt_resource_cap_recovery_years:
  NaturalGas_CCAvg: 15
  NaturalGas_CTAvg: 15
  Battery: 15
  Nuclear: 40

docs.title: resource_modifiers
docs.text:
Type: Dictionary (tech_name → modifications) Required: No Example: See below

Modify ATB technology parameters. Each entry specifies technology/tech_detail matching and parameter changes.

resource_modifiers:
  batteries:
    technology: Utility-Scale Battery Storage
    tech_detail: Lithium Ion
    Var_OM_Cost_per_MWh: [add, 0.15]
    Var_OM_Cost_per_MWh_In: 0.15

Modifiers apply to matching candidates already listed in new_resources; they do not create candidates.

Parameter values inside each modifier can also be specified as year-keyed dictionaries (see Settings by Model Year) to vary costs across planning periods without a full scenario management setup:

resource_modifiers:
  batteries:
    technology: Utility-Scale Battery Storage
    tech_detail: Lithium Ion
    Var_OM_Cost_per_MWh:
      2030: [add, 0.15]
      2040: [add, 0.10]

docs.title: modified_new_resources
docs.text:
Type: Dictionary (new_name → base + modifications) Required: No Example: See below

Create new technology variants by copying and modifying existing ATB technologies.

modified_new_resources:
  NGCCS100:
    technology: NaturalGas
    tech_detail: 1-on-1 Combined Cycle (H-Frame) 95% CCS
    cost_case: Conservative
    size_mw: 500
    new_technology: NaturalGas
    new_tech_detail: CCS100
    new_cost_case: Moderate
    capex_mw: [add, 116000]
    heat_rate: [add, 0.365]
    fixed_o_m_mw: [add, 9670]
    variable_o_m_mwh: [mul, 1.076]

  hydrogen_turbine:
    technology: NaturalGas
    tech_detail: 1-on-1 Combined Cycle (H-Frame)
    cost_case: Moderate
    size_mw: 100
    new_technology: hydrogen
    new_tech_detail: 1-on-1 Combined Cycle (H-Frame)
    new_cost_case: Moderate

Base parameters (copy from existing ATB technology):

  • technology: ATB technology to copy from
  • tech_detail: ATB tech detail to copy from
  • cost_case: ATB cost case to copy from
  • size_mw: Unit size

New parameters (create new technology with this name):

  • new_technology: New technology name
  • new_tech_detail: New tech detail name
  • new_cost_case: New cost case name

Modification operators:

  • [add, value]: Add to base value
  • [mul, value]: Multiply base value
  • [sub, value]: Subtract from base value
  • [truediv, value]: Divide base value
  • Direct value: Override base value

docs.title: Settings by Model Year
docs.text:
Year-keyed values are supported across all settings sections, not just new-build parameters.

Use Year-Keyed Values for the complete rules, validation behavior, and additional examples.

Quick summary:

  • Exact year values take priority.
  • default is a fallback key.
  • Incomplete year coverage without fallback raises a ValueError.

Example in resource_modifiers:

resource_modifiers:
  utility_pv:
    technology: UtilityPV
    tech_detail: Class1
    capex_mw:
      2030: [mul, 0.9]
      2040: [mul, 0.8]

Example with fallback:

carbon_tax:
  2030: 25
  default: 50

Note

The settings_management key itself is never modified by year-keyed resolution; it is always processed by scenario management logic first.

docs.title: new_gen_not_available
docs.text:
Type: Dictionary (region → list of technologies) Required: No

Legacy setting — not applied

This key is only checked for region-name consistency during validation and is not applied to exclude technologies from the model. new_resources is not region-scoped: every technology in it is built in all model regions, so there is currently no supported way to exclude a new-build technology from a subset of regions. To remove a technology entirely, omit it from new_resources. Renewable resource clusters are scoped by region through renewables_clusters.

new_gen_not_available:
  AZ:
    - OffshoreWind_Class1_Moderate_-1
    - Geothermal_HydroFlash_Moderate
  CA_N:
    - Coal_new_Moderate

Use cases:

  • Physical constraints (no offshore wind in landlocked states)
  • Policy constraints (coal banned)
  • Resource availability (no geothermal potential)

docs.title: interconnect_capex_mw
docs.text:
Type: Number or dictionary Required: No Default: None (falls back to legacy transmission_investment_cost if provided) Example: See patterns below

Flexible specification of per-MW interconnection capital cost (USD/MW) applied to new and existing resources. Replaces the deprecated spur line mileage system (transmission_investment_cost with capacity_limit_spur_fn file).

Important: All cost values must be in the same dollar year as target_usd_year (the target dollar year for cost normalization). PowerGenome does not automatically adjust interconnection costs for inflation.

Supported Patterns:

docs.title: 1. Scalar
docs.text:
Apply uniform cost to all resources:

interconnect_capex_mw: 150000  # $150k/MW for all resources

docs.title: 2. Explicit Schema (Recommended)
docs.text:
Use an explicit fallback with typed override blocks:

interconnect_capex_mw:
  fallback_capex_mw: 110000
  by_technology:
    wind: 120000
    offshore_wind: 200000
    battery: 50000
  by_region:
    CA_N: 125000
  by_region_technology:
    CA_N:
      offshore_wind: 210000

Precedence (most specific to least specific):

  1. by_region_technology
  2. by_region
  3. by_technology
  4. fallback_capex_mw

docs.title: 3. Region-Only
docs.text:
Different costs by region (exact region name matching):

interconnect_capex_mw:
  fallback_capex_mw: 120000
  by_region:
    CA_N: 140000
    CA_S: 130000
    AZ: 125000

docs.title: 4. Technology-Only
docs.text:
Different costs by technology using case-insensitive substring matching with shortest-first precedence:

interconnect_capex_mw:
  fallback_capex_mw: 100000
  by_technology:
    wind: 120000          # matches 'LandbasedWind_Class3_Moderate', 'OffshoreWind_Class1_Moderate'
    offshore_wind: 200000 # longer substring overwrites previous 'wind' assignment
    battery: 50000        # matches 'Battery_4Hr_Moderate', 'Battery_*_Moderate'
    solar: 110000         # matches 'UtilityPV_Class1_Moderate'

Precedence rule: Shorter substrings applied first, then longer (more specific) substrings override previous assignments. This allows general categories with specific exceptions.

docs.title: 5. Region -> Technology Nested
docs.text:
Region-specific technology costs with regions as keys under by_region_technology:

interconnect_capex_mw:
  fallback_capex_mw: 110000
  by_region_technology:
    CA_N:
      battery: 60000
      offshore_wind: 210000
      solar: 105000
    CA_S:
      solar: 95000
      wind: 115000
  by_region:
    AZ: 125000

Within each region, technology substrings follow shortest-first precedence.

Matching Rules:

  • Technology matching: Case-insensitive substring search against the technology column
  • Substring precedence: Shortest substrings processed first; longer substrings override
  • Region matching: Exact match against model region names (case-sensitive)
  • Explicit schema: Use only fallback_capex_mw, by_region, by_technology, and by_region_technology at the top level.
  • Invalid mixing: In legacy syntax, mixing region and technology keys at the same top level is invalid.

Examples of Invalid Configuration:

# ERROR: Cannot mix region and technology keys
interconnect_capex_mw:
  CA_N: 140000      # Region key
  wind: 120000      # Technology key - mixing not allowed!

Legacy Syntax (Deprecated):

You may still use the older top-level default style for backward compatibility. A deprecation warning is logged at runtime.

Behavior:

  • Non-destructive: Existing non-zero interconnect_capex_mw values in the resource dataframe are never overwritten
  • Automatic annuity: interconnect_annuity is computed automatically for:
  • Newly assigned capex rows
  • Pre-existing capex rows with zero/blank annuity
  • Financial parameters: Annuity calculation uses plant-specific wacc_real and cap_recovery_years from the resource dataframe
  • Legacy bypass: When interconnect_capex_mw is provided, legacy spur mileage columns (spur_miles, offshore_spur_miles, tx_miles) are ignored (warning logged if present)

Migration from Legacy System:

Old approach (deprecated):

# Settings
transmission_investment_cost:
  spur:
    capex_mw_mile:
      CA_N: 3000
      CA_S: 3200
    wacc: 0.069
    investment_years: 60

# Required extra_inputs file: capacity_limit_spur_fn
# File: resource_capacity_spur.csv
# technology,region,spur_miles
# offshore_wind_fixed,CA_N,45
# solar_pv,CA_N,12

New approach (recommended):

interconnect_capex_mw:
  fallback_capex_mw: 120000
  by_technology:
    offshore_wind: 200000  # Direct cost specification
    solar: 105000

Benefits of new system:

  • No external file dependency
  • More intuitive (direct $/MW vs. mileage calculation)
  • Flexible pattern matching (region, technology, or nested)
  • Automatic annuity handling
  • Better error messages

docs.title: transmission_investment_cost
docs.text:
Type: Dictionary Required: No Deprecated: Use interconnect_capex_mw instead Example: See legacy documentation

Legacy spur line mileage-based interconnection cost system. Contains nested dictionaries for spur, offshore_spur, and tx with keys:

  • capex_mw_mile: Cost per MW-mile (by region)
  • wacc: Weighted average cost of capital
  • investment_years: Capital recovery period

Deprecation notice: This parameter is deprecated and will be removed in a future release. It is only used when interconnect_capex_mw is not provided, and emits warnings during execution. Migrate to interconnect_capex_mw for simplified, more flexible cost specification.

docs.title: renewables_clusters
docs.text:
Type: List of dictionaries Required: For renewable resources (wind, solar, geothermal) with spatially-distributed potential Example: See below

Configure clustering of renewable resource sites from external datasets (e.g., NREL reV). PowerGenome filters, bins, and clusters pre-existing resource data to create representative sites for the model.

renewables_clusters:
  - region: all
    technology: landbasedwind
    filter:
      - feature: lcoe_interconnect_adj
        max: 60
    bin:
      - feature: lcoe_interconnect_adj
        weights: capacity_mw
        mw_per_bin: 10000
    cluster:
      - feature: cf
        n_clusters: 2
        method: agg

  - region: p4
    technology: utilitypv
    filter:
      - feature: lcoe_interconnect_adj
        max: 35
    bin:
      - feature: lcoe_interconnect_adj
        weights: capacity_mw
        mw_per_bin: 50000
    cluster:
      - feature: lcoe_interconnect_adj
        n_clusters: 2
        method: agg

  - region: all
    technology: geothermal
    type: egs
    filter:
      - feature: class
        max: 6
    group:
      - class
    group_modifiers:
      - group: class
        group_value: 6
        Inv_Cost_per_MWyr: [add, 64820]

  - region: all
    technology: offshorewind
    turbine_type: floating
    pref_site: 0
    bin:
      - feature: lcoe_interconnect_adj
        weights: capacity_mw
        q: 2

Common parameters:

  • region: Model region name or all (applies to all regions)
  • technology: Technology type (lowercase: landbasedwind, utilitypv, offshorewind, geothermal)

Filtering (filter):

  • feature: Attribute to filter on (lcoe, cf, lcoe_interconnect_adj, class)
  • max: Maximum value threshold (exclude resources above this)
  • min: Minimum value threshold (exclude resources below this)

Binning (bin):

Groups resources into bins before clustering:

  • feature: Attribute to bin by (lcoe, lcoe_interconnect_adj, cf)
  • weights: Weight bins by capacity (mw, capacity_mw)
  • q: Number of quantile bins (equal-frequency binning)
  • mw_per_bin: Fixed MW capacity per bin (alternative to q)
  • bins: Custom bin edges (list of values)

Clustering (cluster):

Aggregates resources within each bin:

  • feature: Attribute to cluster by (cf, lcoe, lcoe_interconnect_adj, profile)
  • n_clusters: Number of clusters to create
  • method: Clustering algorithm (agg for agglomerative hierarchical clustering)

Grouping (group + group_modifiers):

Alternative to binning/clustering for technologies with discrete classes:

  • group: List of features to group by (e.g., [class])
  • group_modifiers: List of cost adjustments per group value

Technology-specific parameters:

  • Offshore wind: turbine_type (fixed, floating), pref_site (0 or 1 for preferred sites)
  • Geothermal: type (egs, geohydrobinary)

Workflow:

  1. Load resource sites from external data (NREL reV, ReEDS)
  2. Filter sites by quality thresholds
  3. Bin remaining sites by cost/performance
  4. Cluster sites within each bin to reduce model size
  5. Create aggregated resource with weighted-average characteristics

See Configure Renewable Clusters How-To for detailed examples.

docs.title: Cost Multipliers
docs.text:
Regional capital cost multipliers adjust technology costs by region to account for differences in labor costs, permitting, and construction conditions. PowerGenome uses the regional_cost_factor_table to apply these adjustments.

See Regional Configuration - Cost Multipliers for details on cost_multiplier_region_map and cost_multiplier_technology_map parameters.

docs.title: Example Configuration
docs.text:
Complete new-build configuration:

# New-build technologies
resource_data_year: 2024
resource_financial_case: Market
resource_cap_recovery_years: 20

new_resources:
  - [NaturalGas, 1-on-1 Combined Cycle (H-Frame) 95% CCS, Conservative, 500]
  - [NaturalGas, Combustion Turbine (F-Frame), Moderate, 100]
  - [Utility-Scale Battery Storage, Lithium Ion, Moderate, 100]
  - [UtilityPV, Class1, Moderate, 100]
  - [LandbasedWind, Class3, Moderate, 100]
  - [Nuclear, Nuclear - Large, Moderate, 1000]

# Technology modifications
resource_modifiers:
  batteries:
    technology: Utility-Scale Battery Storage
    tech_detail: Lithium Ion
    Var_OM_Cost_per_MWh: [add, 0.15]

# Regional restrictions (legacy — only validated, not applied)
new_gen_not_available:
  AZ:
    - OffshoreWind_Class1_Moderate
  CA_N:
    - Coal_newAvgCF_Moderate

# Capacity limits
input_folder: extra_inputs
capacity_limit_spur_fn: resource_capacity_spur.csv

# Renewable sites
renewables_clusters:
  - region: CA_N
    technology: landbasedwind
    filter:
      - feature: lcoe_interconnect_adj
        max: 60
    bin:
      - feature: lcoe_interconnect_adj
        weights: capacity_mw
        mw_per_bin: 10000
    cluster:
      - feature: cf
        n_clusters: 2
        method: agg

RESOURCE_GROUP_PROFILES: /data/nrel_profiles

docs.title: Regional Configuration
docs.text:
Regional settings define the geographic structure of your model—how base regions aggregate into model regions, and region-specific customizations.

Understanding PowerGenome Regions

PowerGenome uses a hierarchical regional structure based on NREL's Regional Energy Deployment System (ReEDS) regions:

  • Base regions: The fundamental geographic units from the ReEDS model (labeled p1, p2, p3, etc.)
  • Aggregated regions: Groups of multiple base regions combined together (e.g., p1_2 combines p1 and p2)
  • Model regions: The regions in your study - can be either single base regions OR aggregated regions

The region_aggregations parameter defines how base regions map to model regions. While PowerGenome examples use ReEDS regions, you can adapt this structure to any geography (countries, provinces, utility territories, etc.) by providing appropriately structured data tables.

docs.title: model_regions
docs.text:
Type: List of strings Required: Yes Example: ["CA_N", "CA_S", "AZ", "NM"]

Names of the regions that will appear in output files. These can be:

  • Single base regions (e.g., p10, p22)
  • Aggregated region names (defined in region_aggregations)
model_regions: [p1_2, p3, northwest]

Here p1_2 and northwest are aggregated regions and p3 is a base region.

All regional parameters use these names as keys.

docs.title: region_aggregations
docs.text:
Type: Dictionary (model region → list of base regions) Required: Only if using aggregations Example: See below

Maps model region names to the base regions they contain. Use this to combine multiple base regions into larger study areas.

region_aggregations:
  p1_2:      # Aggregated region
    - p1
    - p2
  p3: [p3]   # Pass-through (optional, can omit)
  northwest:  # Custom name for aggregated region
    - p4
    - p5
    - p6

Important:

  • Model region names in region_aggregations must appear in model_regions
  • Base region names must match those in your generation/demand data tables
  • If model_regions contains a name NOT in region_aggregations, it's treated as a pass-through (1:1 mapping to a base region)

docs.title: regional_capacity_reserves
docs.text:
Type: Nested dictionary Required: No Example: See below

Defines capacity reserve requirements by zone. Top-level keys are CapRes_<num> tags, second level keys are model regions.

regional_capacity_reserves:
  CapRes_1:
    CA_N: 0.15  # 15% reserve margin
    CA_S: 0.15
  CapRes_2:
    AZ: 0.12

Configure resource contributions with capacity_reserve_values, model_tag_values, or regional_tag_values; see Resource Tags.

docs.title: cap_res_network_derate_default
docs.text:
Type: Float (0-1) Required: No Default: 0.95 Example: 0.95

Derating factor for transmission imports used to meet capacity reserves. A value of 0.95 means transmission can only contribute 95% of its capacity toward reserve requirements.

cap_res_network_derate_default: 0.95

docs.title: new_gen_not_available
docs.text:
Type: Dictionary (region → list of new-build technologies) Required: No

Legacy setting — not applied

This key is only checked for region-name consistency during validation and is not applied to exclude technologies from the model. new_resources is not region-scoped, so there is currently no supported way to exclude a new-build technology from a subset of regions. Renewable resource clusters are scoped by region through renewables_clusters.

new_gen_not_available:
  AZ:
    - OffshoreWind_Class1  # No offshore wind in AZ
    - Geothermal_HydroFlash  # No geothermal potential
  CA_N:
    - Coal_new  # Coal banned in CA

Technology names must match those in new_resources.

docs.title: cost_multiplier_region_map
docs.text:
Type: Dictionary (cost region name → list of model regions) Required: No (only if regional_cost_factor_table doesn't contain all base regions) Example: See below

Maps cost region names from the regional_cost_factor_table to model regions. Use this when your cost multiplier table uses different region names than your base/model regions.

cost_multiplier_region_map:
  CA_N_SPUR: [CA_N]
  CA_S_SPUR: [CA_S]
  Southwest: [AZ, NM]  # One cost region covers multiple model regions

When to use:

  • Your regional_cost_factor_table doesn't include all base regions
  • Cost table uses aggregate region names (e.g., "Southwest" covers multiple model regions)
  • Using generic cost tables (e.g., from NREL) with different naming conventions

When NOT needed: If regional_cost_factor_table already contains all your base or model regions with matching names.

docs.title: cost_multiplier_technology_map
docs.text:
Type: Dictionary (cost table technology name → list of user technology names) Required: No Example: See below

Maps technology names from the regional_cost_factor_table to user-defined technology names. Use this to apply cost multipliers from one technology to custom technologies created via modified_new_resources.

cost_multiplier_technology_map:
  NaturalGas_2-on-1 Combined Cycle (F-Frame): [hydrogen_turbine, synthetic_fuel_turbine]  # Multiple custom techs use NGCC costs
  LandbasedWind: [Biomass_Dedicated]  # Use wind cost multipliers for biomass

Common use cases:

  • Custom technologies from modified_new_resources that should use cost multipliers from a base ATB technology
  • Technologies from additional_technologies_fn that need regional cost adjustments
  • Applying one technology's multipliers to another (e.g., using wind multipliers for solar)

docs.title: utc_offset
docs.text:
Type: Integer Required: No Default: 0 Example: -8

Hour offset applied when shifting input time profiles to the model timezone.

utc_offset: -8  # Pacific Time (UTC-8)

US time zones:

  • Pacific: -8
  • Mountain: -7
  • Central: -6
  • Eastern: -5

docs.title: fuel_region_map
docs.text:
Type: Dictionary (AEO region → list of model regions) Required: No (legacy workflow only) Example: See below

Legacy Parameter

This parameter is only needed for the legacy AEO fuel workflow. In the simplified workflow (recommended), provide fuel prices for all base regions directly in your fuel price table instead.

Maps EIA Annual Energy Outlook (AEO) fuel price regions to model regions when using the legacy AEO data workflow.

fuel_region_map:
  pacific: [CA_N, CA_S]
  mountain: [AZ, NM]
  west_south_central: [TX]

Common AEO region names:

  • pacific: Pacific
  • mountain: Mountain
  • west_south_central: West South Central
  • east_north_central: East North Central
  • new_england: New England

See Fuel Settings for details on the simplified vs. legacy fuel workflows.

docs.title: Example Configuration
docs.text:
Complete regional settings for a California + Southwest model:

# Base model regions
model_regions: [CA_N, CA_S, AZ, NM]

# Aggregate IPM regions
region_aggregations:
  CA_N: [CA_IID, CA_LADWP, CA_BANC]
  CA_S: [CA_SCE, CA_SDGE]

# Regional capacity reserves
regional_capacity_reserves:
  CapRes_1:
    CA_N: 0.15
    CA_S: 0.15
    AZ: 0.12
    NM: 0.12

cap_res_network_derate_default: 0.95

# Legacy — only validated, not applied
new_gen_not_available:
  CA_N: [Coal_new, OffshoreWind]
  CA_S: [Coal_new]
  AZ: [OffshoreWind, Geothermal]
  NM: [OffshoreWind, Geothermal]

# Timezone
utc_offset: -8

docs.title: Resource Tags Settings
docs.text: Resource tags control how generators are classified in GenX and other capacity expansion models. Tags determine dispatch behavior, policy eligibility, and operational constraints.

docs.title: Tag System Overview
docs.text:
GenX uses binary or integer tags to categorize resources. Common tags include:

  • THERM: Thermal zone for reserves/capacity requirements
  • VRE: Variable renewable energy (wind/solar)
  • STOR: Storage resources (batteries, pumped hydro)
  • FLEX: Flexible demand/demand response
  • HYDRO: Hydroelectric resources
  • MUST_RUN: Must-run generators (cogen, nuclear)
  • LDS: Long-duration storage (>12 hours)

Each resource must have a value for every tag defined in the model.

docs.title: model_tag_names
docs.text:
Type: List of strings Required: No Example: See below

List of all resource tags used in the model.

model_tag_names:
  - THERM
  - VRE
  - STOR
  - FLEX
  - HYDRO
  - MUST_RUN
  - LDS

Tags named here or in the tag-value mappings are initialized to default_model_tag (zero by default). Specify values for technologies that need different values.

Custom Tags

You can define custom tags for specialized models. For example, OFFSHORE for offshore wind, BIOMASS for biomass resources, or NEW_BUILD to distinguish new vs. existing capacity.

docs.title: model_tag_values
docs.text:
Type: Dictionary (tag → technology → value) Required: No Example: See below

Default tag values for each technology. These apply across all regions unless overridden.

Technology Matching

Technology names are matched using case-insensitive substring matching. Shortest (most general) patterns are applied first, then longer (more specific) patterns override previous assignments. This allows you to set broad defaults and create specific exceptions.

model_tag_values:
  THERM:
    NaturalGas: 1
    UtilityPV: 0
    Battery: 0
    Hydroelectric: 0

  VRE:
    NaturalGas: 0
    UtilityPV: 1
    Battery: 0
    Hydroelectric: 0

  STOR:
    NaturalGas: 0
    UtilityPV: 0
    Battery: 1
    Hydroelectric_Pumped: 1  # More specific, overrides 'Hydroelectric'

  FLEX:
    NaturalGas: 0
    UtilityPV: 0
    Battery: 0
    Hydroelectric: 0

  HYDRO:
    NaturalGas: 0
    UtilityPV: 0
    Battery: 0
    Hydroelectric: 1

  MUST_RUN:
    NaturalGas: 0
    UtilityPV: 0
    Battery: 0
    Hydroelectric: 0

  LDS:
    NaturalGas: 0
    UtilityPV: 0
    Battery: 0
    Hydroelectric_Pumped: 1

Tag values:

  • Binary (0/1): Most tags are binary flags
  • Integer (1, 2, 3...): THERM tag often uses integers for thermal zones
  • Technology keys are literal substrings; * is not a wildcard.

docs.title: Technology Matching
docs.text:
Use a shared substring to assign tags to multiple technologies at once.

model_tag_values:
  THERM:
    Battery: 0  # Matches all battery technologies
    NaturalGas: 1  # Matches all natural gas technologies
    LandbasedWind: 0  # Matches all wind technologies
    OffShoreWind: 0  # More specific, can override 'Wind' if both present

  VRE:
    Battery: 0
    NaturalGas: 0
    LandbasedWind: 1
    OffShoreWind: 1

  STOR:
    Battery: 1
    NaturalGas: 0
    LandbasedWind: 0

  FLEX:
    Battery: 0
    NaturalGas: 0
    LandbasedWind: 0

Substring precedence: Shorter substrings are processed first, longer substrings override:

model_tag_values:
  THERM:
    Wind: 0          # Applied first - matches 'LandbasedWind_Class3', 'OffShoreWind_Class12'
    OffShoreWind: 1  # Applied second - overwrites only offshore wind technologies

This makes configuration maintainable when you have many similar technologies.

docs.title: regional_tag_values
docs.text:
Type: Dictionary (region → tag → technology → value) Required: No Example: See below

Override tag values for specific technologies in specific regions. Regional values take precedence over model_tag_values.

regional_tag_values:
  CA_N:
    THERM:
      NaturalGas: 2  # Different thermal zone in CA
    MUST_RUN:
      Hydroelectric: 1  # California hydro is must-run

  AZ:
    THERM:
      NaturalGas: 1  # Arizona thermal zone
    MUST_RUN:
      Hydroelectric: 0  # Arizona hydro is flexible

Use cases:

  • Different thermal reserve zones by region
  • Region-specific must-run requirements (e.g., cogeneration contracts)
  • Policy differences (e.g., renewable portfolio standard eligibility)

docs.title: Energy Share Requirements (ESR)
docs.text:
Tags can define renewable/clean energy eligibility:

model_tag_names:
  - THERM
  - VRE
  - STOR
  - ESR_1    # Renewable Portfolio Standard
  - ESR_2    # Clean Energy Standard

model_tag_values:
  ESR_1:
    UtilityPV: 1  # Eligible for RPS
    NaturalGas_CCS: 0  # Not eligible for RPS
    Nuclear: 0  # Not eligible for RPS

  ESR_2:
    UtilityPV: 1  # Eligible for CES
    NaturalGas_CCS: 1  # May be eligible for CES (with CCS)
    Nuclear: 1  # Eligible for CES (carbon-free)

Practical notes

  • All tag values default to 0; only set entries that should be eligible
  • Region-specific ESR tags can be applied via regional_tag_values when a policy limits deliverability to certain regions (e.g., only PJM resources satisfy a New Jersey RPS)
  • Technology matching is substring-based, so short patterns (e.g., Wind) will match many technologies. Use longer strings to avoid accidental eligibility

See Energy Share Requirements How-To for policy configuration.

docs.title: Minimum/Maximum Capacity Tags
docs.text:
Tags can enforce capacity constraints:

model_tag_names:
  - THERM
  - VRE
  - MinCapTag_1  # Minimum solar requirement
  - MaxCapTag_1  # Maximum gas limit

model_tag_values:
  MinCapTag_1:
    UtilityPV: 1  # Counts toward solar minimum
    NaturalGas: 0

  MaxCapTag_1:
    UtilityPV: 0
    NaturalGas: 1  # Counts toward gas maximum

Configure requirements in emission_policies_table (legacy alias: emission_policies_fn) or via GenX settings.

docs.title: CapRes_<num> Tags
docs.text:
Define which reserve zones each resource contributes to:

model_tag_names:
  - CapRes_1  # Primary reserve zone
  - CapRes_2  # Secondary reserve zone

model_tag_values:
  # Here, all matched resources contribute to the two different reserve requirements
  CapRes_1:
    NaturalGas: 0.9
    Battery: 0.95

  CapRes_2:
    NaturalGas: 0.9
    Battery: 0.9

############################
# *OR*
# Resources in specific regions contribute to different capacity reserve requirements
regional_tag_values:
  CA_N:
    CapRes_1:
      NaturalGas: 0.9
      Battery: 0.95
  AZ:
    CapRes_2:
      NaturalGas: 0.8
      Battery: 0.9

Capacity reserve requirements are set in regional_capacity_reserves.

Simplified Configuration

PowerGenome provides a simplified shorthand for specifying capacity reserve credits via capacity_reserve_values. Instead of manually building the nested regional_tag_values structure shown above, you can use:

capacity_reserve_values:
  NaturalGas: 0.9
  Battery: 0.95

regional_capacity_reserves:
  CapRes_1:
    CA_N: 0.164
    AZ: 0.180
  CapRes_2:
    CA_N: 0.090

The system automatically expands this into the regional_tag_values structure. See Configure Capacity Reserve Requirements for complete examples and best practices.

docs.title: Tag Validation
docs.text: For GenX output, each resource must have exactly one nonzero resource-type tag among the recognized types (such as THERM, VRE, STOR, FLEX, and HYDRO). PowerGenome logs the affected resources and raises a ValueError when a resource has none or more than one. Policy tags such as ESR_1 are additional to the resource type. Unassigned tag values default to zero unless default_model_tag is set.

docs.title: Generator Columns Output
docs.text:
Tags appear as columns in Generators_data.csv:

Resource,technology,THERM,VRE,STOR,FLEX,HYDRO,MUST_RUN,LDS
CA_N_NaturalGas_CC_1,NaturalGas_CC,1,0,0,0,0,0,0
CA_N_Solar_PV_1,UtilityPV,0,1,0,0,0,0,0
CA_N_Battery_1,Battery_4Hr,0,0,1,0,0,0,0

GenX reads these columns to determine resource behavior in optimization.

docs.title: Example Configuration
docs.text:
Complete tag configuration for a multi-region model:

# Define all tags
model_tag_names:
  - THERM
  - VRE
  - STOR
  - FLEX
  - HYDRO
  - MUST_RUN
  - LDS
  - ESR_1
  - CapRes_1

# Technology defaults
model_tag_values:
  THERM:
    NaturalGas: 1
    UtilityPV: 0
    Battery: 0

  VRE:
    NaturalGas: 0
    UtilityPV: 1
    Battery: 0

  STOR:
    NaturalGas: 0
    UtilityPV: 0
    Battery: 1

  FLEX:
    NaturalGas: 0
    UtilityPV: 0
    Battery: 0

  HYDRO:
    NaturalGas: 0
    UtilityPV: 0
    Battery: 0

  MUST_RUN:
    NaturalGas: 0
    UtilityPV: 0
    Battery: 0

  LDS:
    NaturalGas: 0
    UtilityPV: 0
    Battery: 0

  ESR_1:
    NaturalGas: 0
    UtilityPV: 1  # RPS-eligible
    Battery: 0

  CapRes_1:
    NaturalGas: 1
    UtilityPV: 1
    Battery: 1

# Regional overrides
regional_tag_values:
  CA_N:
    THERM:
      NaturalGas: 2  # Different thermal zone
  CA_S:
    THERM:
      NaturalGas: 2

docs.title: Scenario Management Settings
docs.text: This reference defines scenario selectors, file paths, and supported swap shapes. For a complete runnable workflow, see Run Multiple Scenarios. For merge rationale and execution order, see Multi-Scenario Architecture.

docs.title: scenario_definitions_fn
docs.text:
Type: string filename or path, relative to input_folder. Required: no; enables the explicit scenario CSV when set.

scenario_definitions_fn: scenario_inputs.csv
CSV column Requirement case_id Mandatory case identifier; repeat it across that case’s planning years. year Mandatory integer end year from model_year or model_periods. Other columns Dimension names; cells select levels under settings_management.

Each case/year pair must be unique. Include each planning year once per complete case and order years chronologically within cases: row order sets period numbers. The CSV lists only requested combinations; PowerGenome does not expand a full factorial design. The how-to contains a four-row example with two cases and two years.

docs.title: settings_management
docs.text:
Type: mapping of year selector → dimension → level → settings to modify. Default: no swaps. A CSV with only case_id,year is valid without this mapping.

settings_management:
  all_years:
    carbon_policy:
      unchanged: {}
      tax_50:
        carbon_tax: 50
  2040:
    all_cases:
      tx_expansion_per_period: 0.5
Selector Meaning Integer year, such as 2040 Apply to rows for that planning year. all_years Apply to every CSV row before the specific-year block. all_cases inside either block Direct setting/value pairs applied before that block’s dimensions. Dimension and level Match a CSV column and cell value; names and value types must agree. {} or null (~) as a selected level Recognized no-op; keep the base settings unchanged.

Swaps recursively merge dictionaries but replace scalars and entire lists. Within each block, two selected dimensions modifying the same leaf raise an error. The conflict check excludes all_cases and resets between all_years and a specific year. Do not split this top-level mapping across files: loading settings directories uses shallow updates with no guaranteed file order. See merge precedence.

docs.title: Multi-Period Scenarios
docs.text:
Keep model_year and model_first_planning_year lists aligned and chronological, or use start/end pairs in model_periods (see Model Definition). A year-specific swap does not persist into later periods.

A selected swap can contain year-keyed values, avoiding repeated year blocks. If the base value is a scalar, first change it to a year-keyed mapping in its original settings file: a dictionary swap cannot merge into an existing scalar. For example, use this base value and scenario mapping (each defined only once):

carbon_tax: {2030: 0, 2040: 0}
settings_management:
  all_years:
    carbon_policy:
      rising_tax:
        carbon_tax:
          2030: 25
          2040: 50
  2040:
    carbon_policy:
      rising_tax:
        carbon_tax: 75

For a CSV selecting rising_tax in both years, the resolved tax is 25 in 2030 and 75 in 2040. all_years is processed first; the 2040 scalar replaces its whole year-keyed dictionary before year resolution. Year-keyed mappings use integer years and an optional default, not all_years. Cover every year being resolved or provide default; see Year-Keyed Values.

docs.title: Parameter Swap Examples
docs.text: These are alternative fragments to put under a selected level, not a second complete settings file. Use values supported by your configured input tables. The technology and region names below are illustrative; substitute names that exist in your own data tables.

docs.title: Technology Costs
docs.text:
resource_modifiers:
  batteries:
    technology: Utility-Scale Battery Storage
    tech_detail: Lithium Ion
    capex_mw: [mul, 0.8]
    capex_mwh: [mul, 0.8]

The arbitrary short-name key (batteries) identifies a modifier. Include exact technology and tech_detail selectors matching a resource in new_resources; * is not a wildcard. Numeric parameter values set an absolute value; pairs use [operator, value], with add, mul, sub, or truediv. They can also be year-keyed. Reusing an existing modifier key preserves its other fields.

An ATB trajectory (Advanced, Moderate, or Conservative) is the cost_case entry of each new_resources row, not a standalone trajectory setting. To change it with a swap, provide the entire desired resource list in the shape [technology, tech_detail, cost_case, size_mw]. resource_financial_case selects a financial case, not an ATB trajectory. See New-Build Resources.

docs.title: Technology Availability
docs.text:
A list replacement such as this allows only these listed generic candidates:

new_resources:
  - [NaturalGas, 1-on-1 Combined Cycle (H-Frame), Moderate, 500]
  - [Utility-Scale Battery Storage, Lithium Ion, Moderate, 1]

Any other base new_resources entries are removed. Resources can also be produced by renewables_clusters, which must be considered separately. new_resources is not region-scoped: omissions apply everywhere. The legacy new_gen_not_available does not exclude resources, and ALL_REGIONS is not a recognized region key. For region-scoped renewable candidates, use renewables_clusters. Two dimensions replacing new_resources in one block conflict; define a combined candidate list instead.

docs.title: Fuel prices and demand
docs.text:
fuel_scenarios:
  naturalgas: reference

Fuel scenario names must exist in the configured fuel-price data; a high_price label is not automatically available. See Fuel Settings.

Demand curves are read from the DataManager demand table as supplied. Legacy growth_scenario, load_eia_aeo_year, historical_load_region_map, future_load_region_map, and alt_growth_rate do not apply growth; there is no default_growth_rate. Supply different demand data for a demand sensitivity. Distributed generation capacity and profiles also come from configured tables, not a capacity-growth settings value; see Distributed Generation.

docs.title: Retirement assumptions
docs.text:
generation_table:
  table_name: generation_early_retirement.parquet

Use a real table containing the desired retirement_year values. For myopic multi-period studies, select the same generation table in every period of a case, for example with an all_years swap. Fixed membership is needed for consistent generator clusters; do not swap or filter generation data by period. See Retirement filtering and Data Tables for table selection syntax.

docs.title: Transmission and regional reserves
docs.text:
tx_expansion_per_period: 1.0
tx_expansion_mw_per_period: 400
regional_capacity_reserves:
  CapRes_1:
    p1_2: 0.15
    p3: 0.15
    p4: 0.15

The allowed reinforcement is the larger of the fraction of existing line capacity and the specified MW amount. 1.0 allows adding the existing capacity again; the MW amount is a minimum allowance, not a cap. There are no transmission settings named max_network_reinforcement_mw, tx_expansion_per_mw, or enforce_constraints. See Transmission.

Reserve margins use constraint → region → fraction, not a flat region map: 0.15 means 15%, not 1.15. A selected level can change several nested fields at once, with unaffected entries retained by deep merge. See Configure Capacity Reserves.

docs.title: input_folder
docs.text:
Type: string path. Default when omitted: extra_inputs, relative to the working directory.

input_folder: extra_inputs

When explicitly configured as a relative path, it resolves from the parent of the settings directory (or from the parent of a single settings file). scenario_definitions_fn resolves under it. Relative data_location follows the same settings-based rule, while relative RESOURCE_GROUPS and RESOURCE_GROUP_PROFILES use the current working directory.

docs.title: Results Folder
docs.text: Specify the destination with --results_folder; it is not a YAML setting. With default GenX output and a scenario CSV, the path is results/<case_id>/Inputs/Inputs_pN/ when the destination is results. Each period contains resources/, system/, policies/, and the resolved powergenome_case_settings.yml. Without a scenario CSV, the path is results/Inputs/Inputs_pN/. See the CLI Reference for output flags.

docs.title: case_id: all
docs.text:
Type: a value in the case_id column of the emission_policies_table input.

Rows whose case_id is all (any capitalization) are read as the case that is running whenever that case has no rows of its own, so one set of policy rows can serve every case. The substitution is decided per case, not per row: once a case has any row of its own, its all rows are left unused, so a case with only some of its years fails on the missing ones. This is how the bundled fixture shares its caps across cases. See Run Multiple Scenarios.

docs.title: copy_case_id
docs.text:
Type: optional column in the emission_policies_table input, not a YAML setting or a column that copies scenario settings.

case_id,year,region,copy_case_id,ESR_1
baseline,2030,p1_2,,0.50
carbon_50,2030,p1_2,baseline,

The target copies policy values from the source case with the same year and region. Provide corresponding rows for other years and regions as needed. Policy columns must use output names such as ESR_1, not informal RPS or CES labels. Use case_id: all instead when every case shares the same rows. See Energy Share Requirements.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
Condition Behavior Duplicate case/year Error. Unknown dimension/level for a row Warning and no swap unless matched by either applicable block. Two selected dimensions change one leaf in a block Error. CSV years differ from configured years Runner warns; a row with an unconfigured year subsequently fails planning-year resolution. Missing year within a case Not automatically rejected; check completeness yourself. Missing year-keyed coverage without default Error during year resolution. Requested --case-id absent from CSV Error.

Run validate_powergenome --settings_file settings for settings/data checks, then inspect resolved scenario settings and run one case before the full set. The how-to validation example checks CSV completeness explicitly. Reruns do not automatically skip completed cases.

docs.title: Transmission Settings
docs.text:
These parameters define inter-regional transmission network expansion costs, line losses, and reference data tables containing network topology.

Network Topology from Data Tables

Unlike generators and demand, transmission network structure (which regions connect, capacities, distances) is not defined in settings YAML. Instead, PowerGenome loads this from data tables configured via transmission_constraints_table and transmission_cost_table.

docs.title: transmission_constraints_table
docs.text:
Type: String or dictionary Required: For database-based transmission data Example: "trancap_init_energy_wecc_pg.csv"

Table containing transmission capacity between base regions.

Simple:

transmission_constraints_table: transmission_capacity.csv

Advanced:

transmission_constraints_table:
  table_name: transmission.parquet
  scenario: high_capacity
  filters:
    - - [year, '=', 2030]

Expected columns:

  • region_from: Origin base region
  • region_to: Destination base region
  • firm_ttc_mw: Firm transmission capacity (MW)
  • nonfirm_ttc_mw: Non-firm capacity (optional)

PowerGenome aggregates these constraints across base regions according to region_aggregations.

docs.title: transmission_cost_table
docs.text:
Type: String or dictionary Required: For pre-calculated transmission costs Example: "transmission_distance_cost_500kVac_annuity.csv"

Table with transmission line costs and losses calculated from least-cost-path analysis.

transmission_cost_table: network_costs.csv

Expected columns:

  • start_region: Origin model region
  • dest_region: Destination model region
  • total_interconnect_annuity_mw: Annualized cost ($/MW-yr)
  • total_interconnect_cost_mw: Total capital cost ($/MW)
  • total_line_loss_frac: Line loss as fraction (0.05 = 5%)
  • dollar_year: Cost basis year

Provide user-specified costs via transmission_cost_table:

File format (network_costs.csv):

start_region,dest_region,total_interconnect_annuity_mw,total_interconnect_cost_mw,total_line_loss_frac,dollar_year
northeast,midwest,15000,350000,0.08,2018
midwest,south,12000,280000,0.05,2018

Use Pre-Calculated Costs

PowerGenome can calculate costs from region centroids, but pre-calculated costs from least-cost-path analysis are strongly recommended. See Gagnon et al. (2023) for methodology.

docs.title: tx_value_col
docs.text:
Type: String Required: No Default: "firm_ttc_mw" Options: "firm_ttc_mw" or "nonfirm_ttc_mw"

Which capacity column to use from transmission data tables.

tx_value_col: firm_ttc_mw

Firm vs non-firm:

  • Firm: Guaranteed capacity (lower value, more conservative)
  • Non-firm: Opportunistic capacity (higher value, less reliable)

PowerGenome v0.8+ defaults to firm_ttc_mw. Previous versions used nonfirm_ttc_mw.

docs.title: avg_distribution_loss
docs.text:
Type: Float Required: For distributed generation Default: 0.0 Example: 0.06

Distribution-level line loss (transmission substation to customer).

avg_distribution_loss: 0.06  # 6% distribution loss

Used when subtracting distributed generation from total demand. Total demand includes distribution losses, so DG must be adjusted.

docs.title: tx_expansion_per_period
docs.text:
Type: Float Required: For transmission expansion Example: 1.0

Maximum fractional expansion of existing transmission per planning period.

tx_expansion_per_period: 1.0  # Can double existing capacity

Interpretation:

  • 1.0: Can add 100% of existing capacity (500 MW → 1000 MW max)
  • 0.5: Can add 50% of existing (500 MW → 750 MW max)
  • 2.0: Can triple existing capacity

Combined with tx_expansion_mw_per_period — larger value governs each line.

docs.title: tx_expansion_mw_per_period
docs.text:
Type: Integer Required: No Example: 500

Absolute expansion limit per line per period (MW).

tx_expansion_mw_per_period: 500  # Can add up to 500 MW

This is an alternative upper bound, not a minimum build size or a discrete construction increment. If the fractional bound is larger, it takes precedence.

Expansion calculation per line:

max_expansion = max(
    existing_capacity * tx_expansion_per_period,
    tx_expansion_mw_per_period
)

docs.title: GenX Output Files
docs.text:
PowerGenome generates these GenX transmission files:

system/Network.csv (default layout):

  • Network_zones: Zone labels
  • Network_Lines: Line ID number
  • Start_Zone, End_Zone: Numeric zone identifiers for each line
  • Line_Max_Flow_MW: Existing capacity
  • transmission_path_name: Human-readable name
  • Line_Loss_Percentage: Loss fraction
  • Line_Reinforcement_Cost_per_MWyr: Annualized expansion cost

GenX uses these files to optimize transmission expansion and inter-regional power flows.

docs.title: Year-Keyed Settings Values
docs.text:
Year-keyed values let you assign different values to different planning years without creating a full multi-scenario matrix.

This pattern is available for any settings parameter value, including nested dictionaries such as resource_modifiers, regional settings, and policy values.

Advanced usage

Year-keyed values are powerful, but they also add validation rules and precedence behavior. Read this page before using them broadly.

docs.title: When To Use This
docs.text:
Use year-keyed values when:

  • You need values that change by planning year.
  • You have a single case (or a few cases) and do not need full settings_management switching.
  • You want changes to be resolved automatically per planning period.

Use settings_management when:

  • You need different values across many scenario dimensions (case_id, policy, fuel cases, etc.).
  • You need explicit scenario matrices in scenario_definitions_fn.

docs.title: Format
docs.text:
A value is treated as year-keyed when all keys are either:

  • Integer years in the range 1900 to 2200, or
  • The special fallback key default

And at least one integer year key is present.

carbon_tax:
  2030: 25
  2040: 50

Nested example:

resource_modifiers:
  utility_pv:
    technology: UtilityPV
    tech_detail: Class1
    capex_mw:
      2030: [mul, 0.90]
      2040: [mul, 0.80]

docs.title: Selection Rules
docs.text:
For each planning year, PowerGenome resolves one value using this priority:

  1. Exact year match (for example, 2030)
  2. default fallback

If no match is found, PowerGenome raises a ValueError.

Example with fallback:

capex_mw:
  2030: [mul, 0.92]
  default: [mul, 1.0]
  • In 2030, value is [mul, 0.92] (exact year wins).
  • In 2040, value is [mul, 1.0] (uses default).

docs.title: Coverage Validation
docs.text:
When PowerGenome builds per-year case settings, year-keyed values are validated against the planning years in your run.

A year-keyed dict must satisfy one of these:

  • Every planning year has an explicit key, or
  • It includes default as a catch-all fallback

If only some planning years are covered and no fallback exists, PowerGenome raises a ValueError.

docs.title: Common Patterns
docs.text:
Exact years only:

carbon_tax:
  2030: 25
  2040: 50
  2050: 75

Constant across all years (prefer scalar):

# Preferred
carbon_tax: 25

# Also valid, but more verbose
# carbon_tax:
#   2030: 25
#   default: 25

docs.title: Interaction With Scenario Management
docs.text:
Year-keyed resolution is applied to normal settings values when per-year scenario settings are built.

The settings_management structure itself is not transformed by year-keyed resolution.

If you need both scenario and year variation:

  1. Use year-keyed values for baseline by-year behavior.
  2. Use settings_management for scenario-specific overrides.

See Scenario Management for multi-case workflows.

docs.title: Tutorials
docs.text: Start with a complete small study, then change one part at a time. These lessons use the published Texas three-zone study from PowerGenome-examples. Inspect actual outputs without assembling a research dataset or cloning PowerGenome's source. PowerGenome prepares inputs; it does not solve the model.

docs.title: 1. Getting Started
docs.text:
Install a published release with uv, download a pinned examples snapshot, validate the Texas study, and generate inputs for 2030 and 2045. Learn where settings, data, logs, and GenX outputs live.

Prerequisites: uv, curl, tar, a terminal, and basic command-line familiarity.

docs.title: 2. Building a Multi-Region Model
docs.text:
Continue with the downloaded Texas study. Inspect its base-to-model-region aggregation, change transmission expansion limits, and verify both periods' network outputs against the first run.

Prerequisites: Getting Started and its unchanged tx_output/ baseline.

docs.title: 3. Working with Renewable Resources
docs.text:
Aggregate the Texas example's wind candidates into cost-and-profile clusters and compare resource counts, capacity limits, and generation profiles while preserving solar. Follow the separate-settings setup to isolate the change.

Prerequisites: The installed environment and downloaded examples from Getting Started. This lesson can be taken independently of the transmission exercise.

docs.title: Move to your own study
docs.text:
The example has short synthetic profiles and can emit warnings; it demonstrates the workflow, not realistic system economics. Browse PowerGenome-examples for other published cases. A real study needs complete compatible sources for existing plants, technology costs, renewable profiles, demand, fuels, transmission, and any configured policies.

Use the System Design tool to create starting settings, then Configure Data Tables and validate the study. Changing region names or planning years alone does not supply the corresponding data.

docs.text:

  • Reference: exact parameters and schemas.

docs.title: Getting Started with PowerGenome
docs.text:
Install a published PowerGenome release, run the Texas three-zone example from PowerGenome-examples, and inspect the generated GenX inputs. PowerGenome prepares inputs; it does not solve the capacity expansion model.

Prerequisites: Basic command-line knowledge, uv, curl, and tar. The commands below use a macOS/Linux shell and Python 3.12. Git and a PowerGenome source checkout are not required.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
From a directory where you keep projects, create a new tutorial folder and install the published release used by this exercise:

mkdir powergenome-tutorial
cd powergenome-tutorial
uv venv --python 3.12
source .venv/bin/activate
uv pip install powergenome==0.8.0

On Windows PowerShell, activate with .venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1 instead of source .venv/bin/activate. Use curl.exe for the download below, or download and extract the linked archive manually. Keep the environment active when changing directories.

The package version and example snapshot below are pinned together for a repeatable first run. For another release, check example compatibility before upgrading.

Verify installation:

run_powergenome --help

docs.title: Project Structure
docs.text:
PowerGenome projects follow this structure:

my_study/
├── settings/              # Configuration files (YAML)
│   ├── model_definition.yml
│   ├── resources.yml
│   ├── fuels.yml
│   ├── demand.yml
│   ├── transmission.yml
│   └── ...
├── extra_inputs/          # User-provided data files
│   ├── scenario_inputs.csv
│   ├── emission_policies.csv
│   └── ...
├── data/                  # Source data (optional, can be elsewhere)
│   ├── generators.csv
│   ├── demand_profiles.parquet
│   └── ...
└── results/               # Output folder (created by PowerGenome)
    ├── log.txt
    └── Inputs/            # Under a case ID if using a scenario CSV
        └── Inputs_p1/
            ├── resources/ # Thermal.csv, Vre.csv, Storage.csv, ...
            ├── system/    # Demand_data.csv, Fuels_data.csv, Network.csv, ...
            └── policies/

Keep Projects Separate

Create project folders outside the PowerGenome repository to avoid git conflicts and make updates easier.

docs.title: 1. Download the Texas example
docs.text:
From powergenome-tutorial/, download and extract the pinned examples snapshot:

curl --fail --location \
  https://codeload.github.com/PowerGenome/PowerGenome-examples/tar.gz/7e34f714469e68fca173cdb849f74c47be779420 \
  --output powergenome-examples.tar.gz
tar -xzf powergenome-examples.tar.gz --strip-components=1
rm powergenome-examples.tar.gz

This downloads the examples, not PowerGenome's source code. The Texas study is under example_systems/TX-3-zone/, with settings/, data/, extra_inputs/, resource_groups/, and resource_profiles/ already populated. The archive also includes a CA/AZ study; browse the examples repository for its instructions and other available cases.

Stay in powergenome-tutorial/ for all commands below; do not change into example_systems/TX-3-zone/. The published resource-group paths require this working directory.

validate_powergenome --settings_file example_systems/TX-3-zone/settings
run_powergenome \
  --settings_file example_systems/TX-3-zone/settings \
  --results_folder tx_output

This will:

  1. Load the .yml files directly inside example_systems/TX-3-zone/settings/
  2. Read the study's source tables from data/ and policy inputs from extra_inputs/
  3. Aggregate seven base regions into three model zones: TX1, TX2, and TX3
  4. Write the base case's two planning periods (2030 and 2045) to tx_output/base/Inputs/Inputs_p1/ and Inputs_p2/

data_location and input_folder resolve relative to the parent of the settings directory (example_systems/TX-3-zone/). In contrast, relative RESOURCE_GROUPS and RESOURCE_GROUP_PROFILES paths resolve from your current working directory (powergenome-tutorial/).

Demonstration data, not a calibrated study

The Texas example contains 240 synthetic profile time steps, not a complete year. It is intended to demonstrate input generation, not support economic conclusions. Do not change regions, years, or technologies without checking that every source table and profile covers the new configuration.

docs.title: 2. Check completion
docs.text:
Both commands should exit successfully. Confirm that tx_output/base/Inputs/Inputs_p1/system/Demand_data.csv and the corresponding Inputs_p2/ directory exist. If the run fails, read the first error in the terminal and check the log.

The CLI Reference covers optional flags. Do not skip pipeline stages for this first run; the analysis below needs their outputs.

docs.title: 3. Monitor Progress
docs.text: PowerGenome logs progress and warnings to the terminal and writes a more detailed tx_output/log.txt. The example can warn about unassigned resource tags, missing output columns, and missing transmission investment costs for some resources. Review warnings rather than treating a completed run as proof of study quality. Resolve missing costs and prices, unmatched technologies, and incomplete regional data before using your own results.

docs.title: Examining Outputs
docs.text: PowerGenome generates multiple CSV files formatted for GenX:

docs.title: Key Output Files
docs.text:
resources/Thermal.csv, Vre.csv, Storage.csv, Hydro.csv, Must_run.csv : Resource characteristics grouped by resource type; files are written only when that type is present

system/Demand_data.csv : Demand by zone and time step

system/Fuels_data.csv : Fuel prices by region and time step

system/Network.csv : Transmission topology and constraints

system/Generators_variability.csv : Generation profiles for variable resources

These are the default GenX outputs. Set old_genx_format: true only when your GenX workflow requires the legacy flat Generators_data.csv and Load_data.csv layout. See Output Format for both layouts.

docs.title: Exploring Resource Data
docs.text:
from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd

period = Path("tx_output/base/Inputs/Inputs_p1")
resource_files = [
    period / "resources" / f"{name}.csv"
    for name in ["Thermal", "Vre", "Storage", "Hydro", "Must_run", "Flex_demand"]
]
gens = pd.concat(
    [pd.read_csv(path) for path in resource_files if path.exists()],
    ignore_index=True,
)

# View summary
print(f"Total resources: {len(gens)}")
print(f"Regions: {gens['region'].unique()}")
print(f"Technologies: {gens['technology'].nunique()}")

# Check existing vs new capacity
print(f"\nExisting capacity: {gens['Existing_Cap_MW'].sum():.0f} MW")
print(f"New-build available: {gens[gens['New_Build']==1]['technology'].unique()}")

# View by technology
gens.groupby('technology')['Existing_Cap_MW'].sum()

docs.title: Understanding Resource Columns
docs.text:
Common columns in the resource files (some are resource-type specific):

  • Resource: Unique resource name
  • region: Model region
  • technology: Technology type
  • Existing_Cap_MW: Existing capacity
  • New_Build: Can new capacity be built? (0/1)
  • Inv_Cost_per_MWyr: Investment cost ($/MW-yr)
  • Fixed_OM_Cost_per_MWyr: Fixed O&M ($/MW-yr)
  • Var_OM_Cost_per_MWh: Variable O&M ($/MWh)
  • Heat_Rate_MMBTU_per_MWh: Heat rate
  • Fuel: Fuel type

Resource tags (GenX behavior):

  • THERM: Thermal generator (has heat rate, startup costs)
  • VRE: Variable renewable energy (wind/solar)
  • STOR: Storage resource
  • HYDRO: Hydroelectric resource

See Output Format for complete documentation.
